meetings.basis: list 25.11 (revised) · programme 26.11 · DPR 25.11 · HM signals to the evening sheet of 25 Nov (amended 20:28)
meetings.note: None of the three. (1) CD GLORY at CJ-4: the board had given her Parvraj's vacant Govt place under circular 5237 (i). The port gave that place to HAI NAM 81 — HP 1 on the list — as "GOV(30K)", at CJ-15A, a berth CD Glory could have used: the 30K-quote line stands before SAAGAR. And CJ-4 did not come free — Safi Alfa's list ETC moved to 30 Nov with more cargo declared. (2) FORTUNELIT at CJ-15A: the berth went to Hai Nam 81. (3) STAR NEW LONDON at CJ-15: Xin Hai Tong 71 is still there — 910 MT a day, about 1 Dec — and Star New London herself is back on the expected sheet. What the port did instead: the Coastal place the tug Varahi leaves (out 17:30) → JUMBO KINETIC, "CSTL", at CJ-7 — the board had held her to CJ-13–16 — and to seat her it shifts Asian Summit CJ-7 → CJ-5 and Blue Shark CJ-5 → CJ-14, both on Gautam Freight's account, and warps Safi Alfa. Also, outside any programme: CJ-6 went to KATERINA K (GEN 3) at 04:12 on 26 Nov, past GEN 1 and GEN 2 whom the berth does not suit. Same priority first held where it was tested: Coastal → Coastal. Changes made: the quote line before SAAGAR for a vacant Govt / Coastal place; General to the senior vessel the berth suits.

meetings.basis: list 23.11 (revised) · programme 25.11 · DPR 24.11 · HM signals to the evening sheet of 24 Nov (amended to 19:20)
meetings.note: Neither. CJ-14 — the Coastal place behind Lila Tokyo — went to a COASTAL vessel, the tug Varahi with barge AKG 11 (CSTL 1): she declared ready at 11:00 on the day of the meeting, after the call was frozen; the board had filled the place with Hai Nam 81 on a 30K quote. The HP berth went to MSC MAGALI (HP 1) on a 50,000 bid, at CJ-16 — the board had named Meghna Prestige (HP 4) at CJ-15A, by a rank that does not decide HP. To give MSC Magali her 253 m the port shifts African Hornbill from CJ-16 to CJ-15A behind Ocean Kudos, on port convenience; so CJ-15A takes no new vessel and the 24-hrs place Ocean Kudos leaves is given to nobody. CJ-6 (Parvraj out 23:45, a Govt place) and CJ-3: nobody. Xin Hai Tong 71 is moved 2¾ panels south. Same priority first held where there was a vessel: Coastal → Coastal. The meeting section of v270 had no Coastal name for CJ-14 (none was ready) and put the HP names under it — Hai Nam 81, Meghna Prestige; MSC Magali was left out of its HP names because the board held her to CJ-7 / 8. Lesson: coal can lie at CJ-16, and the port will shift a vessel to fit an HP bid in. Circular 5237 (i) was not put to the test: no clean berth was left over for a SAAGAR or a quote vessel.

meetings.basis: list 23.11 (revised) · programme 24.11 · DPR 24.11 · HM signals to the day sheet of 24 Nov (disp 21:15 / 05:47)
meetings.note: Two of three right, vessel and berth: Asian Summit at CJ-7 behind Gokova-M and AG Varvara at CJ-13 behind Uni Blossom. Wrong: CJ-15 went to XIN HAI TONG 71, printed "PROJ", not to Hai Nam 81 on her HP quote — the port did not let an HP bid into the timber berth; it kept it for the SAAGAR column and took the project vessel there. Missed altogether: MANTA SENA at CJ-1 — the board went by Crystal O's DPR pace (done about 25 Nov 20:20, outside the window), the port by her list ETC (24 Nov 23:43; the signal now says 06:00) — and PIONEER FORTUNE at CJ-9, the Gautam Freight berth, which the board does not call. CJ-3 (Horizon Chaser out 08:00) is given to nobody. The berth-wise meeting section of v269 did better than the call: HP at CJ-7 → Asian Summit named; SAAGAR at CJ-13 and CJ-15 → AG Varvara, Xin Hai Tong 71, CD Glory — the two that came were its first two names; it had CJ-1 as continuing, the same miss. Asian Summit is printed "SGR" although she is SGR 7 and came by her HP rank — see the checks.

meetings.basis: list 21.11 (revised) · programme 23.11 · DPR 22.11 · HM signals to the night sheet of 22 Nov (disp 21:30 / 21:55)
meetings.note: Three of the four vessels named, none on the berth the board gave her. Zheng Hui (GOVT) and Gokova-M (HP on a 50K bid) do take Flag Marina's length — the port prints both at "CJ-07": Gokova-M at 50½–57, Zheng Hui at 58–67¾ — so the two vessels and the two berths were right, each on the other's side. Blue Shark (GEN 1) came in, but at CJ-5 behind Vishva Bandhan, not at the clean berth. CJ-15A went to OCEAN KUDOS on a 30K quote under 24 hrs — salt for salt behind Belmoira; the board had held her as not ready on the team's word of 21 Nov. Nothing at CJ-1: Crystal O's ETC is now 24 Nov 23:43, so Manta Sena waits. CJ-3 went to the bitumen tanker Horizon Chaser on space account. What it shows: the port first counts which priority has a place vacant (Govt, HP, 24 hrs — one each — and one berth to spare for General rank 1), then puts each vessel on the berth that suits her; the vessel does not follow the berth her place-holder is leaving. The berth-wise meeting section of v262 had the right group for two of these four (Zheng Hui and Gokova-M at CJ-7 / 8) and missed Blue Shark at CJ-5 and Ocean Kudos at CJ-15A.

meetings.basis: list 21.11 (revised) · HM signal 21 Nov night sheet as amended (disp 22:30) · DPR 21.11 · programme 22.11
meetings.note: 23 NOV: the programme's Hai Nam 81 did not berth — list 23.11 and the day signal of 23 Nov put LILA TOKYO (CSTL(30K), in 10:45) into CJ-14 and Hai Nam 81 back on the waiting sheet; the board's call was wrong either way. AS WRITTEN ON 22 NOV: Right berth, wrong vessel. CJ-14 comes free behind the tug-and-barge (out readiness 23 Nov 17:30) and the port gave it to HAI NAM 81 — salt, coastal, a 30,000 quote ("CSTL(30K)", provisional berthing) — not to Xin Hai Tong 71 on the SAAGAR line through the vacant Govt place. The board had Hai Nam 81 at CJ-15A behind Belmoira two hours later: a coastal vessel with a 30K quote took the first clean berth of the window ahead of the SAAGAR vessel. Nothing else was programmed at the cargo jetties — no move at CJ-7 / 8 (Flag Marina stays, so no HP bid at this meeting, as the HP table said), at CJ-15A (Belmoira stays) or at CJ-5 (Vishva Bandhan is not on the sheet).

None of the three. CJ-1 went to Crystal O under 6.5K — the revised list prints her 8K 1, a rank the morning list did not carry; Manta Sena is now 8K 2. CJ-15A went to Belmoira under 24 hrs as a 30K quote (amended signal, in tonight) — she had been starred "B'TODAY" for three days and the board's v197 had her there; v198 moved her and gave the berth to Blue Shark by General. CJ-14 went to the tug-and-barge (CSTL) and Sanghi Sundarshan (space a/c) side by side — not to Xin Hai Tong 71. Sand Topic is the GFPL berth's own vessel.

Uni Blossom was right, berth too. Parvraj — reported that same morning, GP 1 — took the Govt place the board had given to Sea Postman's rock phosphate. Flag Marina took CJ-7 on a 42.5K quote; she lies across CJ-8 as well, so Vishva Bandhan is shifted to CJ-5. Tai Keystone had not arrived (readiness moved to 21 Nov). Nobody was sent to CJ-3. Safi Alfa (GEN 1) goes into CJ-4 under General — by signal (IN "o/c", Capt G. Raj), confirmed by Mihir at 20:22.

Programmed but NOT berthed, so out of the count: Belmoira (a Govt place on her 30K quote, CJ-15) — Truong Minh Dream's sailing was delayed and the place did not open (Mihir, 20 Nov) — and Katerina K (provisional berthing, CJ-6), cancelled by Traffic. African Hornbill came in by the evening signal after Ocean Kudos' holds were rejected. The two General vessels the board named were passed over.
No call — no sheets reached the board on 17 or 18 Nov, so this day is not scored. Ocean Kudos was programmed for CJ-16 and did not berth (holds rejected).

Risk: Andreas Petrakis (coal) is declared SGR 4 and ready — a SAAGAR bulk vessel takes the bulk slot before a cross-fill, but at 14.15 m draught she has no CJ berth under the chart limits, so the board leaves the slot to Quail.

The programme for 3 Nov filled every clean berth Quail could have had: CJ-13 → Lakmos (steel, till ~7 Nov), CJ-15 → Outrivaling 3 (General, back from OTB), CJ-15A → Nord Newport beside a warped Centurion Buyo, CJ-16 → Emmanouil shifted from CJ-1. If the port shifts Outrivaling 3 again to make a clean berth for an HP vessel, CJ-15 could open earlier; nobody quoted HP today, so the board does not count on it.

Orion and Mettle Star withdrew HP priority at the 2 Nov meeting, so the board no longer plans a port-convenience shift of Outrivaling 3 to make them a clean berth. With CJ-15 staying General, the first berth where logs can work after the SAAGAR bulk slot frees (Rome Trader, 4 Nov 22:02) is now CJ-7 once Yasa Eagle (HP, after Yuan Hang Wei Ye) finishes ~5 Nov 10:30 — about 3 h earlier than the CJ-4 reading. Aya's CJ-4 (ETC 5 Nov 13:06, typo-read) remains the fallback.

The port's DPR shows Centurion Buyo working at 7,749 CBM/day — her balance of 8,939 CBM finishes around 3 Nov midday, not 5 Nov as the list ETC says. The SAAGAR break-bulk slot therefore frees on 3 Nov. The first clean berth after that is CJ-16, where Emmanouil (shifted there from CJ-1 by the programme) has 7,940 MT left at 4,163 MT/day → ~4 Nov 05:00. So Quail ~4 Nov 06:46 at CJ-16 — about a day earlier than the list-ETC reading. Hinges on Centurion keeping yesterday's rate and on the port actually shifting Emmanouil; the 3 Nov meeting will show.

Same time, different berth. Today's list does not carry the programme's shift chain: Emmanouil stays at CJ-1 (ETC 5 Nov 22:30; by the DPR rate ~4 Nov 05:00) and CJ-16 goes to Nord Newport (General, B'TODAY after Alasia). The SAAGAR break-bulk slot still frees when Centurion Buyo finishes (DPR-based ~3 Nov midday; list says 5 Nov) — but that berth (CJ-15A) would go to Unity Melody if she declares HP at the meeting (ETA 13:00, HP Y), because the two HP slots are empty since Orion / Mettle Star withdrew. Quail then takes the first clean berth after that: CJ-1 when Emmanouil finishes, ~4 Nov 06:46. If Unity Melody does not declare, Quail could have CJ-15A this evening instead — ask at the meeting.

A day later. The programme for 04.11 uses both berths the board had for Quail: Centurion Buyo sails tonight 23:00 (the DPR reading was right) but CJ-15A goes to Emmanouil (night shift from CJ-1, a/c Genesis) so that Levante Spirit can move to CJ-1 and Yuan Hang Wei Ye to CJ-7 — the Govt / 24-hr / Coastal chain. So the SAAGAR break-bulk slot is free from tonight, but there is no berth for it until the 4 Nov meeting. Board's reading for that meeting: CJ-15A frees again when Emmanouil finishes (DPR ~4 Nov 05:00) and a HP vessel (Unity Melody, if she declares) has first call on it; Quail then needs the port to shift Outrivaling 3 (bags, 118 m, 1 day left) to vacant CJ-3 to open CJ-15 — ~4 Nov 20:30. If Unity Melody does not take HP, Quail gets 15A directly ~18:00. Zheng Rong / Leya (HP, declared today) are too long for 15A. Ask at tomorrow's meeting for 15A — Quail is SGR 1, ready since 27 Oct.

Later again, for two reasons. (1) The DPR the board used for Emmanouil's early finish is from 2 Nov 0700 and is now more than 36 h old, so the board drops it (its own staleness rule) and falls back to the list ETC: Emmanouil at CJ-15A till ~6 Nov 01:30, not 4 Nov 05:00 — CJ-15A does not free tomorrow. (2) CJ-15 (opened by a port-convenience shift of Outrivaling 3 to CJ-3) goes to Unity Melody under HP first, if she declares. Two things bring it back to 4 Nov: today's DPR (03.11) with Emmanouil's balance — the board would re-read 15A — or Unity Melody not quoting HP, in which case CJ-15 opens for Quail ~4 Nov 20:30 as before. Team ETB stays 4 Nov. Tonight's signal itself changed nothing for Quail: Centurion Buyo sails 23:15 and Emmanouil moves to 15A at 05:15 as programmed.

Berthing TODAY. (b) Programme 21.11 now puts VISHVA BANDHAN into CJ-5 behind Ken Ann (out 16:00) — shifted from CJ-8 on the port's account, because Flag Marina (254 m) needs CJ-7 and CJ-8 together — and she finishes there: about 20:00 on the 21st at the DPR pace (15,488 MT left at 0700 on the 20th, at 10,860 a day), 22 Nov 14:33 by her list ETC. So CJ-5 comes free in the NEXT window, in which the 6.5K place is open (New Bliss leaves CJ-1 about 21 Nov 22:20 at her pace; list ETC 22 Nov 10:05). (c) The rule (Mihir, 11 Nov): each berth, as it frees, goes to the senior vessel of the line that the berth suits; the place is not held for a berth that frees later. None of the eight vessels ahead of her in 6.5K / 8K can lie at CJ-5 — the bag vessels load at CJ-1 to 4 or the clean berths, Gokova-M loads too deep, Uni Blossom berths tonight by SAAGAR. If CJ-5 clears first it is hers: about 21 Nov 22:00, done about 26 Nov 14:40. (d) It is a close call — the two berths are some two hours apart on yesterday's rates. If New Bliss is out first, or the meeting of 21 Nov keeps the place for Manta Sena at CJ-1, CD Glory is back to General (CJ-15A, about 25 Nov) or the SAAGAR line (about 27–28 Nov; SGR 4 now, behind AG Varvara and Xin Hai Tong 71). The desk says 26 Nov. The meeting of 21 Nov (11:00) decides it — the berth to ask for is CJ-5 under 6.5K / 8K. Laytime runs out 23 Nov 01:38.

CD Glory.d: 20 Nov 16:50 · Mihir — she cannot take the 6.5K place ahead of her seniors
CD Glory.slot: SAAGAR — CJ-16 about 24 Nov 06:00, when ML Egret's place opens · General — CJ-15A about 25 Nov · 6.5K / 8K CLOSED (eight vessels senior to her) · timber desk 26 Nov
CD Glory.why: Mihir (20 Nov 16:50): CD Glory cannot berth at CJ-5 under the 6.5K priority, because other vessels are senior to her in that line. The board had given her CJ-5 on the night of the 21st on its 11 Nov reading — that the place passes down the line when the berth does not suit the seniors. For 6.5K / 8K that reading is withdrawn: the place goes by seniority, and she is 8K 9. So Manta Sena (8K 1) takes the place at CJ-1 behind New Bliss, about 22 Nov 00:20, and CJ-5, when Vishva Bandhan has finished there, goes to General — AG Varvara (GEN 16), the senior vessel that does not load bags. That last point helps CD Glory: with AG Varvara (SGR 2) berthed by General and Xin Hai Tong 71 (SGR 3) taken by the project route, she is next in the SAAGAR line for ML Egret's place — about 24 Nov at the DPR pace (list ETC 28 Nov) — and the board seats her at CJ-16 behind African Hornbill: 24 Nov 06:00, done about 2 Dec 21:50. Weak points: AG Varvara must indeed get CJ-5 by General (if she does not, the SAAGAR place is hers first and CD Glory waits for Uni Blossom's, about 28 Nov); ML Egret must keep her pace; African Hornbill's sailing (24 Nov 04:00) is the board's own estimate. The timber desk says 26 Nov. Laytime (arrival + 12 hours) runs out 23 Nov 01:38. This is her fourth date today — 21 Nov night, 23 Nov night, 21 Nov night, 24 Nov morning; the last move rests on Mihir's word, not on a document.

CD Glory.d: 20 Nov 17:13 · Mihir — General is by seniority too; his reckoning for her is 26 Nov
CD Glory.slot: SAAGAR — CJ-14 about 26 Nov night, when Uni Blossom's place opens · General and 6.5K / 8K CLOSED (seniors ahead in both) · Mihir and the timber desk: 26 Nov
CD Glory.why: Mihir (20 Nov 17:13): AG Varvara cannot come in by General on the 21st — many vessels are senior to her; the board's calculation was wrong. And by his reckoning CD Glory berths on the 26th. The board had been letting a junior take a General berth whenever the seniors were bag vessels shut out by the three-bag limit or by the berth — that put AG Varvara (GEN 16) into CJ-5 on the 21st, and with her out of the SAAGAR line CD Glory moved up to 24 Nov. Corrected: General goes strictly by seniority, as 6.5K / 8K does. So AG Varvara waits in the SAAGAR line (SGR 2) and takes ML Egret's place — about 23–24 Nov at the DPR pace, 26 Nov by the desk — and CD Glory (SGR 4; Xin Hai Tong 71, SGR 3, goes by the project route) takes the next one, Uni Blossom's. Uni Blossom berths on the night of 20–21 Nov; taken at 5,600 CBM a day (the record average of the completed log vessels — the list has printed no norm for her yet) she is through about 27 Nov 08:00, and the board counts the place from the evening of the 26th: CJ-14, 26 Nov 22:00, done about 5 Dec. That is Mihir's 26th. Only the SAAGAR line counts for her now: General (GEN 20) and 6.5K / 8K (8K 9) are both closed by seniority. What can still move the date: Uni Blossom's real rate (at ML Egret's 8,000 a day she is through on the 25th, at the 4,600 norm on the 28th), and whether Xin Hai Tong 71 really goes by the project route. Laytime runs out 23 Nov 01:38 — nearly four days on demurrage before she berths. This is the fifth reading today; the last two corrections are Mihir's, and they corrected the board's rules, not the facts.

CD Glory.d: 20 Nov 20:11 · HM signal 20 Nov as amended (disp 14:00)
CD Glory.slot: SAAGAR — 26 Nov about 22:00, when Uni Blossom's place opens · berth on this reading CJ-4 · General and 6.5K / 8K closed · Mihir and the timber desk: 26 Nov

The berth is the weak part of the reading, the date is not — it rests on Uni Blossom's rate (5,600 CBM a day assumed).

CD Glory.d: 20 Nov 20:22 · Mihir — Safi Alfa berths at CJ-4 under General
CD Glory.slot: SAAGAR — CJ-14, 26 Nov about 22:00, when Uni Blossom's place opens · General and 6.5K / 8K closed · Mihir and the timber desk: 26 Nov

Dariya Priya (SGR 4, behind her) has started discharging at midstream.

CD Glory.d: 21 Nov 14:46 · programme 22.11 + list 21.11 revised
CD Glory.slot: SAAGAR (SGR 3) — CJ-15, 26 Nov about 21:00, on ML Egret's place · 6.5K / 8K closed (8K 9 now) · General closed · Mihir and the timber desk: 26 Nov

CD Glory.d: 22 Nov 12:18 · DPR 22.11 + day signal of 22 Nov

CD Glory.d: 22 Nov 15:39 · programme 23.11
CD Glory.slot: SAAGAR (SGR 3) — CJ-14, 25 Nov about 21:00, behind Hai Nam 81

CD Glory.d: 23 Nov 14:10 · programme 24.11 + revised list 23.11
CD Glory.slot: SAAGAR (SGR 3) — the night of 25 / 26 Nov; the board now shows CJ-4 about 00:15 behind Safi Alfa (CJ-13 about 19:30 before) · the night is firmer than the berth

The revised list gives numbers to Asian Summit (HP 4) and Hai Nam 81 (HP 5), so the board now fills the two Higher-productivity places that open on the 24th–25th (African Hornbill's and Gokova-M's) with them — Hai Nam 81 on ML Egret's berth, CJ-15 — and Xin Hai Tong 71 (SGR 2, project cargo), who had been going to CJ-16 by that route, now comes to Uni Blossom's berth, CJ-13. CD Glory keeps her SAAGAR place of the 25th and takes the next berth that suits her — CJ-4, behind Safi Alfa (about 25 Nov 22:15 at the DPR rate). TWO THINGS TO WATCH. (1) The berth is the weak part: programme 24.11 showed that the port counts the vacant places by priority and then chooses the berth — the board named three of four vessels right today and none of their berths. (2) Xin Hai Tong 71: if the port counts her inside the SAAGAR line (she is SGR 2), the two places of 25 Nov go to AG Varvara and to her, and CD Glory waits for the next SAAGAR sailing — Xin Hai Tong 71 has only 5,706 MT, so about 27 Nov. CD Glory.d: 24 Nov 10:40 · DPR 24.11 + night and day signals
CD Glory.slot: SAAGAR (SGR 3) · CJ-1 behind Crystal O is the board's reading · two SAAGAR berths come up at today's meeting — CJ-15 tonight, CJ-13 tomorrow midday

(2) CRYSTAL O at CJ-1 clears about 25 Nov 20:20 at 5,347 MT a day — the board now puts CD Glory there about 22:20 on 25 Nov. (3) The two timber berths clear sooner: ML EGRET about 22:00 tonight (4,879 CBM left), UNI BLOSSOM about 10:30 on 25 Nov (10,414 left). Both are SAAGAR places and the SAAGAR line is AG Varvara (SGR 1), Xin Hai Tong 71 (SGR 2), CD Glory (SGR 3). The board gives CJ-15 to Hai Nam 81 on her HP quote and CJ-13 to AG Varvara. BEST CASE: the port keeps both places for the SAAGAR line and counts Xin Hai Tong 71 by the project route — then CD Glory is on today's programme for CJ-13, about midday 25 Nov. MIDDLE: CJ-1, 25 Nov about 22:20. LATE: Crystal O slips or the 8K line (Manta Sena) takes CJ-1 — then CJ-4 behind Safi Alfa, about 26 Nov 20:45.

CD Glory.why: The meeting of 24 Nov gave CJ-13 to AG Varvara (SGR 1) and CJ-15 to Xin Hai Tong 71 (SGR 2, printed PROJ); CJ-1, where the board had CD Glory for 25 Nov 22:20, went to Manta Sena, the senior 6.5K vessel — Crystal O sails on her list ETC, not on the DPR pace. The timber desk's sheet of 24 Nov, written after the meeting, gives the same day: ETB 27 Nov. EARLIER IF Asian Summit counts under HP (she took the HP berth by her HP rank): then CD Glory is the next SAAGAR vessel for CJ-15A / CJ-15, about 26 Nov 13:35. Berths falling vacant inside tomorrow's window (to 26 Nov 18:00): CJ-14 Lila Tokyo about 25 Nov 23:00 · CJ-16 African Hornbill about 26 Nov 11:10 · CJ-15A Ocean Kudos about 11:35 · CJ-15 Xin Hai Tong 71 about 11:55.

CD Glory.slot: SAAGAR — SGR 1 on list 25.11, first of her line · both SAAGAR places are taken: AG Varvara (CJ-13) and Asian Summit (CJ-7) · her turn hangs on Asian Summit
CD Glory.why: List 25.11 settles yesterday's doubt: it prints ASIAN SUMMIT under SAAGAR at CJ-7 — the port counts her in the SAAGAR places — and CD GLORY as SGR 1. The SAAGAR line has two places; AG Varvara takes CJ-13 tonight for nine days, so the place that opens for CD Glory is Asian Summit's. The list gives Asian Summit an ETC of 28 Nov 22:59, worked at the petcoke NORM of 16,100 MT a day (yesterday the board had reckoned her at a 30K quote, 27 Nov 04:25 — that is where the 27 Nov 08:00 came from). On that ETC CD Glory comes in about 29 Nov 02:20, at CJ-16 — CJ-7 itself goes to Tai Keystone (Govt, can lie only at CJ-7 / 8). BUT the norm is a floor: Asian Summit landed 3,800 MT in her first two hours on 5 hooks, and Sand Topic finished 51,292 MT of the same cargo in 47 hours at the next berth. At that pace Asian Summit is done about midday on 27 Nov and CD Glory follows the same night, about 22:30 — the timber desk's ETB of 27 Nov. The board keeps the list ETC till a full day of her work is on a DPR (tomorrow's). RANGE: night of 27 Nov to early 29 Nov. Also from this list: Star New London (salt, HP 2) and Pacific Apex (HP 6) are new in the HP line; they do not touch the SAAGAR place.

CD Glory.d: 25 Nov 15:00 · Mihir — no HP bid · circular 5237 (i) read against the policy papers
CD Glory.slot: A vacant Coastal place under circular 5237 (i) — she is SGR 1 · CJ-14 behind Jumbo Kinetic, 26 Nov about 19:30 · on the circular as written, not yet seen at a meeting
CD Glory.why: Two days earlier than this morning, and by a different door. Mihir (14:47): no vessel bid for the HP category, and berthing goes by the vacant places, in order of priority. He asked for circular 5237 (i) to be read against the policy of 24.03.2025, the circular of 21.05.2026 and the corrigendum of 09.07.2026. On those papers a vacant Govt or Coastal place, with no vessel of its own, goes down the order: Coastal, then an HP bid, then SAAGAR — 3(B) in the table of 21.05.2026 — and only after that to a 30K / 25K quote. With no HP bid it reaches SAAGAR, and CD Glory is SGR 1. Places in sight: the Govt place Parvraj leaves today, and the Coastal place behind Lila Tokyo (out about 26 Nov 01:36). The coastal vessels come first — the tug Varahi with her barge, and Jumbo Kinetic, a 14-hour call at CJ-14 — and CD Glory follows Jumbo Kinetic into CJ-14 on the evening of 26 Nov; it is for the meeting of 26 Nov to give. WHAT IT RESTS ON: the wording of the circular. The port has not yet filled a Govt or Coastal place under it, and the timber desk's ETB (27 Nov) does not count on it. Weak points: the corrigendum of 09.07.2026 calls the 24-hour category "3(B)" in one heading, and 5237 does not strike out the 30K quote in words. If the port gives these places to 30K quotes as before, her date is this morning's: Asian Summit's SAAGAR place, the night of 27 Nov to early 29 Nov. RANGE: evening of 26 Nov to early 29 Nov.

CD Glory.d: 25 Nov 16:11 · programme 26.11 + list 25.11 revised after the meeting
CD Glory.slot: A vacant Govt place under circular 5237 (i) — she is SGR 1 · CJ-4 behind Safi Alfa, 26 Nov about midnight · for the meeting of 26 Nov · on the circular as written, not yet seen
CD Glory.why: Programme 26.11 does not name her — and could not have: no timber berth came free in its window. The head of CJ-14 goes to the tug Varahi and her barge (the Coastal place, to a coastal vessel), CJ-15A to the shift of African Hornbill, CJ-16 to MSC Magali on an HP bid of 50K. What the programme does show: Parvraj sails at 23:45 tonight and her GOVT PLACE is given to nobody. On circular 5237 (i) that place, with no Govt or Coastal vessel for it and no HP bid, comes to the SAAGAR line, and CD Glory is SGR 1. The 3 pm reading had her in the Coastal place at CJ-14 behind Jumbo Kinetic; the Coastal place has now gone to the tug till about 27 Nov 18:00, so it is the Govt place and CJ-4, where Safi Alfa finishes about 26 Nov 21:55 at her DPR pace. THE WEAK LINKS: (1) the port has still not given a Govt or Coastal place under the circular — the 26 Nov meeting is the first real test; (2) MSC Magali's bid shows vessels DO bid for HP, and an HP bid stands before SAAGAR for this place; (3) Safi Alfa's list ETC is 28 Nov 00:00 — if the port goes by it, CJ-4 is not in the 26 Nov window, and the next timber berths are CJ-15 (Xin Hai Tong 71, no ETC) and CJ-14 behind the tug, 27 Nov evening; (4) Jumbo Kinetic, a coastal vessel with the Coastal place taken, stands before SAAGAR for this same Govt place — she can lie only at CJ-13 to 16, so the board lets CJ-4 pass her by; if the port holds the place for her, CD Glory waits for the next one (the Coastal place behind the tug, or Zheng Hui's Govt place, both 27 Nov evening). If the circular is not applied at all: Asian Summit's SAAGAR place, about the evening of 29 Nov on her list ETC. RANGE: midnight of 26 Nov to the evening of 29 Nov.

CD Glory.d: 25 Nov 17:02 · Mihir — strictly by the order of priority, then a suitable berth
CD Glory.slot: Unchanged — a vacant Govt place under circular 5237 (i), CJ-4 behind Safi Alfa, 26 Nov about midnight · for the meeting of 26 Nov
CD Glory.why: The rule Mihir gave is now in the calculation: the place goes strictly by the order of priority and the berth is found for the vessel afterwards. For Parvraj's Govt place the order under the circular is: a coastal vessel first (Jumbo Kinetic — the Coastal place itself is taken by the tug), then an HP bid, then SAAGAR (CD Glory). Jumbo Kinetic can lie only at CJ-13 to 16, and none of those has a DECLARED sailing inside the 26 Nov window — CJ-15 (Xin Hai Tong 71, project cargo, no ETC), CJ-15A (African Hornbill, the same) and CJ-14 (the tug, no norm) are all the board's estimates — so the board does not hold the place for her and it comes to CD Glory at CJ-4. IF THE AGENTS DECLARE THOSE SAILINGS AT THE MEETING, Jumbo Kinetic takes the Govt place at one of them and CD Glory waits for the next place: the Coastal place behind the tug or Zheng Hui's Govt place, both about the evening of 27 Nov — the timber desk's date. The other weak links stand as written at 16:11: the circular not yet applied by any meeting; a possible HP bid; Safi Alfa's list ETC of 28 Nov. RANGE: midnight of 26 Nov to the evening of 29 Nov; 27 Nov evening is the likeliest if the circular is applied.

CD Glory.d: 26 Nov 15:14 · programme 27.11 + list 26.11 revised + DPR 26.11
CD Glory.slot: SAAGAR (SGR 1) — her line's own place when Asian Summit finishes; CJ-5, 27 Nov evening · for the meeting of 27 Nov
CD Glory.why: NOT ON PROGRAMME 27.11. The reading of the last two days — a vacant Govt place under circular 5237 (i), CJ-4 on 26 Nov night — did not hold: the port gave Parvraj's Govt place to Hai Nam 81 (salt, HP 1) as "GOV(30K)" at CJ-15A, a berth she could have used; and CJ-4 is not free, Safi Alfa's ETC is now 30 Nov. So the 30K-quote line stands before SAAGAR for a vacant Govt place, and she is back to her own line. THAT LINE IS NOW CLOSE: Asian Summit — the SAAGAR bulk place — discharged 26,200 MT in her first full day and had 30,499 left at 07:00 on 26 Nov. She is shifted CJ-7 → CJ-5 tonight (Gautam Freight's account); at that pace she finishes about 27 Nov 16:00, shift included. CD Glory is SGR 1 and CJ-5 takes hardwood logs (Lanna Naree, 5–9 Nov), so the board gives her CJ-5 about 27 Nov 18:00 — to be given at the meeting of 27 Nov, which programmes from 18:00. WHAT CAN MOVE IT: the port programmes on its own ETC — Asian Summit's is 28 Nov 22:59; unless her agent declares the earlier completion at the meeting, the place comes a day later, 29 Nov. And petcoke at CJ-5 may not keep the rate it had at CJ-7. ONE MORE: Asian Summit holds the SAAGAR BULK place, and a SAAGAR bulk vessel that is ready takes that place before the logs — New Joyful (petcoke, SGR Y, ETA 28 Nov 05:00, printed "RDY") is the one to watch; if the place frees only on 28 / 29 Nov, she can be ahead of CD Glory for it. Timber desk (24 Nov): ETB 27 Nov.

CD Glory.d: 26 Nov 23:10 · HM evening signal (disp 18:10, to 21:00) + corrigendum 26.11.2026
CD Glory.slot: SAAGAR (SGR 1) — Asian Summit's place; CJ-5, 27 Nov about 20:00 · for the meeting of 27 Nov
CD Glory.why: Same reading as the afternoon, two hours later on the clock: Asian Summit has no outward row on programme 27.11, so the board lets her go at the end of that window, 18:00 on 27 Nov, and CD Glory is alongside about two hours after. NOT KNOWN TONIGHT: whether Asian Summit was shifted CJ-7 → CJ-5 this evening. The night signal sheet starts at 23:00 and has none of the four moves programme 27.11 set for the evening (tug Varahi out, Blue Shark to CJ-14, Asian Summit to CJ-5, Jumbo Kinetic in); they would be on the day sheet's afternoon rows, which have not come. If the shift did not happen, she is still at CJ-7 — CD Glory then follows her there or wherever the meeting seats the SAAGAR place. THE CORRIGENDUM OF 26 NOV (Bitumen berth → 6.5K line, break bulk only) does not move her: she is 8K 5, with four bag vessels ahead for that one berth.

CD Glory.d: 27 Nov 10:19 · list 27.11 + DPR 27.11 + Mihir on HP bids and Steel
CD Glory.slot: SAAGAR (SGR 1) — Asian Summit's place; berth CJ-15 behind Xin Hai Tong 71, 29 Nov about 02:00 — or CJ-5 on 28 Nov afternoon if no HP bidder takes that berth
CD Glory.why: A day later than last night, for two reasons. (1) ASIAN SUMMIT LOST HALF A DAY TO HER SHIFT: 13,600 MT in the day against 26,200 the day before; 16,899 left at 07:00 on 27 Nov → about 28 Nov 12:50 at that rate. The list has her at CJ-5 with ETC 28 Nov 22:59 — so her place is outside what today's meeting can see on the port's own ETC, unless her agent declares the earlier finish. (2) MIHIR, 27 Nov: the HP column vessels are bidders. The second HP place is vacant, and HP stands above SAAGAR — when CJ-5 frees, the board gives the BERTH to Rex (HP 5, ball clay; the HP vessels senior to her cannot use CJ-5) and CD Glory, who has the SAAGAR place, takes the next berth that suits her: CJ-15, when Xin Hai Tong 71 is done — 1,767 MT a day now, 3,006 left → about 28 Nov 23:50. So: 28 Nov afternoon at CJ-5 if Rex is not seated there; otherwise CJ-15 about 29 Nov 02:00. Either way it is for the meeting of 28 Nov, not today's, unless Asian Summit's early completion is declared today. New Joyful (petcoke, SGR Y, ETA 28 Nov 05:00) is still the SAAGAR bulk vessel to watch.

Paiwan Ace.slot: SAAGAR (SGR 6) — a long-range reading, not a date: between about 4 Dec and 11 Dec · timber desk: 8 Dec
Paiwan Ace.why: List 23.11 puts her on the waiting sheet (still printed "PAIWAN ICE"): reported 22 Nov 00:06, readiness 22 Nov 11:00, SGR 6 · 8K 12 · Sr No 7 — she is in the SAAGAR line from today. A SAAGAR place opens only when a SAAGAR vessel has sailed. The two places that ML Egret and Uni Blossom leave on 25 Nov go to AG Varvara (SGR 1) and CD Glory (SGR 3); Xin Hai Tong 71 (2) goes by the project route. After that the board's long run opens a place on about 1 Dec (CD Glory out) for Dariya Priya (SGR 4), on about 4 Dec (AG Varvara out) for African Tiger (SGR 5), and on about 11 Dec (Dariya Priya out of CJ-13) for Paiwan Ace. Two things move it: vessels not yet alongside are reckoned at the 4,600 CBM norm, while the log vessels now at berth are doing 6,800–8,000 a day — every such day brings her forward; and Dariya Priya is discharging at midstream (41,306 CBM left) — if she does not take a berth, Paiwan Ace moves up to the place of about 4 Dec. The timber desk sheet of 21 Nov has her ETB as 8 Dec. By 6.5K / 8K she is last of the line (8K 12) — closed. Shown as beyond the projection on the board until the SAAGAR line ahead of her shortens.

Paiwan Ace.d: 25 Nov 15:00 · Mihir — no HP bid · circular 5237 (i) read against the policy papers
Paiwan Ace.slot: SAAGAR (SGR 4) — her line's own place when Asian Summit sails, about 29 Nov · ONLY IF the three log vessels ahead of her go in on vacant Govt / Coastal places under circular 5237 (i) · the earliest, not the date
Paiwan Ace.why: The same reading that brings CD Glory forward. On the circular as written the vacant Coastal and Govt places go to the SAAGAR line while nobody bids for HP: CD Glory (SGR 1) on 26 Nov, Dariya Priya (2) on 27 Nov, African Tiger (3) on 28 Nov. That leaves the SAAGAR place Asian Summit vacates — list ETC 28 Nov 22:59 — to Paiwan Ace: a free bulk place may be given to a log vessel when no SAAGAR bulk vessel is waiting. Four berthings must fall this way before hers, and the port has not yet given one Govt or Coastal place under the circular. If it keeps to the 30K quote, she is back on the desk's dates: 7 Dec under SAAGAR, 2 Dec under 6.5K. Treat 29 Nov as the EARLIEST.

Paiwan Ace.d: 25 Nov 16:11 · programme 26.11 + list 25.11 revised after the meeting
Paiwan Ace.slot: SAAGAR (SGR 4) — her line's own place when Asian Summit sails; CJ-15A behind Star New London, 30 Nov early · ONLY IF the three log vessels ahead of her go in on vacant Govt / Coastal places under circular 5237 (i) · the earliest, not the date
Paiwan Ace.why: A day later than the 3 pm reading. Programme 26.11 gives the Coastal place to the tug Varahi till about 27 Nov 18:00 and CJ-16 to MSC Magali till about 28 Nov 15:20, so the timber vessels ahead of her go in later: CD Glory 26 Nov night (Govt place), Dariya Priya 27 Nov night (Govt place), African Tiger 28 Nov midday (Coastal place). Asian Summit's SAAGAR place (list ETC 28 Nov 22:59) is then hers, at the first berth she can use — CJ-15A on 30 Nov. Every step before hers rests on the circular being applied as written, which no meeting has yet done. If it is not: the desk's dates — 7 Dec under SAAGAR, 2 Dec under 6.5K. Revised list: SGR 4 · 8K 10 · GEN 20.

Paiwan Ace.slot: SAAGAR (SGR 4) — the place CD Glory leaves; CJ-16, about 3 Dec evening · the earliest, not the date
Paiwan Ace.why: Three and a half days later than yesterday's reading, because the short cut is gone: the port gives a vacant Govt / Coastal place to the 30K-quote line before SAAGAR (Hai Nam 81, programme 27.11), so the log vessels ahead of her no longer clear through those places as fast. Revised list: SGR 4 · 8K 8 · GEN 17. How the board gets there: CD Glory takes Asian Summit's SAAGAR place about 27 Nov; Dariya Priya (SGR 2) a Govt place at CJ-15A about 29 Nov once the quote line has nobody for that berth; African Tiger (SGR 3) CJ-15 about 1 Dec when Xin Hai Tong 71 is done; then she is first of the line, and the next SAAGAR place is CD Glory's, about 3 Dec. Each of those steps is an estimate on an estimate. If Xin Bo is declared ready on 27 Nov she takes the 29 Nov Govt place at CJ-15A instead of Dariya Priya, and everything behind moves about two days.

Paiwan Ace.d: 27 Nov 10:19 · list 27.11 + DPR 27.11 + Mihir on HP bids and Steel
Paiwan Ace.slot: a General place (GEN 18) at CJ-16, about 2 Dec night — the earliest, not the date
Paiwan Ace.why: About a day earlier than yesterday's reading and by a different door: with the HP column counted as bidders (Mihir, 27 Nov) the salt and clay vessels clear through the HP places, and the log vessels ahead of her go faster — CD Glory about 29 Nov, Dariya Priya a vacant Coastal place at CJ-14 about 1 Dec, African Tiger CJ-15A about 2 Dec. Xin Bo.d: 26 Nov 15:14 · list 26.11 revised (ETA sheet) — first reading
Xin Bo.slot: a vacant Govt place on the 30K quote, behind Hai Nam 81 — CJ-15A, about 29 Nov 01:00 · ONLY IF she is declared ready on 27 Nov and the port ranks her in the HP column

Rome Trader (salt, next call).slot: SAAGAR — bulk place · if the port ranks her behind the log vessels ~18 Nov at CJ-13 · HP if declared ~19 Nov 21:30 at CJ-15 · 6.5K / 8K or General ~20 Nov 20:00 at CJ-15A
Rome Trader (salt, next call).why: Salt 55,275 MT EXP, 189.9 m, 6.6 m on arrival, ETA / readiness 14 Nov 17:00, agent Mihir, "SGR- NEELKANTH", SGR Y. Salt works only at CJ-13 to CJ-16. Enishi finishes ~16 Nov 17:00 on the DPR pace — inside the window of the 15 Nov meeting (15 Nov 18:00 to 16 Nov 18:00) — so that meeting can programme Rome Trader into CJ-16 as soon as Cape Diversity is out (~15 Nov 19:00 on the DPR pace; she is not on programme 15.11). Rome Trader (salt, next call).d: 14 Nov 18:00 · Mihir confirms the SAAGAR rule · board correction

So the place Enishi vacates is Rome Trader's. Her BERTH changes from the 16:30 reading: the board had still counted Bomustafao O (a General cross-fill of 8 Nov) against the HP slot and so offered CJ-16 to SAAGAR. Theometor is running about 1½ days behind (DPR pace ~17 Nov 19:30) and the port has not pulled Bomustafao O out at hers, so CJ-14 may not be cleared; then it is CJ-15 behind Enishi, ~16 Nov 19:00. The SAAGAR place she waits for is held by a log vessel, and both log vessels slowed down: Enishi did only 2,312 MT in the last 24 h (4,578 the day before) — 8,760 left → ~19 Nov 02:00 at this rate, and she loses more hours in this evening's shift to CJ-15; African Peacock did 3,040 MT — 11,086 left → ~18 Nov 22:30. So the first SAAGAR place now frees with African Peacock on the night of the 18th and Rome Trader follows her into CJ-13 about 19 Nov 00:30. If Enishi works at her two-day average (~3,450 a day) she is through ~17 Nov 20:00 and Rome Trader can follow her into CJ-15 that night. Declaring HP as well would bring ~18 Nov 06:00 at CJ-14 — less than a day earlier, with the HP commitment.

Rome Trader (salt, next call).d: 15 Nov 10:49 · Mihir — declared under SAAGAR, HP, 30K/25K and 8K
Rome Trader (salt, next call).slot: HP or 30K / 25K quote — CJ-14 after Rahma · SAAGAR bulk place ~18 Nov 22:00 at CJ-14
Rome Trader (salt, next call).why: Mihir: Rome Trader is ready under SAAGAR, HP, 30K/25K and 8K — the single "SGR Y" on list 14.11 is the port's mistake. With all four routes her earliest berth is CJ-14 about 18 Nov 06:00, under HP or as a 30K/25K quote — some 16 hours ahead of the SAAGAR place (~18 Nov 22:00). What holds her is a clean berth, not the priority: in the window the 15 Nov meeting programmes, CJ-16 (Cape Diversity out today) goes to the senior HP vessels (Evangelia D, HP 2; HN Doris, HP 3) and CJ-14 (Theometor) to Rahma (STL 1), because both HP places and both SAAGAR places are occupied through that window. CJ-13, CJ-15 and CJ-15A stay taken till the 17th to 19th.

Rome Trader (salt, next call).slot: HP — CJ-14, 17 Nov afternoon if a clean berth is opened for her; else CJ-15A after Rahma ~18 Nov 18:00 (HP or 30K / 25K) · SAAGAR bulk place ~19 Nov 00:30 at CJ-13
Rome Trader (salt, next call).why: Programme 16.11 (window to 16 Nov 18:00) does not berth her: the one clean berth that frees, CJ-16, goes to Evangelia D (HP 2) after Cape Diversity sails at 03:00, and Rahma (STL 1) is seated at CJ-15A by moving North Gate to CJ-3 at her agent's cost. Her date moves EARLIER on the board, from 18 Nov 06:00 to 17 Nov ~13:30, for two reasons: both HP places come free on the 17th (Evangelia D ~11:30, Cape Venture ~12:50 — board estimates until the list prints an ETC), and Rahma no longer needs CJ-14. It is a range, not a date: on the 17th three vessels want a clean berth — Xin Hai Tong 71 (Coastal slot as SAAGAR project), HN Doris (HP 3, senior to her) and Rome Trader (HP 4) — and only two free by themselves (CJ-16 when Evangelia D sails, CJ-14 when Theometor finishes ~14:00 on the DPR pace). The third needs the port to shift a log / bag vessel (African Peacock, CJ-13 → CJ-5). With that shift she berths on the 17th; without it she waits for CJ-15A behind Rahma, ~18 Nov 18:00. Programme 16.11 shows the other way a berth is opened: the shift is made at the cost of the agent who wants the berth (North Gate for Rahma, a/c Parekh Marine; Enishi for African Hornbill on programme 15.11, a/c Delta). MIHIR (15 Nov 17:48): that does not apply to her — she needs a clean berth and her cargo lies on the CJ-13 to 16 side, so the shift is made on PORT account. The 17 Nov berth stands. Theometor is not overstaying either: every bag vessel under General has 2 days' extension (hers runs to 18 Nov 02:06).

Rome Trader (salt, next call).d: 15 Nov 18:40 · night signal — Evangelia D alongside ~06:00
Rome Trader (salt, next call).why: Night signal 15 Nov: Cape Diversity RT OUT 03:00, Evangelia D IN o/c — made fast ~06:00 (the board had 05:00 from the programme). Her ~29 h of loading then end ~12:30 on the 17th, so the HP place, and Rome Trader behind it, moves by one hour to ~14:30. Nothing else changes for her; the date still rests on Evangelia D's loading rate and on the port making the African Peacock shift in the window of the 16 Nov meeting.

Rome Trader (salt, next call).d: 15 Nov 20:54 · amended night sheet — Evangelia D alongside ~08:30
Rome Trader (salt, next call).slot: HP — CJ-14 · the HP place now comes from Cape Venture
Rome Trader (salt, next call).why: Amended night sheet (disp 2048): Evangelia D now comes in o/c with Capt Bali after TCI Anand's 05:25 sailing — alongside ~08:30, sailing ~17 Nov 15:00 est. That would have cost Rome Trader 2½ hours, but the other HP place frees first: Cape Venture (CJ-7 + CJ-8) ~12:50 on the 17th, so her berth is offered ~14:50. Twenty minutes later than the last run — effectively no change. Both sailings are board estimates.

Rome Trader (salt, next call).d: 16 Nov 18:17 · list 16.11 + programme 17.11 — not berthed under HP
Rome Trader (salt, next call).slot: SAAGAR bulk place — CJ-13 when African Peacock is through · HP only at the quote of the day · the desk sheet seats two log vessels on the SAAGAR places
Rome Trader (salt, next call).why: Programme 17.11 does not berth her. Both HP places came free in this window (Cape Venture and Evangelia D out at 17:00 on the 17th) and both went to salt vessels at a 46,000-MTPD quote: HN Doris (HP 2) at CJ-16 and Bristol (HP 7, arrived that morning) at CJ-15A — North Gate is moved to CJ-2 to clear CJ-15A for Bristol. Rome Trader is HP 3 on the revised list and was passed over: the HP place goes to the highest quote of the day, not to the rank (15 Nov: Evangelia D at 50,000). The board had her at CJ-14 on the 17th under HP — wrong on the route. Her line now is the SAAGAR bulk place: the first SAAGAR place a log vessel vacates is hers (Mihir, 14 Nov). African Peacock is through ~18 Nov 22:30 and Enishi ~19 Nov 02:00 on the DPR 15.11 pace (list ETCs 19 Nov 18:34 and 09:34) — both in the window of the 18 Nov meeting, so ~19 Nov 00:30 at CJ-13 is the earliest and it slips with them (DPR 16.11 was not received). Two things can change it: (a) if she quotes at the level of the day she can take an HP place when Bristol (~19 Nov 08:00) and HN Doris (~15:00) finish — the same day; (b) the timber desk seats ML Egret on the 18th and Uni Blossom on the 19th, which uses BOTH SAAGAR places for logs — if the port sees it that way, she does not berth on the 19th by this line. The list prints no 8K rank and no Sr No 7 place for her. 55,275 MT at about 23,000 a day → ~21 Nov 15:00.

Rome Trader (salt, next call).d: 19 Nov 12:29 · BERTHED — CJ-13, 18 Nov 17:00, under SAAGAR
Rome Trader (salt, next call).slot: alongside CJ-13 · SAAGAR bulk place · loading — about 21 Nov 09:30 at the first-night pace
Rome Trader (salt, next call).why: DPR 19.11: MADE FAST 17:00, COMMENCED 19:25 on 18 Nov at CJ-13 (113–125¼), behind African Peacock, who completed 12:00 and left 14:45 — a day ahead of her list ETC. List 18.11 has her under SAAGAR with the remark "SGR- NEELKANTH"; programme 18.11 had named CJ-15 after Enishi, and the 18 Nov signal moved her to CJ-13, which freed first. The board (16 Nov) had CJ-13 on 19 Nov 00:31 by the same route — the SAAGAR bulk place — so the berth and the slot were right and she came 7½ h sooner. She waited 4 d 1 h from reporting (14 Nov 16:00). No HP place was taken: both went by quote again. Loading: 10,324 MT by 0700 on the 19th, the first 11½ h, on two shifts of 4 gangs — about 21,400 MT a day; 44,951 MT left → about 21 Nov 09:30 at that rate. No norm or ETC is printed for her yet; the next list will give the permissible time.

Rome Trader (salt, next call).d: 19 Nov 16:12 · list 19.11 — norm and ETC printed
Rome Trader (salt, next call).slot: alongside CJ-13 · SAAGAR · norm 26,000 · list ETC 20 Nov 22:01
Rome Trader (salt, next call).why: List 19.11 prints her under SAAGAR at CJ-13 with NORM 26,000 MT a day and ETC 20 Nov 22:01 (55,275 MT from commencement 18 Nov 19:25). Her first night ran at about 21,400 MT a day (DPR 19.11: 10,324 MT in 11½ h on two shifts of 4 gangs; 44,951 left at 0700 on the 19th) — at that rate she is through about 21 Nov 09:30, some 11 h past the permissible time; to make 22:01 on the 20th she needs about 27,700 MT a day from 0700 on the 19th. Programme 20.11 has no outward row for her — the ETC falls after its window — and names nobody for CJ-13; on the board Uni Blossom (SGR 1) follows her there.

Rome Trader (salt, next call).slot: alongside CJ-13 · SAAGAR · norm now 23,000 · list ETC 21 Nov 04:40 · DPR pace about 21 Nov 01:30
Rome Trader (salt, next call).why: List 20.11 restates her NORM as 23,000 MT a day (26,000 on list 19.11) and her ETC as 21 Nov 04:40 (was 20 Nov 22:01) — Nord Copper, the other salt vessel, is printed at 23,000 too. DPR 20.11: 25,320 MT in the 24 hours on 12 hooks (her first night had run at about 21,400 a day); 35,644 MT loaded, 19,631 left at 0700 on the 20th → cargo done about 21 Nov 01:30 at this rate, three hours inside the permissible time. She is not on programme 20.11 (her ETC is after its window); her outward row should come on programme 21.11.

Rome Trader (salt, next call).d: 20 Nov 12:52 · timber desk after the meeting — Uni Blossom to berth 23:00 tonight
Rome Trader (salt, next call).slot: alongside CJ-13 · SAAGAR · sailing about 20 Nov 21:00 — IMPLIED, not printed · list ETC 21 Nov 04:40 · DPR pace about 21 Nov 01:30
Rome Trader (salt, next call).why: The timber desk's sheet of 20 Nov 12:00, written after the berthing meeting, has Uni Blossom berthing at 23:00 tonight under Saagar. It names no berth. Rome Trader's is the only SAAGAR place that can free tonight (ML Egret stays at CJ-15 — her shift is off), so the board reads it as CJ-13 behind Rome Trader. That needs her off the berth by about 21:00 — seven and a half hours inside her permissible time and four and a half ahead of the DPR 20.11 pace (19,631 MT left at 0700, at 25,320 a day → about 01:30). To be done by about 20:00 she has to load at roughly 36,000 a day today. Entered as an ESTIMATE: neither signal sheet of today carries her outward movement yet (they run to 19:00). The evening signal sheet or programme 21.11 will give the hour. If Uni Blossom is meant for another berth, Rome Trader stays on her list ETC.

Rome Trader (salt, next call).slot: alongside CJ-13 · SAAGAR · PROGRAMMED OUT 21 Nov 00:30 at 12.9 m, night sailing · list ETC 21 Nov 04:40 · DPR pace about 01:30
Rome Trader (salt, next call).why: Programme 21.11 prints her outward readiness: 21 Nov 00:30, draught 12.9 m, NIGHT SAILING — with Uni Blossom into 113–124¾ behind her, night berthing. That is four hours inside her list ETC and an hour ahead of the DPR 20.11 pace: the 19,631 MT left at 0700 have to be on board by about 23:00, some 29,500 a day against 25,320 on the 19th. The board's 21:00 of this afternoon was read off the timber desk's hour for Uni Blossom (23:00) and was three and a half hours early; the berth reading (CJ-13) was right. Her let-go hour comes with DPR 21.11; after that she leaves this card.

Rome Trader (salt, next call).d: 20 Nov 20:11 · HM signal 20 Nov as amended (disp 14:00)
Rome Trader (salt, next call).slot: alongside CJ-13 · SAAGAR · SIGNALLED OUT 21 Nov 00:30 · Capt Omesh · Uni Blossom in behind her
Rome Trader (salt, next call).why: The amended signal sheet carries her outward movement: RT OUT 00:30, 113–125¼ → OTB, Capt Omesh, with Uni Blossom IN "o/c" at 113–124¾ and Meghna Prestige out after that. It agrees with programme 21.11 (00:30, 12.9 m). Her let-go hour comes with DPR 21.11; after that she leaves this card.

Rome Trader (salt, next call).slot: SAILED · completed 20 Nov 20:00, left the berth 23:40 · 55,275 MT
Rome Trader (salt, next call).why: DPR 21.11: COMPLETED 20:00 and LEFT THE BERTH 23:40 on 20 Nov — 55,275 MT loaded in 2 d 0½ h from commencement (18 Nov 19:25), about 27,300 MT a day; the last 19,631 MT went on board on 10 hooks in two shifts. She left fifty minutes ahead of the programmed 00:30 and five hours inside her permissible time (list ETC 21 Nov 04:40). Uni Blossom made fast behind her at 02:00. She leaves this card.

learn.d: 26 Nov 15:14 · Xin Bo — our salt vessel on the expected sheet
learn.ask: Xin Bo (our salt vessel, 50,000 MT, ETA 27 Nov 03:00): under which line do we take her — 30K quote, SAAGAR or 8K — and when will she be declared ready?
learn.v: The line and the readiness of MV Xin Bo.
learn.exp: The revised list 26.11 has her on the expected sheet: agent Mihir, HP Y · SGR Y · 8K Y, "30K/25K/10K Sr No 07", readiness N/A.
learn.act: A "Y" is willingness, not a place in the line: she gets a number only when she has reported and is declared ready.
learn.why: Salt works only at CJ-13 to 16. Tried on the board with her ready on 27 Nov 11:00 and last in the HP column (HP 7): she takes the Govt place Hai Nam 81 leaves — CJ-15A, about 29 Nov 01:00 — on the 30K quote, ahead of the log vessels of the SAAGAR line. Declared a day later, that place has gone to Dariya Priya.
learn.fix: MIHIR, 27 Nov 10:19 — "In today's berthing list it will be declared." The board waits for the list revised after the meeting of 27 Nov and takes her line and readiness from it. ANSWERED AND CLOSED. Before: Until she is declared ready the board shows no berth for her. OPEN — Mihir to say the line and the readiness.

learn.d: 26 Nov 15:14 · Katerina K at CJ-6 — General past its two senior vessels
learn.ask: Katerina K (GEN 3) was given CJ-6 past GEN 1 and GEN 2, whom CJ-6 does not suit. So General goes to the senior vessel the berth suits — is that how you want the board to count it?
learn.v: How the General line fills a berth its senior-most vessel cannot use.
learn.exp: Mihir, 20 Nov 17:13: General goes strictly by seniority — a junior is not given a General berth past a ready senior. The board therefore gave General nothing when the berth did not suit GEN 1.
learn.act: DPR 26.11 and the revised list: MV KATERINA K — GEN 3, kaolin / bentonite / soya bean meal, 199.99 m — made fast at CJ-6 at 04:12 on 26 Nov, two hours after Parvraj let go, under GENERAL. Fortunelit (GEN 1) and Crystal Land (GEN 2), both bag vessels, were waiting; CJ-6 is not a berth for them. She is on no programme and no signal sheet in hand.
learn.why: The port did not leave CJ-6 vacant for want of a berth for GEN 1. It agrees with Mihir's word of 22 Nov that no berth is left vacant, and with 25 Nov 17:02 — the place by priority, then a suitable berth.

learn.d: 21 Nov 20:25 · Circular 5237, point (i) — vacant Govt / Coastal places
learn.ask: Answered on 26 Nov: for a vacant Govt place the port took the senior 30K-quote vessel of the HP column (Hai Nam 81, "GOV(30K)") before the SAAGAR line.
learn.v: Point (i): with no suitable Govt / Coastal vessel, allotment goes down the order of priority up to and including Sr. No. 3(B) — 3(A) Higher productivity, 3(B) SAAGAR.
learn.exp: Board till 25 Nov: a vacant Govt or Coastal place went to SAAGAR project cargo, else to a vessel that quoted 30K / 25K (Sr No 7).
learn.act: PROGRAMME 27.11 (the meeting of 26 Nov): THE TEST CAME, AND WENT THE OTHER WAY. Parvraj's Govt place is given to MV HAI NAM 81 — salt, HP 1 on the list, "30K/25K/10K Sr No 07" — printed "GOV(30K)" at CJ-15A. CD Glory, SGR 1, was waiting and CJ-15A suits her. So the port reads "3(A) Higher productivity" in point (i) as the vessels standing in the HP column of the list on their 30K quotes, by that column's order — not only a vessel bidding 40,000 or more — and SAAGAR, 3(B), comes after them. The wording of the circular holds; the board had read the HP step too narrowly. EARLIER — PROGRAMME 26.11 (the meeting of 25 Nov): NOT PUT TO THE TEST. Parvraj's Govt place is given to nobody — CJ-6 gets no inward vessel — and the Coastal place behind Lila Tokyo goes to a coastal vessel, the tug Varahi with her barge. No SAAGAR vessel and no 30K quote is printed in a Govt or Coastal place: no timber or clean berth was left over for either. The Govt place stands vacant from 25 Nov 23:45 — the meeting of 26 Nov is the test. EARLIER: The port has said nothing yet (Mihir, 25 Nov 14:47); he asked for the clause to be read against the three papers it names. WHAT THE PAPERS SAY — (1) Policy of 24.03.2025, on allocation: the vacant berths are assessed in the Order of Allotment, a vessel of a higher category ahead of a lower one. (2) Circular of 21.05.2026, the table in force: Sr 1 Govt (2 berths) · Sr 2 Coastal (1) · 3(A) Higher productivity (2) · 3(B) SAAGAR (2) · 3(C) 24 hours (1) · 3(E) 8,000 / 6,500 (1). With no Govt or Coastal vessel, the place went to the 30,000 / 25,000 / 10,000 quotes, by seniority. (3) Corrigendum of 09.07.2026: the 48-hour wait for a Govt vessel is withdrawn; a vessel standing in a Govt place moves to Sr No 7 when a Govt vessel comes; HP ceiling 50,000; Sr No 7 is created for the berths remaining after Sr 1 to 6. (4) Circular 5237 (i): with no suitable Govt / Coastal vessel, allotment goes down the order up to and including Sr. No. 3(B).
learn.why: RESULT ON PAPER: a vacant Govt place goes to a Coastal vessel, then to an HP bid, then to the SAAGAR line by seniority; a vacant Coastal place to an HP bid, then SAAGAR. The 30K / 25K quote comes only after these. With no vessel bidding for HP (Mihir, 25 Nov), a vacant Govt or Coastal place goes straight to SAAGAR — and CD Glory is SGR 1. TWO WEAK POINTS: (a) the corrigendum of 09.07.2026 calls the 24-hour category "Sr. No. 3(B)" in a heading, though the table of 21.05.2026 has SAAGAR at 3(B) and 24 hours at 3(C). Circular 5237 itself calls the 6,500 line "3(E)" and Bitumen "Sr. No. 5" — the numbering of the 21.05.2026 table — so its 3(B) is SAAGAR; but the port could point to that heading. (b) 5237 does not strike out the 30K / 25K quote in words; it says the rest stays in force. The board reads the quote as what is left when no Coastal, HP or SAAGAR vessel can use the berth. NOT YET SEEN AT A MEETING: the one Govt place given since 23 Nov went to a Govt vessel (Zheng Hui). First test: the Govt place Parvraj leaves and the Coastal place behind Lila Tokyo — programmes 26.11 and 27.11.
learn.fix: CLOSED AGAINST THE BOARD'S READING, 26 Nov (v278), as this row said it would be. In the calculation now: a vacant Govt place goes to a Coastal vessel, then to the senior 30K / 25K quote vessel of the HP column the berth suits, then to the SAAGAR line; a vacant Coastal place to the quote vessel, then SAAGAR. CD Glory goes back to her own line's place. Whether to take this up with the port is Mihir's call — the papers of this row are the material for it. (1) ANSWERED by Mihir's team, 21 Nov 16:19 — NOT READY; her agent has not declared, and the list will show it when he does; she stays held. Mihir said on 20 Nov that she is not ready; she is still HELD out of the projection on his word — is she ready now? learn.d: 16 Nov 00:01 · Mihir — timber sheet, the 12 free hours
learn.v: TIMBER LAYTIME: after the vessel arrives, the first 12 hours are free; if she is berthed inside those 12 hours, despatch / demurrage is counted from berthing. The 12 hours are not counted. Timber is to have its own sheet, with every vessel's average and the completed vessels kept on it.
learn.exp: Board: laytime counted from the NOR itself and up to the hour the vessel let go; the timber tables sat at the bottom of the Cargo jetties page; completed vessels were mixed into the same list and their record was thin.
learn.act: Mihir, 16 Nov 00:01.
learn.why: Turn time: 12 hours after arrival, unless she berths sooner.
learn.fix: v166: TIMBER TAB — tiles, the active list (working · waiting · expected), laytime / demurrage with a bar per vessel, and the completed record (AC Kathryn, Centurion Buyo, African Quail, Lanna Naree), kept for good. Laytime now starts 12 h after arrival (or at berthing if sooner) and stops at the hour the vessel COMPLETED, not the hour she let go — about USD 10,000 a vessel less than before (Drake Well at completion ~USD 88,000, was ~98,000). Average discharge per vessel = quantity ÷ commencement-to-completion; for a waiting vessel the sheet also shows the demurrage if she works at the record average instead of the port norm. DESPATCH = HALF OF DEMURRAGE (Mihir, 16 Nov 00:24) — v167: USD 10,000 a day on the laytime saved, shown per vessel and totalled apart from demurrage. CONFIRMED by Mihir, 21 Nov 16:45: "avg dispatch" = the average DISCHARGE per day.

learn.v: The day of 20 Nov and the night, against the DPR of 21 Nov — and three faults the DPR brought out in the board's own projection.
learn.exp: Board (v198): Rome Trader out 00:30 on 21 Nov (programme / signal) · Meghna Prestige out about 04:00 (est) · Jeil Crystal out 19:00, Jag Pushpa 17:45, Kestrel 11:00 (signals / programme) · ML Egret done about 24 Nov 09:40 (DPR 20.11 pace, 7,863 CBM a day) · New Bliss done about 21 Nov 22:20 · African Hornbill out about 24 Nov (a guess — no norm) · AG Varvara into CJ-5 on 23 Nov, Manta Sena into CJ-1 at 00:21 on 22 Nov.
learn.act: DPR 21.11: Rome Trader COMPLETED 20:00, LEFT 23:40 on 20 Nov · Meghna Prestige completed 23:30, left 02:45 · Jeil Crystal left 20:00 · Jag Pushpa 17:55 · Kestrel 10:30 · Saga Viking 11:10 · Seacon Monaco completed 07:30 on the 21st. ML Egret 6,473 CBM in the day (25,854 left → about 25 Nov 06:50) · New Bliss 6,422 MT (6,072 left → about 22 Nov 05:40, so her list ETC 10:05 stands) · African Hornbill only 803 MT in a full day (10,804 left → about 4 Dec at that rate) · DSM London 4,846 MT with sugar bags started (→ about 26 Nov 16:00) · Sea Postman 8,484 MT and Dariya Priya 643 CBM at midstream.
learn.why: Sailing hours were within an hour of the signals, mostly a little late; Rome Trader a little early. The moves in the projection come from two paces: ML Egret slowed by 1,400 CBM a day, which puts her place — AG Varvara's — a day later (CJ-5, 24 Nov evening); New Bliss slowed too, so Manta Sena waits for her list ETC (CJ-1, 22 Nov about noon). African Hornbill's 24 Nov was the board's guess before she had worked a full day; at 803 MT a day she holds CJ-16 for about two weeks, and the salt vessels that need a clean berth lose it. THREE FAULTS OF THE BOARD, found because CJ-16 closed: with that berth gone the engine 'shifted' Uni Blossom off CJ-13 — first into CJ-8, which lies under Flag Marina, then into CJ-5 — for Belmoira's 6.5K / 8K place, which she cannot take past Manta Sena. (1) the shift never checked that the shifted vessel fits the berth she is moved to; (2) the free run was measured on across CJ-9 to CJ-12, which the pool does not hold; (3) the shift ignored the seniority rule of the 6.5K / 8K line.
learn.fix: All three corrected in the code (v199): the shifted vessel must fit her new berth beside its neighbours; the free run is cut at the ends of the berth's own quay (CJ-1 to CJ-8, CJ-13 to CJ-16); a line that goes by seniority makes no shift for a junior. No shift of Uni Blossom is projected now. Also: a status line no longer gives a completion date from a start-up of under six hours (Uni Blossom's first three hours, Woohyun Dream's first half hour) — the rate is counted from the commencement once she has six hours of work. African Hornbill is carried at the DPR pace, to be re-read with every DPR. The 21 Nov meeting call stays as published at 10:45, before the meeting (Blue Shark 15A · Manta Sena 1 · Xin Hai Tong 71 14) — the DPR came after the meeting hour and does not change it. CD Glory: unchanged, CJ-14 on 26 Nov night. STILL TO WATCH: by the strict General rule nobody is given CJ-5 between Vishva Bandhan (out tonight) and AG Varvara (24 Nov) — the list still prints Katerina K "B'TODAY"; programme 22.11 will show whether the port fills it.

learn.d: 20 Nov 23:48 · Mihir — geared or gearless against every vessel, by the rule
learn.v: "Waiting ya koi bhi vessel ho, waha gear or gearless wala likh do, jo gear and gearless ka rule hai woh hisab se" — with a screenshot of the Tuna tab showing MAY BE GEARLESS and NO GEAR DETAILS.

And the board had been throwing away the port's own mark: the berthing list prints "(GL)" after the name of some gearless vessels (Europa Graeca, Lila Tokyo, MSC Magali, Cretansea on list 20.11) — the name cleaner stripped it.
learn.why: The 00:05 instruction (nothing from size) was kept too long once he had himself given a size line at 00:26; what he wants on the board is an answer against every vessel.
learn.fix: v197: every vessel reads GEARED or GEARLESS — (1) found online → solid chip with the cranes; (2) "(GL)" on the DPA list → GEARLESS, solid; (3) otherwise by the size rule — above 215 m GEARLESS · BY RULE, 215 m or less GEARED · BY RULE, tug with barge GEARLESS · BARGE — dashed chip, so a confirmed one can be told from a rule one; (4) NO GEAR DETAILS only where the board has no LOA. learn.d: 20 Nov 20:11 · HM signal 20 Nov as amended (disp 12:40 / 13:25 / 14:00)

learn.exp: Board (v189–v193), from the 12:40 dispatch: Safi Alfa (GEN 1) in at 23–31¾ behind Propel Confidence, about 19:00; Propel Confidence sailing at 17:00; Meghna Prestige out 19:39 (programme 21.11); Heng Yuan Fa Zhan turned round at 16:00.

Programme 21.11 has no CJ-04 row, and the revised list keeps Safi Alfa waiting at GEN 1.

learn.fix: v194: Safi Alfa is back in the waiting rows (GEN 1) and out of the 20 Nov meeting count; CJ-4 stands empty from 17:00; Meghna Prestige's sailing is entered at about 04:00 on 21 Nov (est); the oil-jetty hours follow the amended sheet. Projection: CJ-4 → Manta Sena under 6.5K at the start of the next window (the place opens with New Bliss); Safi Alfa, whose length only CJ-4 and the clean berths take, waits for CJ-16 on the 24th; CJ-1 behind New Bliss then goes to Blue Shark. If Mihir says Safi Alfa is for CJ-4, Manta Sena goes back to CJ-1 behind New Bliss. CD Glory's date does not move (26 Nov night). ANSWERED (Mihir, 20 Nov 20:22): YES — Safi Alfa berths at CJ-4 under General. v195: she is back at CJ-4 as a fixed entry (hour estimated, about 23:00 on the 20th) and in the 20 Nov meeting count; Manta Sena returns to CJ-1 behind New Bliss. LESSON: a row that is merely ABSENT from an amended signal sheet is not cancelled — Konrad's outward row was absent too, and Flexi-2 took her berth at 16:45. Only a struck-out row is a cancellation; when the papers fall silent on a berthing, ask before taking it off. AND (20:26): the image of 20:11 was only the CONTINUATION page — the first page of the same amended sheet, received at 20:26, still carries Safi Alfa IN "o/c" at 23–31¾ and Konrad RT OUT 15:15, neither struck. A signal sheet can run to two pages; rows missing from one page may simply be on the other. The first page also corrects one hour the board had misread on the continuation page — Jag Pushpa OUT 17:45, not 14:45 — and shows why Meghna Prestige is late: her first outward row is struck "postponed due to delay in cargo operation".

learn.d: 20 Nov 17:13 · Mihir — General is strictly by seniority; CD Glory is the 26th by his reckoning
learn.v: (1) AG Varvara cannot come in General on the 21st — many vessels are senior to her; the board's calculation is wrong. (2) Laytime — noted. (3) CD Glory comes to the 26th by his reckoning.
learn.exp: Board (v192): CJ-5, free on the night of 21 Nov, goes by General to AG Varvara (GEN 16), because the seniors are bag vessels shut out by the three-bag limit or by the berth; CD Glory then moves up the SAAGAR line to CJ-16 on 24 Nov.
learn.act: Mihir's word, 20 Nov 17:13. The record agrees with him: the board's General picks have failed for days — AG Varvara for CJ-5 and Safi Alfa for CJ-4 on programmes 19.11 and 20.11, Aboudi D for CJ-3 on programme 21.11 (that berth has stood empty since the morning of the 20th) — while Safi Alfa, GEN 1, waited 32 days for her berth.
learn.why: The board read "General by seniority, at most three bag vessels alongside" (19 Nov) as: skip the seniors that cannot come in and give the berth to the next vessel that fits. The port does not do that — in General a junior does not pass a senior; the berth waits, or goes to another group.
learn.fix: v193: GEN_STRICT — a General berth, and a General cross-fill, is offered only to the senior-most ready vessel still waiting in the General line; if the berth does not suit her or the bag limit keeps her out, General takes nothing there. Result: no General berthing in the window of the 21 Nov meeting (CJ-3 and CJ-5 stand empty in the projection) · Blue Shark (GEN 2) CJ-16 24 Nov · AG Varvara CJ-5 23 Nov 22:00 by SAAGAR (ML Egret's place) · CD GLORY CJ-14 26 Nov 22:00 by SAAGAR (Uni Blossom's place) — Mihir's 26th. Uni Blossom's stay is estimated at the record average of the completed log vessels (5,600 CBM a day) until the list prints her ETC. With the 16:50 ruling, a junior no longer passes a senior in General or in 6.5K / 8K.

learn.d: 20 Nov 16:50 · Mihir — the 6.5K / 8K place goes by seniority
learn.v: CD Glory cannot berth at CJ-5 under the 6.5K priority, as other vessels are senior to her in that priority. (His second point: the note on laytime was not clear to him — explained again in the chat; no rule changed.)
learn.exp: Board (v190 / v191): CJ-5, when Vishva Bandhan has finished there on the night of 21 Nov, goes down the 6.5K / 8K line to CD Glory (8K 9), because none of the eight ahead of her can lie at CJ-5 — the 11 Nov reading, "the place is never held for a berth that frees later".
learn.act: Mihir's word, 20 Nov 16:50 — in answer to the board's question whether the port would give her CJ-5 or keep the place for Manta Sena.
learn.why: In 6.5K / 8K seniority decides, not which berth frees first. The 11 Nov answer ("if no suitable berth is available for the senior, the berth goes to the next senior that fits") does not carry a junior past eight ready seniors — the more so when a berth that suits the senior-most (CJ-1, behind New Bliss) frees the same night.
learn.fix: v192: SENIOR_ONLY=['8K'] in the projection — in the 6.5K / 8K line a junior is not a candidate while a ready senior of the line is still waiting (a senior with no berth she could ever use is not counted); the berth goes down the order to the other groups. Result: Manta Sena CJ-1 about 22 Nov 00:20 (8K) · AG Varvara CJ-5 21 Nov 22:00 (General) · CD Glory CJ-16 24 Nov 06:00 by SAAGAR. The other single-place lines (Coastal, 24 hrs, Steel / Project) still follow the 11 Nov reading — Mihir spoke of 6.5K only. OPTS ranks brought to the revised list (SGR 4, 8K 9).

learn.v: (1) Rock phosphate is NOT government cargo. (2) The sailing of Truong Minh Dream (Govt priority) was delayed; because of that Belmoira could not berth, so the shifting of ML Egret was not required and was cancelled. (3) Uni Blossom is senior in SAAGAR, so she berths after Rome Trader sails. (4) Timber laytime — apply the simple rule: 12 hours free from arrival, no further rule.
learn.exp: Board: (1) since v189 rock phosphate gets no automatic Govt rank — its own reading. (2) v189 had read the cancelled shift as the port preferring Safi Alfa (GEN 1) for CJ-4. (3) Uni Blossom at CJ-13 behind Rome Trader — read from the desk sheet, then printed on programme 21.11. (4) Laytime started 12 hours after arrival, OR at berthing if she berthed inside those 12 hours (16 Nov).
learn.act: Mihir's word, 20 Nov 15:53.
learn.why: (2) is the point the board had wrong. Belmoira was to berth as GOVT(30K) — a 30K quote against the Govt place that Truong Minh Dream was to vacate. Truong Minh Dream (list ETC 19 Nov 13:46) was still alongside through the window of programme 20.11 and sails only at 18:15 on 20 Nov, so the place never opened for Belmoira; with no Belmoira there was nothing to clear CJ-15 for, and ML Egret stayed. CJ-4 was then simply free — Safi Alfa. A quote vessel's berthing against a priority place stands or falls with the sailing of the vessel that holds the place.
learn.fix: v191: (1) confirmed — no code change; the cargo rule already skips rock phosphate (Sea Postman, Princess Manissa). (2) notes on ML Egret and Belmoira corrected; ML Egret stays in NO_SHIFT (cancelled); in the 19 Nov meeting record Belmoira and Katerina K are taken out of the berthed count — they were programmed but did not berth. (3) confirmed, nothing to change. (4) CODE: laytime now starts at arrival + 12 h in every case — the clause about berthing inside the 12 hours is removed from the calculation and from the rule text on the Timber tab. No vessel on the sheet had berthed inside her 12 hours, so no figure moves (CD Glory: laytime from 15 Nov 18:42, ends 23 Nov 01:38).

learn.d: 20 Nov 12:52 · HM signals 20 Nov (disp 10:55 and 12:40) + timber desk sheet 20 Nov 12:00
learn.v: The day sheets of 20 Nov against programme 20.11 and the board. TO CONFIRM WITH MIHIR: (1) Uni Blossom "will berth 23:00 under Saagar" — at CJ-13 behind Rome Trader? Then Rome Trader sails about 21:00 tonight. (2) Parvraj is signalled in with the berth "pending" — is it CJ-6 behind Truong Minh Dream?
learn.exp: Programme 20.11 / board v188: Katerina K into CJ-6 behind Truong Minh Dream ("provisional berthing") · ML Egret shifted CJ-15 → CJ-4 on the port's account about 17:30, and Belmoira into CJ-15 as GOVT(30K) · Ken Ann into CJ-5 about 19:30 · Willows into OJ-6 · Sea Postman next under Govt (bulk rock phosphate — the board's cargo rule) · Uni Blossom into CJ-13 about 21 Nov 06:40 · CD Glory CJ-5 21 Nov 21:30 under 6.5K / 8K.
learn.act: Signals: KEN ANN in at 11:00 behind Saga Viking (shifted to OTB) — eight hours early · KATERINA K struck out, "cancelled by Traffic" · SAFI ALFA (GEN 1) in at 23–31¾ — CJ-4 — behind Propel Confidence (RT OUT 17:00): the berth printed for ML Egret, whose shift is not signalled · PARVRAJ (DAP, GP Y, reported 01:56 today) in "o/c", berth "PENDING" · Truong Minh Dream out 18:15 · Orchids, not Willows, into OJ-6 · Hatnyanawati into OJ-2 behind Jeil Crystal (19:00) · Belmoira not signalled. [CORRECTED by Mihir, 20 Nov 15:53: it was the other way round — Truong Minh Dream's sailing was delayed, so Belmoira could not take the Govt place; ML Egret's shift was then not required and was cancelled, which left CJ-4 for Safi Alfa.] The board had read: the port preferred the senior General vessel (Safi Alfa, waiting since 19 Oct) to its own programmed shift of ML Egret, so Belmoira's clean berth did not open — the board's run of 19 Nov 12:29, before programme 20.11, had Safi Alfa at CJ-4 behind Propel Confidence. [CORRECTED 20 Nov 15:13: the board also said here that its own date for CD Glory had stood on a misread note about Manta Sena. It had not — see the entry of 15:13. Ken Ann's early berthing was the cause.]
learn.fix: v189: signals entered (Safi Alfa CJ-4, Ken Ann CJ-5, Katerina K and Belmoira back in the waiting rows, Parvraj at the fertiliser berth that frees first, oil jetties). RULES — (a) the automatic Govt rank by cargo no longer covers ROCK phosphate [CONFIRMED by Mihir, 20 Nov 15:53: rock phosphate is not government cargo]; (b) NO_SHIFT: a shift the port has dropped (ML Egret) is not projected again until a programme prints it [Mihir, 20 Nov 15:53: the shifting was not required and cancelled]; (c) the meeting call is FROZEN as it stood before the meeting, so papers that arrive after the meeting cannot improve the score; (d) Manta Sena's note reworded — a note that says "CJ-1 to 4" is read as a berth request. Uni Blossom is entered at CJ-13 for 23:00 and Rome Trader's sailing at about 21:00, both as estimates. CD Glory: SAAGAR line, CJ-14 about 23 Nov night (desk 26 Nov). ANSWERED by programme 21.11 (20 Nov 15:13): (1) Uni Blossom — CJ-13, 113–124¾, behind Rome Trader, as read; Rome Trader out 21 Nov 00:30, not 21:00. (2) Parvraj — CJ-6, 43–51¼, GOV.

learn.why: The step was the board's own estimate, set from bulk loaders. Bag vessels of this size do load at CJ-1 to 4 — what they cannot take at the berth is finished at midstream.
learn.fix: v188: for bag cargo the 11.2 m step starts at 35,000 MT (bulk stays at 30,000). Manta Sena and Crystal Land can now be seated at CJ-1 to 4 as well. learn.why: (1) THE HP PLACE GOES TO THE HIGHEST MTPD QUOTE OF THE DAY, NOT TO THE HP RANK: 46,000 on 16 Nov (two salt vessels), 50,000 on 15 Nov (Evangelia D). A ranked vessel that does not quote at that level is passed over: CJ-15A, a clean berth Rome Trader (HP 3, salt) could have used, went to Bristol (HP 7, salt). (Gokova-M, HP 1, was not passed over in that sense — the deep berths she can use, CJ-7 and CJ-8, went to the Coastal and Govt slots, which come first.) The board had ordered the HP line by rank. (2) The list now prints, in the column of the slot itself, the place of each Sr No 7 quote vessel for that slot when it is vacant (CSTL: Nord Copper 1, Propel Confidence 2; 24H: Gokova-M 1) — the board had one pool for all vacant slots, ordered by reporting time, which is how Gokova-M came to be its pick for the Coastal place. A true 24-hour vessel (Phoenix Coral, 24H 2) goes before a quote vessel standing in that column; a quote vessel that needs a clean berth (Nord Copper, CSTL 1) is passed when none is given to that slot. (3) A vessel that declares readiness between two lists takes her place by reporting time at once: New Bliss (reported 19 Oct, ready 15 Nov) is 8K 1 ahead of Pioneer Fortune — and the board never saw list 15.11. (4) The port cleared a clean berth for an HP salt vessel by moving North Gate (CJ-15A → CJ-2), not the two vessels the board had picked. (5) No outward row on a programme = no sailing in that window: Theometor, Bomustafao O, Drake Well and Princess Joanna all stayed past the end of programme 16.11's window though their pace or ETC ended inside it.
learn.fix: v172: programme 17.11, the night sheet and the revised list entered; every waiting vessel's ranks, readiness and remarks refreshed. Code: (a) Rome Trader is carried as not taking part in HP at the level of the day — she goes through the SAAGAR bulk place (CJ-13, ~19 Nov 00:30); her HP route stays on the Mihir & Co card as an option; (b) the Sr No 7 places are taken from the list's own columns where it prints them; (c) a Sr No 7 vessel is given 30,000 a day — the norm the list prints for every one of them — in place of her cargo norm (a comparison in the code that was meant to do this never matched, which had stacked Propel Confidence, Meghna Prestige and Bristol at CJ-16 a day apart); (d) a vessel alongside with no outward row on the programme in hand keeps her berth to the end of its window (Theometor → 17 Nov 18:00 at the earliest); (e) horizon to 24 Nov. OPEN (1) — ROME TRADER AND HP: was she offered for HP at the 16 Nov meeting, and at what MTPD? If she can quote at the day's level (46,000 on the 16th) she can take an HP place when Bristol / HN Doris finish (~19 Nov); if not, SAAGAR bulk is her only line. OPEN (2) — THE DESK SHEET of 16 Nov seats ML Egret on the 18th and Uni Blossom on the 19th, i.e. both SAAGAR places to log vessels. By the rule of 14 Nov the first place that frees goes to Rome Trader (bulk) — and Uni Blossom then waits till ~21 Nov. Which is right? OPEN (3) — list 16.11 prints NO 8K / 6.5K rank for CD Glory or Rome Trader and no Sr No 7 place (CSTL / 24H column) for Rome Trader, though both vessels were to be declared under those — to check with the port. The board's own soft spots: AG Varvara at CJ-4 on 18 Nov under General (the desk says 24 Nov) rests on Rahma leaving CJ-3 by the morning of the 18th and on three bag vessels counting against the General limit; DPR 16.11 was not received, so African Peacock, Enishi, Theometor and North Gate still run on the pace of 15 Nov.
