learn.d: 15 Nov 17:48 · Mihir answers the two points on programme 16.11
learn.v: (1) EVERY BAG-CARGO VESSEL BERTHED UNDER GENERAL GETS 2 DAYS' EXTENSION. (2) ROME TRADER needs a clean berth and her cargo lies on the CJ-13 to 16 side — so the shift that opens her berth is on PORT account, not hers.
learn.exp: Board (v162): read Theometor and Bomustafao O as "past the permissible time, not moved because the programme has no outward row for them"; and asked whether a clean berth for Rome Trader has to be opened at the agent's cost, as Parekh Marine did for Rahma.
learn.act: Mihir, 15 Nov 17:48 — as above.
learn.why: The permissible time of a bag vessel under General is the list ETC plus two days — Theometor (list ETC 16 Nov 02:06 → 18 Nov 02:06) and Bomustafao O (14 Nov 11:33 → 16 Nov 11:33) are inside it, which is why programme 16.11 does not move them; Bomustafao O's DPR pace (~16 Nov 11:00) ends almost exactly with her extension. A shift is at the agent's cost when the agent wants a particular berth (Rahma, "REQ CJ 13 TO 16"; African Hornbill at CJ-4); it is on port account when the vessel must have a clean berth for her cargo and the cargo is on that side (salt).
learn.fix: v163: a berthed bag vessel under General is carried at her DPR pace up to list ETC + 48 h — the berth is free at the earlier of the two (Theometor ~17 Nov 14:13, North Gate ~18 Nov 11:05 instead of 17 Nov 04:59, Bomustafao O ~16 Nov 11:00); beyond the extension the port enforces as before. Projected stays of bag vessels that have not berthed yet stay at the norm — they can run up to 2 days longer. Rome Trader: no change of date (CJ-14, ~17 Nov 13:30 under HP); the port-convenience shift in the projection is confirmed as the right basis.

learn.v: Programme 16.11 against the board (DPR 15.11 run, 10:30 / 10:50): of four berthings the board had inside this window, the programme makes two — EVANGELIA D at CJ-16 (berth and group as predicted, ~11 h later) and RAHMA (at CJ-15A, not CJ-14). DENIZ ID and SAGA VIKING are not programmed. HONOR STAR goes to the GFPL berth CJ-9 and the pipe barge to CJ-15A — neither is in the board's pool. ROME TRADER is not on it.
learn.exp: Board: Evangelia D → CJ-16 15 Nov 18:00 (HP) · Rahma → CJ-14 16 Nov 04:06, at Theometor's permissible time · Deniz ID → CJ-2 16 Nov 12:58 after Bomustafao O · Saga Viking → CJ-5 16 Nov 15:00 after Princess Joanna · Cape Diversity out ~13:00 on the 15th · Shanaya out ~16 Nov 18:00 · Lujain to stay at OJ-4.
learn.act: PROGRAMME 16.11 (TF/SH/2102, dated 15 Nov): Cape Diversity out 16 Nov 03:00 (night) → Evangelia D CJ-16 173½–188 HP(50K), night berthing. Merchia out 13:00 → North Gate SHIFTED CJ-15A → CJ-3 (18½–26¼) "A/C PAREKH MARINE" → Rahma CJ-15A 156–164½ STEEL/PROJ. Leya "shifting from CJ-09 to OTB, agent's req." 17:30 → Honor Star CJ-9 (GFPL). Tug Chandra Sun + barge Victoria 251 → CJ-15A (CSTL, night). No outward row for Theometor, Bomustafao O, Drake Well; no rows for CJ-5 / CJ-6. Oil jetties: Lavraki out 20:00 → Haein Hope OJ-2 · Bow Platinum out 21:00 → Lujain moved OJ-4 → OJ-3 (agent's a/c) → Avyaan OJ-4 · Shanaya out 02:00 → Ishaan OJ-6. Tuna: Mykonos Wave out 12:30 → Beagle TT-3.
learn.why: (1) A vessel past her permissible time is not moved unless the programme carries an outward row for her: Theometor (list ETC 16 Nov 02:06) and Bomustafao O (over since 14 Nov) work on, and a berth is programmed only against a declared outward readiness — so CJ-2 and CJ-5, which the board expected to free on its own estimate, were not allotted. (2) The berth for Rahma was opened by shifting a working vessel at the cost of the agent who wanted the berth (Parekh Marine is Rahma's agent) — the second such case in two programmes (Enishi for African Hornbill, a/c Delta). The board had modelled such shifts only as port convenience. (3) A cape that completes by day can still be held for a night tide: Cape Diversity completes ~13:00 and sails 03:00, which sets the time of the vessel behind her. (4) An oil-jetty vessel can be moved between jetties at her agent's cost to make a particular jetty free (Lujain for Avyaan, which needs OJ-4).
learn.fix: v162: programme 16.11 is on the board. New in the projection: a vessel whose permissible time falls inside a programme that has no outward row for her is carried to her DPR completion (Theometor → ~17 Nov 14:13). Rome Trader: CJ-14 ~17 Nov 13:30 under HP on the board — a range of 17 Nov afternoon to 18 Nov evening, see her log. Options run corrected: a vessel limited to one route was being ranked through the 30K/25K pool first and then dropped, which left her SAAGAR / 6.5K-8K / General lines without a date since v161. OPEN — to confirm with Mihir: (a) is a vessel past her permissible time moved only when another vessel needs that berth and the port programmes it — Theometor and Bomustafao O were both left; (b) can an agent ask for a working log / bag vessel to be shifted off a clean berth at his own cost (as Parekh Marine did for Rahma) — for Rome Trader that would be African Peacock or Theometor — or does the port make that shift itself, as port convenience, for salt? — BOTH ANSWERED by Mihir, 15 Nov 17:48: see the entry of that time.

learn.v: Yesterday's movements against the board's estimates: sailings and berthings came within minutes to about 3 hours. The two night moves (Princess Joanna to CJ-5, Truong Minh Dream into CJ-6) were not made by 0700. TPT Heart was sent out of OJ-2 with two-thirds of her cargo still to load. The log vessels slowed sharply.
learn.exp: Board (14 Nov 18:15): Chang Hang out 13:45 · Karpathos Dawn out 14:30 · Merchia re-berthed CJ-3 16:00 · Cape Venture in 16:30 · CD Cherry in 17:00 · Belasitza out 17:30 · Bristol to CJ-5 19:00, out 23:45 · Princess Joanna in 20:30, to CJ-5 ~02:00 · Truong Minh Dream in ~03:00 · Doukato out 03:00, Europa Graeca ~05:00 · TPT Heart out 04:00, Lavraki ~06:00 · Enishi through ~16 Nov 17:00 · African Peacock ~18 Nov 08:00.
learn.act: DPR 15.11: Chang Hang 13:45 · Karpathos Dawn 14:45 · Merchia re-made fast 18:50 · Cape Venture made fast 19:45 · CD Cherry 17:15 · Belasitza 17:40 · Bristol re-made fast CJ-5 18:30, let go 02:30 · Princess Joanna 20:42, still at CJ-6 at 0700 · Truong Minh Dream not berthed · Doukato 04:42, Europa Graeca 06:15 · TPT Heart: work stopped 02:42, let go 04:30, to OTB with 4,016 of 6,302 MT still to load; Lavraki 06:54 · Enishi 2,312 MT in 24 h (8,760 left → ~19 Nov 02:00) · African Peacock 3,040 MT (→ ~18 Nov 22:30) · Cape Diversity 9,936 MT left (≈ 13:00 today), no outward row · Drake Well 7,882 CBM (→ ~17 Nov 01:15).
learn.why: The small slips are tide and pilot timing. Cape Venture (+3¼ h) and Merchia (+2¾ h) both hung on Chang Hang's 13:45 sailing and the shift behind it. Bristol finished at 22:55 and sailed on the next tide (02:30), so CJ-5 was free for Princess Joanna only after the night window. TPT Heart: the port ended her stay at the programmed time although loading was not complete — the same enforcement as Alberta on 13 Nov. Log vessels: a day's output swings by half, and one slow day moves a SAAGAR place by two days.
learn.fix: v160: actual times entered; DPR rows, balances and paces refreshed; Princess Joanna's shift and Truong Minh Dream's berthing carried as placeholders (~13:00 / ~15:00 today) until a signal sheet gives the times. learn.v: RULE CONFIRMED — SAAGAR bulk and break bulk are separate priorities. BOARD ERROR FOUND while checking Rome Trader's date on that rule: Bomustafao O was still counted against the HP slot, so the board saw HP as full and gave CJ-16 to SAAGAR.
learn.exp: v158 (16:30): CJ-16 after Cape Diversity → Rome Trader under SAAGAR bulk, 15 Nov ~21:00; the HP slot "no taker"; Rahma CJ-14 on 16 Nov 04:00.
learn.act: Mihir: bulk and break bulk are separate SAAGAR priorities. If no bulk vessel is waiting, a SAAGAR break-bulk vessel gets the berth and the priority is occupied; when a berth frees again and a SAAGAR bulk vessel is waiting, she gets it even if a SAAGAR break-bulk vessel is senior. — List 14.11 prints Bomustafao O under GENERAL (CJ-2), and from 12 Nov two HP vessels lay alongside while she worked (Cape Diversity + Chang Hang, then Cape Venture): her 8 Nov cross-fill ("C/F") against the vacant HP slot does not hold that slot against a real HP vessel.
learn.why: The bulk-first order was already in the board (regulation of 1 Nov) and stands as coded. The error was in the slot count: a General vessel cross-filled against HP was treated as an HP occupant for good. HP stands above SAAGAR in the slot order, and two HP vessels that fit CJ-16 are ready (Evangelia D, HP 2; HN Doris, HP 3) — so CJ-16 is theirs before Rome Trader's.
learn.fix: v159: Bomustafao O carried as a General vessel; a General cross-fill no longer blocks a real HP vessel; CJ-16 after Cape Diversity → Evangelia D (HP); Rome Trader → CJ-14, ~16 Nov 04:00, in the SAAGAR bulk place — CJ-15 behind Enishi (~16 Nov 19:00) if the port does not clear Theometor at her permissible time. Also: the port-convenience shift is now made for the group's SENIOR vessel that needs a clean berth, by cargo or by her berth requirement (Rahma, STL 1, REQ CJ 13–16, was being passed over for Heng Yuan Fa Zhan, STL 2). The 16:30 predictions that changed are kept in the log and marked superseded.

learn.v: Programme 15.11 against the board: NONE of the three cargo-jetty berthings was projected. TRUONG MINH DREAM (Govt, CJ-6) and AFRICAN HORNBILL (24 hrs, CJ-4) declared readiness after the list the board had; ENISHI is shifted CJ-4 → CJ-15 at the cost of Hornbill's agent.
learn.exp: Board (DPR 14.11, 10:15): CJ-15 after CD Cherry → Xin Hai Tong 71 (24 hrs); CJ-14 → Rahma, with Theometor moved; CJ-16 → HN Doris (salt) after Cape Diversity; CJ-5 after Bristol → Sea Gautham, then CD Glory; Princess Joanna to stay at CJ-6 till ~17 Nov; Enishi to finish at CJ-4.
learn.act: PROGRAMME 15.11 (TF/SH/2102): Bristol out 14 Nov 23:45 (night) → Princess Joanna moved CJ-6 → CJ-5, 37–45¾, port convenience → Truong Minh Dream CJ-6, 46¾–54½, GOVT, night berthing. CD Cherry out 15 Nov 17:00 → Enishi shifted CJ-4 → CJ-15, 142½–155, "agent's a/c (Delta Shg)" → African Hornbill CJ-4, 27¼–36, 24 HRS, sailing draft 10.0. No outward row for Cape Diversity, Bomustafao O, Theometor or Merchia; Rahma, Xin Hai Tong 71, HN Doris, Gokova-M, Pioneer Fortune and Uni Blossom are not berthed. LIST 14.11: Truong Minh Dream ready 13 Nov 11:00, GP 1; African Hornbill ready 14 Nov 11:00, 24H 1 · SGR 2 · STL 3 — both were N/A on the 13.11 list, both reported 9 Nov. Pioneer Fortune ready, 8K 1. Sea Gautham "DISPUTE (waiting for shipper's confirmation)". Xin Hai Tong 71: SGR 4 · STL 4, no 24H. ML Egret: SGR "Y", 8K 2. CD Glory: 29,158 CBM, 179.9 m, 10.5 m, ETA 15 Nov 12:00, N/A. Rome Trader: salt 55,275 MT, agent Mihir, SGR Y.
learn.why: (1) A senior vessel that is N/A on the morning list can declare readiness before the 11:00 meeting and take her group's slot the same day; the board works from the printed readiness and cannot see that coming. (2) The port makes the particular berth a 24-hr vessel needs by shifting the working vessel at the incoming agent's cost (Enishi for Hornbill), and re-seats a Govt vessel hours after berthing so that the deeper one gets CJ-6. (3) 25,000 MT loads to 10.0 m — CJ-4 suits a 25K loader; the board's loaded-draught step (11.2 m from 25,000 MT) was too strict.
learn.fix: v158: programme 15.11 entered; ranks, readiness and remarks of every waiting vessel refreshed from list 14.11; CD Glory on her real particulars; Rome Trader (salt) added as a Mihir & Co vessel with options — as the only SAAGAR bulk vessel she is given the SAAGAR place Enishi vacates, ahead of the next log vessel (regulation: 1 bulk + 1 break bulk; the board had been counting the finishing vessel when deciding which place was free); loaded-draught step moved to 30,000 MT, so Pioneer Fortune (8K 1) can use CJ-1 to CJ-4 — she, not CD Glory, is next for the 6.5K / 8K berth; horizon extended to 22 Nov; Sea Gautham held while the DISPUTE remark stands; tanker ETC on the list = made fast + quantity ÷ hourly norm + 4 h (fits all four printed ETCs). The "if ready today" date on each N/A vessel's card is the guard against point (1). (1) ANSWERED (Mihir, 14 Nov 18:00): yes — a waiting SAAGAR bulk vessel gets the freed place even if a break-bulk vessel is senior; see the 18:00 entry, where her berth is corrected to CJ-14 on 16 Nov. Still OPEN on Rome Trader: is SAAGAR the only route to be declared? OPEN (2): CD Glory — readiness N/A and no group marked. Which groups will be declared, and will she be ready on arrival (15 Nov 12:00)? The board assumes ready on arrival, SGR + 6.5K. OPEN (3): Xin Hai Tong 71 — her "4" stood under 24H on the 13.11 sheet and stands under SGR today; taken as printed. Right? OPEN (4), carried: Karpathos Dawn stayed about 31 hours under the 24-hr priority — tide wait, or an extension? — ALL ANSWERED by Mihir, 15 Nov 10:49: see the entry of that time.

(2) carried into the 15:55 entry.

learn.d: 13 Nov 23:07 · Mihir + gang sheet III shift + night sheet (amendment)

CRANES TONIGHT: nine HMCs working and all nine allotted — Chang Hang 5, Cape Diversity 3, Karpathos Dawn 1.

GANG SHEET 13 Nov III shift — working cranes: S/C 1–5, NEW HMC 4–8 (NEW 3 is also allotted), DPA Liebherr 01 / 02, OLD HMC 02; OLD HMC 01 out of order since 10 Oct 15:00. Allotment: CJ-7 Chang Hang (GL) 4 NEW + 1 OLD · CJ-16 Cape Diversity (GL) 1 NEW + 2 Liebherr · CJ-15 Karpathos Dawn 1 NEW · CJ-8 Merchia private AVJ HMC · CJ-9 Leya 2 GFPL · Cape Venture 1 floating crane at midstream. NIGHT SHEET (amendment, disp 2000 / 2055): oil-jetty and mooring rows only — no cargo-jetty movement before 10:00 on the 14th.
learn.why: (1) The Govt rank belongs to the CARGO, not to the morning sheet: fertiliser = Govt. (2) The 24-hr rule is the no-slot-holding rule the board already runs — CD Glory gets CJ-15 because Honor Star (24H 1, gearless coal) cannot use it. (3) Two gearless HP vessels alongside split the HMC pool 5 : 3 — the cape has three cranes tonight, not the four of her first day, and nothing is spare for a third user.
learn.fix: v154: a bulk fertiliser vessel without a printed Govt rank now queues as Govt by seniority (Vishva Bandhan, urea 44,000 MT — her readiness of 12 Nov 23:54 had also been left blank; corrected with Sea Gautham and Xin Hai Tong 71). OPEN (1): does the Govt priority also cover BAGGED fertiliser parcels (NPK / manganese sulphate J-bags)? The board leaves them as listed. OPEN (2): Cape Diversity at three cranes — the 33,000/day pace and her list ETC (15 Nov 05:43) are at risk; DPR 14.11 will show. Queen Coral and Tan Binh 259 go to moorings (MRG-2 / MRG-3, 09:45 on the 14th) and are not berth takers. — ANSWERED (Mihir, 14 Nov 10:07): only BULK cargo counts as Govt priority (the board already ran it that way); "2 shore crane req" = CJ-2 / 3 for a bag vessel, CJ-6 / 7 / 8 or 13–16 for a bulk vessel (coded v156). DPR 14.11: Cape Diversity did 33,104 MT on gangs 4 / 4 / 3 — the pace held.

learn.v: Programme 14.11 vs the board's DPR-based predictions: NONE of the eight matched. The port berths CAPE VENTURE (HP 1, 292 m, after lighterage to 13.5 m) across CJ-7/8, PRINCESS JOANNA (MOP) at CJ-6 as GOVT, CD GLORY (new, 24 hrs) at CJ-15 — and shifts three working vessels (Bristol CJ-6→5, Merchia CJ-8→3, Enishi warped) to do it.
learn.exp: Board (DPR 13.11 + policy, 09:30): Rahma CJ-15, Gokova-M CJ-7, CD Cherry CJ-5, Saga Viking CJ-2, Honor Star CJ-8, AG Varvara CJ-5, ML Egret CJ-7, Uni Blossom CJ-16.
learn.act: Programme 14.11: CJ-7/8 → Cape Venture HP(42.5K) 55¾–67½ "13.50 M after lighterage"; CJ-6 → Princess Joanna GOV (GEN 19 on the sheet); CJ-5 → Bristol shifted from CJ-6 (PORT C.); CJ-3 → Merchia shifted from CJ-8 (PORT C.); Enishi warped 22¼–30¼ → 28¾–36¾ (A/C Genesis); CJ-15 → CD Glory 24 HRS (not on any list yet). Rahma, Gokova-M, CD Cherry, Saga Viking, Honor Star, ML Egret, AG Varvara, Uni Blossom: not programmed. Bomustafao O (permissible 11:33) not programmed out.
learn.why: Three blind spots, each now a rule. (1) LIGHTERAGE: a cape at midstream becomes berthable when lightered to 13.5 m — the board treated Cape Venture (17.39 m) as unplaceable; at ~135 t/cm she needed ~52,000 MT off, and DPR 13.11 showed 33,525 + barges — berthable on the 14th was computable. (2) GOVT CARGO: MOP for a Govt consignee berths under GOV although the waiting sheet prints only a GEN rank — the board must flag Govt fertiliser imports (MOP / urea / DAP for Govt account) as GOV candidates. (3) PORT CONVENIENCE SHIFTS: to seat an HP cape and a Govt vessel the port moves working vessels (Bristol, Merchia, Enishi) — the board's shift logic exists but only fires for a vessel it already sees as ready. Also: a new 24-hr arrival (CD Glory) can take the 24-hr berth over the ranked 24H queue when none of the ranked vessels suits that berth (Honor Star 24H 1 is gearless coal → CJ-7/8 only).
learn.fix: Board set to the programme. New rules to code next: lighterage draught model for capes (berthable when (draught − 13.5 m) × TPC is discharged), Govt-cargo flag for fertiliser imports with a Govt consignee (Mihir: how is a Govt vessel recognised before the programme — consignee on the IGM?), and the 24-hr berth going to any ready 24-hr vessel that fits when the ranked ones do not. The 8 open predictions stay open until the actuals (they will score as misses). — ANSWERED (Mihir, 13 Nov 23:07): all fertiliser cargo = Govt priority (the 0700 list may omit the rank; it shows on the noon list); the 24-hr slot goes by seniority to a vessel that can finish in 24 h and fits the berth, else to a 30k/25k vessel. v154 codes the fertiliser flag; the 24-hr rule was already the board's (no slot holding). The lighterage model is to be coded with the next cape.

learn.v: ALBERTA SHIFTED OUT AT HER PERMISSIBLE TIME with 3,517 MT still to load — work stopped 02:30, let go 04:45, to OTB 07:18; Chang Hang (HP) in behind her. Nord Newport, by contrast, was let to finish.
learn.exp: Board (12 Nov): permissible time tolerated up to a day when the DPR pace runs over (Nord Newport rule); Alberta complete ~03:00 at her first-night rate.
learn.act: DPR 13.11: Alberta 31,409 MT in 24 h but 3,517 short at the list ETC 04:31 — the port stopped work at 02:30 and shifted her to OTB; she now waits for a re-berthing (as Karpathos Dawn, 9 Nov). Nord Newport (50 MT left at 0700) sails 11:10.
learn.why: The difference is the queue, not the balance: Chang Hang was PROGRAMMED into CJ-7 behind Alberta, so the permissible time was enforced to the minute; nothing was programmed behind Nord Newport, so she was let run. Rule: permissible time is a hard limit when the next vessel is on the programme for that berth; otherwise a small overrun is tolerated.
learn.fix: Coded: the under-a-day tolerance applies only when no fixed (programmed) vessel is due at that berth around the permissible time. Alberta added to the waiting list (re-berthing, 3,517 MT, loaded ~13 m → CJ-7/8).

learn.v: CJ-16 OPEN TO ALL DRY CARGO in practice — "the port has given no notification, but it has removed the cargo restriction from berth 16". CJ-13 / 14 / 15 / 15A remain clean (pellets allowed at all of 13–16 since 11 Nov).

From today the projection berths coal / dirty bulk at CJ-16 when the slot order brings such a vessel to it (gearless coal still needs the CJ-7/8 shore cranes). learn.v: 24-HRS PRIORITY RULE: a vessel berthed under 24 hrs has to sail within 24 hours of berthing, unless the port grants an extension — which it normally does not. 24 hrs = 1 berth. Karpathos Dawn will berth and sail within 24 h.
learn.exp: Board: Karpathos Dawn at CJ-15 ~2.7 days at the 3,450 bagged norm (to 16 Nov); the single 24-hr slot held till then, so General (Saga Viking) was taken before the waiting 24H vessels.
learn.act: Mihir: the 24-hrs vessel sails in 24 hours anyhow — the slot is free again by 14 Nov ~14:00. Saga Viking (General) should not come before a 24H vessel while a 24-hr slot is vacant.
learn.why: The 24-hrs priority is a promise, not a norm: the vessel commits to finish in a day and goes out whatever is left. So the slot turns over daily and the waiting 24H vessels (Honor Star 24H 2, Gokova-M 24H 3, CD Cherry 24H 4) each get a berth before a General vessel — at a berth that suits them (coal / clay / kaolin → CJ-5–8).
learn.fix: Fixed 24H entries capped at berthing + 24 h (Karpathos Dawn out ~14 Nov 14:00); projected 24H stays were already 22 h. The projection now shows the 24H queue turning over at CJ-5–8 ahead of General.

learn.v: DRAKE WELL PROGRAMMED — CJ-1 after Nord Newport (readiness 13 Nov 11:10), 6.5K, 7¼–N, starboard side. CJ-15 went to KARPATHOS DAWN (24 HRS), not to the 8K slot; Nord Newport was let to finish past her permissible time
learn.exp: Board (11:30): Drake Well → CJ-15 tonight after Bao He Ling (DPR pace ~17:30) under the 8K slot; Nord Newport shifted out at the permissible time 19:08 (Karpathos precedent); Zheng Rong out ~23:30; Alberta ~03:00; CJ-8 next → Gokova-M (24-hr / Coastal, 30K quote).

learn.why: Three lessons. (1) 24-hr slot before 8K: Karpathos Dawn is 24H 1 on the 12.11 list and fits CJ-15 — by the slot order (Govt, Coastal, HP, SAAGAR, 24-hr, 8K …) the 24-hr vessel takes the first suitable berth before the 8K vessel; the board had her at rank "Y" only and under-weighted her. (2) Permissible time is not a guillotine: Nord Newport, ~2,500 MT short at 19:08, is let to finish (readiness 11:10 next day) — the port shifts a vessel out when the balance is large (Karpathos, ~2 days), not for a few hours. (3) A pellet vessel's sailing is programmed at the list ETC / a daylight readiness, not the DPR pace: Zheng Rong 06:00 (not 23:30), Bao He Ling 12:00 (not 17:30).
learn.fix: Drake Well fixed at CJ-1 ~13:00 tomorrow (6.5K), 8,000 / 6,500 norm, ~16 Nov est. Rule: a DPR overrun under 24 h is let run (T = DPR ETC, flagged), over 24 h the permissible time still stands. Karpathos Dawn, Chang Hang, Merchia fixed per the programme; ranks from the 12.11 list loaded (Gokova-M HP 3 / 24H 3 / 8K 8; CD Cherry 24H 4 / 8K 9; Honor Star 24H 2 / 8K 7).

learn.v: Belasitza took CJ-5 (not CJ-8), Alberta goes straight to CJ-7 under HP, Zheng Rong to CJ-8 under the 24-hr slot — the port re-dealt the programme again

learn.why: Same pattern as 9–10 Nov: the programme names the vessels, the berths are re-paired as they free. Belasitza (Govt 1) took the first berth she fits the moment CJ-5 opened — a deep berth was never needed for her. Alberta (sailing draft 13.3 m) was given the deep berth outright under HP(40K), so no CJ-5 stage; CJ-7 and CJ-8 go to the two 30K loaders (Alberta HP, Zheng Rong 24-hr). THREE fertiliser vessels worked together from 10 Nov 23:20 to 11 Nov 15:15 (HN Doris, Bristol, Belasitza) — the two-vessel limit of 7 Nov is evidently per stevedore (RSIPL has HN Doris and Belasitza; Bristol is JMB Port/LGS) — QUESTION FOR MIHIR.

Coded: an EXPORT vessel is not projected to a berth she would have to shift out of after loading — loaded draught as printed ("DD") or stated, else estimated from the parcel (≥ 40,000 MT ≈ 12.5 m, ≥ 25,000 ≈ 11.2 m); CJ-1–5 (10.5 m) drop out for such loaders when a deeper berth is allowed, and the shallow berth goes to the next vessel direct. Zheng Rong's 24-hr / Coastal label: taken as printed.

learn.v: CJ-16 went to Star Fighter on the 9th afternoon — Karpathos Dawn shifted out incomplete, and Safi Alfa (8K 1) was passed over

(2) An unprogrammed berth freed mid-window and the port filled it at once from the 8K queue in seniority among the vessels that FIT and are AVAILABLE: Safi Alfa (8K 1) is working at midstream, Zheng Rong / Leya (229 / 235 m) need CJ-7/8, Yasa Eagle was bound for CJ-9 — Star Fighter (8K 8 on 07.11, salt → clean berth) was the first that could take it. QUESTION FOR MIHIR: is a vessel "WORKING AT MS" (Safi Alfa, Crystal O, Yara J, Mak 1, Libra) simply not berthed at CJ until her midstream work is finished / she asks? The board treats them as ready and keeps projecting Safi Alfa into the first clean berth.

learn.v: Morning re-planned on the 0655 → 0952 sheet; Lanna Naree is back as an export; new arrivals re-rank the queue
learn.exp: 2328 sheet: Global Express OUT 08:00, Michelangelo RT OUT 07:00 + Mariblue IN, Yasa Eagle IN 06:00; night sheet: Mekele IN 23:45, SSL Gujarat OUT 02:00.
learn.act: Amended sheet: Global Express OUT 07:00, SSL Gujarat OUT 10:00, Mekele IN 08:30, Iki OUT 08:30 (programme 16:00), Caribbean 1 → OJ-3 after SC Amber's 10:00 RT OUT, RM 7 → OJ-2 after FPMC 13:00, Hari Priya → OJ-6 after Iki, Fareeda 5 OUT 16:00. Michelangelo / Mariblue done before the sheet (Mariblue made fast 07:55); Yasa Eagle not re-signalled yet. Waiting sheet: Lanna Naree re-listed EXP (20,000 rice bags + 5,000 project, N/A) · new: Heng Yuan Fa Zhan (windmill, STL/PRJ 1, ready 10 Nov 11:00), Cape Venture (HP 3, 8K 7, 292 m, 17.39 m), Uni Blossom (SGR 3, 8K 8), Ariston Bulker (GEN 19), Truong Minh Dream, African Hornbill, Chang Hang, Aboudi D (all N/A).
learn.why: The 23:28 day sheet is the HM's first plan; the morning re-issue (dispatched 06:55, 08:10, 09:52) is the one that runs — the board applies the latest dispatch and keeps the superseded times in the notes. Drake Well is now SGR 1 / 8K 5 / GEN 13.
learn.fix: Waiting list rebuilt from the 10.11 sheet (35 CJ vessels waiting, 19 expected); Liquid and Tuna tabs rebuilt from the list.

learn.v: CJ-6 to Bristol, not Belasitza — the senior Govt vessel declared readiness after lighterage
learn.exp: Board (9 Nov 10:50): Belasitza (GP 2) into CJ-6 ~9 Nov 18:00, the moment Michelangelo's sailing freed a fertiliser place; Bristol carried as not a berth taker (Mihir, 6 Nov: discharges the whole cargo at anchorage).
learn.act: Programme 10.11: CJ-06 → MV BRISTOL, GOV, "NIGHT BERTHING AFTER LIGHTERAGE. DR 11.80M."; night signal: IN 05:00 (Capt Mittal) → 41–49¾. Belasitza not programmed.
learn.why: Bristol is GP 1 by reporting (29 Oct). She lightered ~9,400 MT at the anchorage to come down to 11.8 m for the 12 m berth, declared readiness at the 9 Nov meeting and took the Govt slot and the fertiliser place that Michelangelo's sailing opened. The board's meeting preview had named exactly this flip ("a Govt vessel declares readiness — Bristol"). Rule confirmed: readiness N/A is not final; and "discharges at anchorage" can mean lighterage to the berth draught, not the whole cargo.
learn.fix: Bristol fixed at CJ-6 ~07:30 est (~15 Nov at a 10,000/day default — no norm printed). Belasitza back in the Govt queue: next chance CJ-8 after HN Doris (list ETC 11 Nov 04:37).

learn.v: The CJ-5 → CJ-7 top-up conveyor: Shen Hai Shou Xin shifted to CJ-7 behind Mariblue, Alberta straight into CJ-5
learn.exp: Board: Mariblue top-up at CJ-7 (confirmed — 50¾–57¼ after Michelangelo), then the HP queue (Yasa Eagle) at CJ-7; Shen Hai Shou Xin finishes at CJ-5 (~11 Nov 00:30); CJ-5 then to the slot order.
learn.act: Programme 10.11: Mariblue out of CJ-7 at 14:00 (12.8 m) after a 4½-hour top-up → SHEN HAI SHOU XIN "SHIFTING FROM CJ-05 TO CJ-07. PORT C." → ALBERTA (aggregates, N/A on the list, ETA 9 Nov) into CJ-05 31¼–40 as CSTL(30K), sailing draft 13.3. Yasa Eagle went to CJ-9 (GFPL, outside the pool).
learn.why: Fourth time in a week (Tan Binh 267, YHWY, Mariblue, now SHSX): a loader with a sailing draft above 10.5 m takes CJ-5 to the berth draught and is shifted to CJ-7 the moment it frees, on port convenience, and CJ-5 is backfilled at once with the next deep-draft 30K loader. The deep berth is used for the last few metres only (Mariblue 4½ h) — that is why CJ-7 turns over so fast.
learn.fix: Board: SHSX CJ-5 → CJ-7 ~16:00 est (~11 Nov 06:00), Alberta CJ-5 ~18:00 est (expect her to need the same shift). To model: a CJ-5 loader whose sailing draft exceeds the berth takes the next CJ-7/8 that frees ahead of the slot order — the board does it by hand for now (same as the top-up rule of 5 Nov).

learn.v: Michelangelo: DPR pace said complete ~17:40 on the 9th — sailing readiness 03:00, RT OUT 07:00 on the 10th; Yasa Eagle to the GFPL berth
learn.exp: Michelangelo out ~17:38 (DPR 12,486/day, 5,540 left) → Mariblue top-up ~21:00; Yasa Eagle (HP 3) CJ-7 after Mariblue.
learn.act: Programme: Michelangelo readiness 03:00 ("NIGHT SAILING"), signal RT OUT 07:00 with Mariblue IN on the round trip; Yasa Eagle IN 06:00 to 69¼–79¼ (CJ-9, GFPL) after Global Express.
learn.why: The DPR pace gives the completion, not the sailing: a night completion goes out on the morning tide with the inward vessel on the same pilot (round trip). Yasa Eagle: the list had remarked "CJ-09" — an HP coal vessel can be berthed at the GFPL berth, which the board cannot see; she leaves the DPA HP queue.
learn.fix: Michelangelo out 07:00, Mariblue in ~09:30; Yasa Eagle out of the waiting list (CJ-9 entry ~08:30 est, 20,000 GFPL norm). No rule change beyond: pace → completion, sailing follows the pilot plan.

learn.v: ANSWERED (Mihir, 11 Nov 20:08): a slot's berth goes to the SENIOR vessel if that berth suits her; if no suitable berth is available for the senior, the berth goes to the NEXT senior that fits. The slot is never held for a berth that frees later. (CJ-5 itself goes to the Govt priority first.) [20 Nov 16:50, Mihir: in the 6.5K / 8K line seniority comes first — a junior does not take the place past her seniors; see that entry.]
learn.exp: Board until now: the slot went to the first vessel of the group that could use the first berth to free — so Drake Well (8K 10, logs) would have taken CJ-5 after Shen Hai Shou Xin (~11 Nov 02:30) because Safi Alfa (8K 1, bags) cannot use CJ-5.
learn.act: Not tested yet — the 10 Nov meeting will show it. In the same window Karpathos Dawn (CJ-16, ~07:00) and Ege-M (CJ-15A, ~04:30) also free, both berths Safi Alfa can use.
learn.why: Seniority is applied berth by berth, not window by window: when CJ-5 frees tonight and the senior 8K vessel cannot use it, the junior who fits takes it under the 8K slot — the senior keeps her rank for the next berth that suits her. Simpler than the board's 9 Nov hold, and it matches how the port actually works a freeing berth.
learn.fix: Window-seniority hold switched OFF (WINDOW_HOLD = false). Each freeing berth now goes through the slot order and, within the slot, to the most senior vessel that fits that berth — a senior who does not fit is passed over for that berth only.

learn.v: Dip days on the DPR: Karpathos Dawn 2,226 · Nord Newport 1,085 · Theometor 652 MT in 24 h — what pace should the projection use?
learn.exp: Rule of 3 Nov (Mihir): balance ÷ yesterday's rate gives the real finish. Taken literally: Karpathos Dawn ~13 Nov 12:40, Nord Newport ~22 Nov, Theometor ~23 Dec.
learn.act: Those three worked at a quarter of their own pace yesterday (Sunday 8 Nov — labour / cargo?); the day before they did 5,398 / 4,156 / 3,533.
learn.why: One slow day pushed three ETCs by 1–45 days — the literal rule breaks on a dip. Board rule from today: when the 24-h figure is below HALF the vessel's own average since berthing, the average pace is used instead (Karpathos ~11 Nov 07:00, Nord Newport ~14 Nov 20:00 — her average includes the slow CJ-16 days — Theometor ~21 Nov). Mihir to confirm, or say "kal ka rate hi lo" — or whether the port re-prints the ETC on the 09.11 list anyway.
learn.fix: ANSWERED — Mihir (11 Nov 12:10): the DPR shows the last 24 h only, it can be less or more; the ETC must be calculated on BOTH bases — the DPR balance at that rate AND the permissible time per the berthing list. Board rule from today: two ETCs per vessel; the berth is taken as free at the EARLIER (a fast vessel frees it early — Star Fighter tonight, Bao He Ling 12 Nov, Enishi 16 Nov); a DPR pace running past the permissible time does not move the berth but flags OVERRUN (Nord Newport, Theometor, Bomustafao O); a vessel past her permissible time is OVERSTAYING and may be shifted out (Haj Abdullah T; Karpathos Dawn was). The 9 Nov dip-day averaging is withdrawn.

learn.v: Bao He Ling into CJ-15 (not CJ-4) and Enishi into CJ-4 (not CJ-15) — the programme's berths swapped overnight
learn.exp: Programme 09.11 / board: Bao He Ling (STEEL) → CJ-4 22¼–30½ after Mariblue's shift out (~22:00); Enishi (SAAGAR 2) → CJ-15 after African Quail (readiness 04:00), ~06:30.
learn.act: Mariblue's shift out of CJ-4 was postponed ("delay in cargo operation" — she had 27,174 MT loaded by 0700 and kept going); African Quail let go at 00:00; the port put Bao He Ling into CJ-15 at 00:54 (DPR), and the day signal sends Enishi to 22½–30½ (CJ-4) this afternoon once Mariblue has gone out.
learn.why: The programme fixes WHICH vessels berth in the window, not which berth each gets: when one berth is delayed and another frees, the port re-pairs the programmed vessels to the berths they fit (project cargo at a clean berth, timber at CJ-4 — both allowed). Same logic as the Peacock / Enishi swap the night before.
learn.fix: Board re-paired: Bao He Ling CJ-15 00:54 (~11 Nov 02:00 est, DPR 10,184 MT), Enishi CJ-4 ~17:30 est (~16 Nov 22:30). No rule change — the projection already berths a programmed vessel on any berth she fits.

learn.v: Programme readiness vs actual sailing (window 8 Nov 18:00 → 9 Nov 18:00)
learn.exp: Readiness as programmed: Lakmos 20:00 · Bow Caroline 21:00 · Western Bergenia 23:00 · JKT Miracle 04:00 · Lanna Naree 03:30 · African Quail 04:00 · Mettle Star 17:45 · Sky Dream 09:45.
learn.act: Let go: Lakmos 20:40 · Bow Caroline 21:20 · Western Bergenia 22:00 · JKT Miracle 23:55 · Lanna Naree 08:00 (completed 06:45) · African Quail 00:00 (completed 20:00) · Mettle Star 13:30 (completed 04:30) · Sky Dream 09:45.
learn.why: Readiness is the agent's declaration: the DPR completion decides — three vessels went 4 h early (Quail, JKT Miracle, Mettle Star) and one 4½ h late (Lanna Naree, cargo ran on). Within ±1 h for the chemical tankers.
learn.fix: No change: the board keeps the programme time until a signal / DPR gives the actual; the DPR pace is shown beside it (Quail's 21:28 completion estimate was 1½ h out).

learn.v: Mariblue shifts out to OTB (port convenience) — a TOP-UP vessel waiting for a deep berth; CJ-4 to Bao He Ling (STEEL)
learn.exp: Board: Mariblue works CJ-4 as HP(40K) to ~9 Nov 23:00 (60,000 MT at 40,000/day); Bao He Ling (STL 1) ~10 Nov at CJ-13/16.
learn.act: Programme 09.11 (TF/SH/2102): CJ-04 — Mariblue "SHIFTING FROM CJ-04 TO OTB. PORT C." (readiness blank, draft 10.5) → Bao He Ling 22¼–30½ STEEL. She berthed at ~09:00 today (day signal, IN o/c after JSW Mihirgad).
learn.why: The board cannot see why from the sheets: either her cargo is not at the berth yet / she is not ready to load (so the port uses the berth for the Steel-slot vessel and keeps her first for the next one — the YHWY-type rule), or the 40K commitment was not being met. "PORT C." means the shift is on port account, so it is the port's own convenience, not a penalty.
learn.fix: ANSWERED — Mihir (9 Nov 00:04): Mariblue shifts to OTB on the 9th EVENING because deep-draft berths are not available — she loads at CJ-4 to the berth draught and needs a deep berth to top up to 13.0 m (the YHWY pattern). 9 Nov day signal: the 10:00 shift was postponed (cargo delay), RT shift o/c this afternoon; DPR 09.11: 27,174 MT loaded by 0700. Board: top-up at CJ-7 after Michelangelo (DPR pace: tonight). Bao He Ling went to CJ-15 instead (see above).

learn.v: Ege-M back in the programme — CJ-15A after Mettle Star (9 Nov 17:45), 24HRS(30K)
learn.exp: Board (Mihir, 7 Nov 15:40): Ege-M not ready (technical), out of the queue.
learn.act: Programme 09.11: CJ-15A → Ege-M 161½–172¼, 24HRS(30K), "30000 MTPD", after Mettle Star's 17:45 readiness tomorrow.
learn.why: Her technical issue must be cleared (or expected to be by tomorrow evening); the port gives her the 24-hrs slot with the 30k/25k fallback as it did on 6 Nov — seniority intact.
learn.fix: Board: Ege-M fixed at CJ-15A ~20:00 est on 9 Nov; removed from the not-ready list.

learn.v: Peacock and Enishi swapped against the board: Enishi → CJ-13 after Lakmos, Peacock → CJ-15 after Quail
learn.exp: Board: African Peacock (SGR 1) → CJ-13 after Lakmos (18:00), Enshi (SGR 2) → CJ-15 after African Quail.
learn.act: Programme 09.11: CJ-13 → ENISHI 112½–124 SGR after Lakmos (readiness 20:00); CJ-15 → AFRICAN PEACOCK 146½–158 SGR after African Quail (readiness 9 Nov 04:00). Same two vessels, same night (team ETB 9 Nov for both).
learn.why: The senior SAAGAR vessel is matched to the SAAGAR berth that frees, not to the first berth that frees: Peacock (SGR 1) replaces Quail at the logs berth CJ-15; Enishi (SGR 2) takes the other. The port also puts the readiness times later than the DPR pace (Lakmos 20:00, Quail 04:00, Lanna Naree 03:30) — agents' declared figures.
learn.fix: Overtaken the same evening: the night sheet (disp 1540) struck "Enishi" and sent AFRICAN PEACOCK into CJ-13 after Lakmos — the board's original reading — so Enishi takes CJ-15 after Quail. Rule that survives: the senior SAAGAR vessel takes the first SAAGAR berth that frees.

learn.v: Lanna Naree warped at CJ-5 instead of the programmed shift to CJ-13 — SHSX waits for her completion
learn.exp: Programme 08.11 / board: Lanna Naree shifted CJ-5 → CJ-13 (112½–124) after Lakmos (17:30) on Genesis's account, Shen Hai Shou Xin into CJ-5 31½–39¾ (Coastal 30K) ~22:00.
learn.act: Day signal 8 Nov (disp 0535): Lanna Naree WARP 08:30 (Capt Sachin) 30–38 → 31½–39½ — 1½ panels east, staying at CJ-5; Mariblue IN o/c → 22¼–30½ (1 panel clear of her). No CJ-13 shift, no SHSX movement on the sheet.
learn.why: With the DPR of 8 Nov in hand the port could see she finishes tonight (board's DPR pace: ~21:20), so a shift to CJ-13 was not worth the move; a warp makes the clearance for Mariblue. SHSX keeps her programme berth (the same panels) but after Lanna Naree completes — the 8 Nov meeting will say.
learn.fix: Board: Lanna Naree stays at CJ-5 (31½–39½) to ~21:20; SHSX fixed after her, ~00:30 est, until signalled; CJ-13 after Lakmos (17:30) is free for the next vessel in order.

learn.v: CJ-6 left vacant — Belasitza (fertiliser, Govt priority 2) not in the programme for 08.11: only 2 fertiliser vessels work at a time
learn.exp: Board: Belasitza (ammonium sulphate bulk, 28,500 MT, 186 m, 10.5 m) into CJ-6 as the next fertiliser vessel — CJ-6 free since Levante Spirit sailed 08:00, hopper / truck discharge, "fertiliser vessels normally" (Mihir, 6 Nov).
learn.act: Programme 08.11 (TF/SH/2102): no CJ-6 movement at all — the berth stays vacant from 7 Nov 08:00 through 8 Nov 18:00 while Belasitza waits (GP 2, GEN 20).
learn.why: Either her receiver will not take hopper-to-truck discharge at CJ-6 (wants CJ-7/8 with the shore crane / stacking), or she is not actually ready (readiness 3 Nov 15:30 printed), or CJ-6 is being kept for something the board cannot see. The board cannot tell which from the sheets.
learn.fix: ANSWERED — Mihir (7 Nov 15:40): only TWO fertiliser vessels can work at a time, as per the stevedores' arrangements; Michelangelo (NPK, CJ-7) and HN Doris (urea, CJ-8) are the two, so Belasitza waits for one of them to complete (Michelangelo ~10 Nov). Coded as a hard cap (FERT_MAX = 2) in the berth check — the board now puts Belasitza into CJ-6 only after Michelangelo.

learn.v: Ege-M still not ready (technical) — Shen Hai Shou Xin, next in the 30k/25k pool that fits CJ-5, took the Coastal(30K) berth
learn.exp: Board (after the 15:02 correction): Ege-M, senior 30k/25k vessel (27 Oct), into CJ-13 after Lakmos as the Coastal fallback from 8 Nov 18:00.
learn.act: Programme 08.11: CJ-05 → Shen Hai Shou Xin (reported 28 Oct) CSTL(30K) after Lanna Naree is shifted out to CJ-13 on Genesis's account; Ege-M nowhere on the sheet, readiness unchanged on the revised list (27 Oct 23:59).
learn.why: Consistent with her technical issue of 6 Nov night (Mihir, 11:37): a vessel that cannot move is passed over without losing seniority. Zheng Rong (229 m) and Leya (235 m), senior to SHSX, do not fit CJ-5; SHSX (190 m, iron ore under 30k/25k — Mihir's CJ-5 rule) does, and the port moved the logs vessel out for her at the requesting agent's cost (the "2nd shift on agent account" practice).
learn.fix: ANSWERED — Mihir (7 Nov 15:40): Ege-M is still not ready. Board now carries her as not ready (readiness blank) with her seniority intact; she re-enters the queue the moment she is declared fit.

learn.v: Rule corrected: HP participation is per berth — Mariblue (HP 6, "withdrawn" on the board) takes CJ-4 as HP(40K); aggregates ARE berthed at CJ-1–4
learn.exp: Board: Mariblue listed in NOHP (no HP taker) and aggregates barred from the bag berths CJ-1–4 (board's own reading of 6 Nov) — she was projected ~18 Nov at CJ-5 as 30k/25k.
learn.act: Programme 08.11: CJ-04 after JSW Mihirgad → Mariblue 22¼–30½, HP(40K), sailing draft 13.0.
learn.why: Mihir's 6 Nov statement was "no vessel is ready to participate in HP for CJ 13 to 16" — a clean-berth statement, not a withdrawal by the vessel. Mariblue (aggregates, dirty) never wanted CJ-13–16; for CJ-4 she commits 40,000. And the port has no objection to aggregates at CJ-4.
learn.fix: NOHP now holds only Orion (withdrew) and Star Fighter (salt — clean berths only, where nobody takes HP); the CJ-1–4 bar keeps coal / petcoke / ore but lets aggregates and limestone through.

learn.v: Rule adopted: a vacant HP / Bitumen slot passes the berth down to General beyond the three General slots — the programme's "C/F" (cross-fill)
learn.exp: Board: General capped at 3 (Nord Newport, Theometor, Haj Abdullah T) — Bomustafao O (GEN 1) not before ~10 Nov; Haj Abdullah T at CJ-2 9½–13¼.
learn.act: Programme 08.11: CJ-02 → Bomustafao O 9–16 GEN "NIGHT BERTHING. C/F."; CJ-03 → Haj Abdullah T 17–21¼ GEN "NIGHT BERTHING. C/F." — two General vessels berthed tonight with three General vessels already alongside, while one HP slot (after Mariblue) and the Bitumen slot are vacant.
learn.why: Mihir (2 Nov): a vacant HP slot sends the berth down the order, lastly to General; regulation: Bitumen → the most senior General vessel. The port marks such berthings C/F.
learn.fix: Coded: when nothing up the order can use a freed berth and an HP / Bitumen slot is vacant, the senior ready General vessel takes it against that slot (it then counts in that slot, not against General). Haj Abdullah T moved to CJ-3 17–21¼, Bomustafao O fixed at CJ-2 9–16, both for tonight after the Karpathos Dawn shift.

learn.v: Lakmos: programme sailing 8 Nov 17:30 against a list ETC of 08:59 and a DPR pace of 06:30
learn.exp: Board: Lakmos sails 8 Nov 08:59 (list ETC; the DPR pace agreed within 2½ h).
learn.act: Programme 08.11: outward readiness 17:30 — the agent declared a later completion / sailing (2,704 MT of pipes left at 0700, 2/2/2 gangs).
learn.why: Break-bulk steel pipes: the last bundles, lashing release and the pilot slot make the programme time, not the tonnage pace. The programme supersedes the list ETC (standing rule).
learn.fix: Board uses 17:30; Lanna Naree's shift and SHSX's berthing hang on it.

learn.v: CJ-5 and CJ-15 after Lanna Naree / African Quail (8 Nov night): SAAGAR next, not 30k/25k — board rule corrected
learn.exp: Board: when the two SAAGAR logs vessels sail (~8 Nov 21:20 / 21:30, DPR pace) the freed berths go to the vacant HP slots' 30k/25k fallback first — Shen Hai Shou Xin → CJ-5, Star Fighter → CJ-15 (~8 Nov 23:30) — and African Peacock / Enshi (SGR 1 / 2) follow on 10 Nov at CJ-16 / CJ-15A. This is the rule read from 6–7 Nov: with both SAAGAR slots full, CJ-15A went to Ege-M (6 Nov, "senior against 24-hrs 30k/25k") and then to Mettle Star ("24HRS(30K)") ahead of Safi Alfa (8K 1).
learn.act: Timber desk (07.11 1200, updated after today's meeting): African Peacock ETB 9 Nov and Enishi ETB 9 Nov — i.e. straight into the berths the two SAAGAR vessels vacate. The 6–7 Nov cases never tested 30k/25k against a waiting SAAGAR vessel, because both SAAGAR slots were occupied then.
learn.why: Two readings of the regulation: (a) a vacant HP berth is filled by the senior 30k/25k vessel (what the port did on 6 and 7 Nov) — then SAAGAR waits; (b) a vacant HP slot passes the berth down the order — SAAGAR next — and 30k/25k vessels only come in through the Govt / Coastal / 24-hr fallbacks. The board runs (a). Under (b) Peacock and Enshi berth 9 Nov morning (CJ-15 / CJ-5), SHSX and Star Fighter wait, and Drake Well's SAAGAR turn also moves up.
learn.fix: RESOLVED by the regulation text Mihir re-sent (7 Nov 15:02): "High Productivity 2 slots" has NO fallback — only Govt, Coastal (→ SAAGAR project → 30k/25k), 24-hrs (→ 30k/25k) and Bitumen (→ General) have one. So a vacant HP slot passes the berth down the order and SAAGAR is next: Peacock / Enshi take the berths the two SAAGAR vessels free (team ETB 9 Nov). The 6–7 Nov cases are the 24-hrs fallback, not an HP fallback: Orion (24-hrs) had a firm sailing inside the window, so her slot was available for the window and went to the senior 30k/25k vessel (Ege-M, then Mettle Star — "24HRS(30K)" on the list) ahead of 8K. Board corrected: HP fb removed; a slot whose vessel sails inside the meeting window counts as available for that window (firm sailings only).

learn.v: JSW Mihirgad sent to CJ-4 (22¼–27¼) after Aya, not to 14¼–19¾ as the 0700 list printed
learn.exp: List 07.11 / board: JSW Mihirgad (coastal) at CJ-3 14¼–19¾ tonight, after the Karpathos Dawn shift frees CJ-2/3.
learn.act: 1241 → 1330 sheet: Aya OUT 16:00 (Capt Sud), JSW Mihirgad IN o/c with the same pilot → 22¼–27¼ (first written 18¾–24¼, amended) — straight into Aya's CJ-4 on the afternoon round trip.
learn.why: The berth that frees first and fits gets the vessel: Aya's 21¼–29 run (with 1-panel clearance to Lanna Naree at 30) takes a 122 m vessel at once, while 14¼–19¾ needed Karpathos Dawn gone first (evening). The 0700 list's printed panels for a B'TODAY vessel are the meeting's intention, not a fixed allotment — the HM re-plans on the day.
learn.fix: Board moved her to CJ-4 22¼–27¼ ~18:30 est. CJ-2/3 after the Karpathos shift: Haj Abdullah T at 9½–13¼ and a run 14¼–21¼ (~160 m less clearance) for one more short vessel.

learn.v: Rule adopted: between two vessels a minimum of 1 panel space is mandatory (Mihir)
learn.exp: Board treated any free run as usable to its full length (LOA up to ~10 % over the measured run).
learn.act: Mihir (7 Nov 14:45): "between 2 vessels minimum 1 panel space mandatory".
learn.why: Matches every allotment on the sheets: Mettle Star 159–171½ beside African Quail 146½–158 (1 panel), Haj Abdullah T 9½–13¼ beside Nord Newport 0–8 (1½), Michelangelo 49–57¼ beside HN Doris 58¼ (1).
learn.fix: Coded: a free run loses 1 panel at each end that touches a vessel (not at a quay end) before the LOA check — in the projection's fit test at every berth, in the free-runs card (shown as "− x m clearance") and in the projected hull positions.

learn.v: Ege-M missed her berthing (technical issue — seniority kept) — Mettle Star took CJ-15A on the morning flood, in the 24-hrs slot
learn.exp: Board (6 Nov 22:15): Ege-M berths 161–171¾ ~23:30 after Unity Melody (night signal IN 21:30, Capt Goel); Mettle Star next day at CJ-16 ~18:00 as the 30k/25k quote in the Coastal slot.
learn.act: 0530 amendment: Ege-M's IN struck — "IN idle due vessel not reach OTB at requested time". 0800 sheet: Mettle Star IN o/c on the flood → 159–171½ (Capt Pankaj after Levante Spirit), African Quail warped 3¼ panels west for her. List 07.11 puts Mettle Star under the "24 HRS" priority, remark 24HRS(30K) B'TODAY; Ege-M is back on the waiting list — 8K 7, GEN 13, readiness unchanged (27 Oct 23:59), no B'TODAY.
learn.why: A vessel that is not at OTB when the pilot is sent loses that movement; the free berth then goes to the next ready 30k/25k vessel by reporting (Mettle Star, 1 Nov 06:42) — the same fallback order the board uses, only the slot label differs (24-hrs fallback, since the Coastal slot now has a real taker in JSW Mihirgad). What the board cannot tell from the sheets: whether Ege-M keeps her seniority for the next programme or is penalised for the idle call.
learn.fix: ANSWERED — Mihir (7 Nov 11:37): Ege-M had a TECHNICAL issue, so her seniority stays the same. Rule: if an agent cancels a movement for anything other than a technical issue, the vessel may be penalised — 3 days no berthing; a technical cancellation keeps seniority. Board: Ege-M stays in the queue with her 27 Oct seniority (as it already did); a non-technical idle call would be entered as a 3-day hold (rdy = idle time + 72 h) when the port says so.

learn.v: Karpathos Dawn shifted CJ-2 → CJ-16 on port account to seat two short vessels at CJ-2/3
learn.exp: Board: Haj Abdullah T into CJ-3 after Aya (run 17¾–30 from ~noon); Karpathos Dawn stays at CJ-2 to her ETC.
learn.act: List 07.11: Karpathos Dawn printed at berth 16, 174¼–188, remark "W1, W2, S1 FROM CJ-02 TO 174¼–188" (Orion's berth after her 17:46 sailing); Haj Abdullah T GENERAL B'TODAY at CJ-2 9½–13¼; JSW Mihirgad (coastal, bentonite 7,500, 122 m, reported 5 Nov 17:47) COASTAL B'TODAY at CJ-3 14¼–19¾.
learn.why: The port shifts one long vessel on port account to a berth that frees anyway (Orion out), and packs two short ready vessels — the Coastal-slot taker and the two-crane bagged vessel — into the CJ-2/3 run. Consistent with Mihir's rule (port shifts 1 vessel on port a/c to allot a berth) and with "berthing follows the printed slot sequence". CJ-4 (Aya out) stays free for the next bagged vessel.
learn.fix: No rule change; the board carries the three movements as fixed entries with estimated times until the evening signal. Note for the model: when a clean berth frees and CJ-1–4 have two short ready vessels, expect a port-account shift of the long bagged vessel.

learn.v: Levante Spirit (CJ-6) — DPR 06.11 pace said finished 6 Nov afternoon; she actually completed 7 Nov 04:15 and sailed 08:00
learn.exp: Board: completion ~7 Nov 09:00 est (DPR 05.11 pace 11,587/day on 24,052 MT); the 6 Nov night sheet (amended 2150) and the 7 Nov day sheet (first version) carry no OUT for her.
learn.act: DPR 06.11 (0700 6 Nov): at CJ-6 she did 15,688 MT between re-commencement 13:05 and 0700 — ≈ 21,000/day with 12 hooks — leaving 8,364 MT, i.e. ~6 h of work → complete by ~13:00–16:00 on 6 Nov. Yet no sailing on either sheet up to the 2150 amendment.
learn.why: Either she completed and the sailing is on a later signal we have not seen (night 6 Nov, second version), or work slowed / stopped (hatch, documents, draught survey) — cannot tell from the sheets. Until confirmed the board keeps her at CJ-6 to ~7 Nov 09:00 est, so CJ-6 (the no-taker berth) shows as busy one more morning.
learn.fix: ANSWERED by DPR 07.11 and the 7 Nov day sheet: COMPLETED 04:15 on 7 Nov, OUT 08:00 (Capt Pankaj). The last 8,364 MT took 21 h with 3/3/2 gangs and 8 hooks — half the previous day's pace (trimming / last hatch / fewer gangs). Lesson folded in: a DPR pace over-predicts the tail of a bulk discharge; the board's own ~09:00 estimate was right in effect. No rule change.

learn.v: Andreas Petrakis over-ran — Govt berthing moved to the morning flood
learn.exp: Board / night sheet 1648: Andreas Petrakis OUT 00:19 (7 Nov) → Michelangelo IN o/c on the night flood; Caribbean 1 shifts out of OJ-7 01:22.

learn.v: 8K slot: Safi Alfa (8K 1) takes CJ-2 · the slot sequence governs · "Y" is not a rank
learn.exp: Board (21:00): CJ-2 after Karpathos Dawn (list ETC 8 Nov 11:18) → Mariblue (aggregates, ETA sheet) as the 24-hr slot's 30k/25k quote vessel, Safi Alfa (8K 1) sent to 15A; before that Drake Well ("8K Y") had been given CJ-14 on 8 Nov.
learn.act: Mihir (6 Nov 20:23 / 20:39 / 21:46): Drake Well cannot berth on 8 Nov — about 9 vessels are senior in 8K/6.5K; the 8K senior is Safi Alfa — CJ-2 direct, or CJ-14 after shifting Theometor; and berthing follows the priority sequence exactly as the slot-wise card lists it.
learn.why: (1) A "Y" flag on the ETA sheet (rank 98/99) is not a place in the queue. (2) The slot sequence stands, fallbacks inline — the 24-hr slot's 30k/25k turn comes before 8K — but a fallback vessel only counts if she can use the freed berth: the 30k/25k vessels in seniority order are pellets / coal / salt (not CJ-2), and Mariblue's aggregates do not go to a bag berth (board's reading), so the 24-hr turn passes and CJ-2 goes to the 8K senior.
learn.fix: Adopted in code: 98/99 = willing, not ranked; pick order = the slot sequence as printed (an earlier "ranked before fallback" patch was withdrawn at 21:46); dirty bulk (coal, pellets, aggregates, bauxite, clinker, limestone, manganese, chrome) is not berthed at CJ-1–4; ball clay is allowed at CJ-13–16 but agents normally take CJ-5–8 (Mihir, 22:04) — the board uses 13–16 for clay only when the list remark asks (Ege-M). Safi Alfa projects CJ-2 ~8 Nov 13:18; Drake Well is General by reporting until the 06.11 list ranks her.

learn.v: CJ-15A went to Ege-M (30k/25k quote, not on the HP list) — the board had Mettle Star
learn.exp: Board: Coastal slot vacant → 30k/25k (Sr No 7) fallback → Mettle Star (HP 5, salt 79,080, reported 1 Nov; HP withdrawn) at 15A ~7 Nov 00:00 after Unity Melody.
learn.act: Night signal 6 Nov (disp 1648): Ege-M IN 21:30 (Capt Goel) → 161–171¾; Unity Melody OUT 22:45. Ege-M on the 05.11 list: ball clay 43,000 EXP, 190 m, "CJ13 TO 16, 2 HMC · 30K/25K/8K/10K Sr No 7", reported 27 Oct 23:59 — 8K 7 / GEN 14, NOT on the HP list. Mettle Star not programmed. Mihir (6 Nov): "HP mein CJ-1 to 9 mein berth available nahi".
learn.why: Mihir (6 Nov 20:14): "No vessel is ready to participate in Higher Productivity for CJ-13 to CJ-16. Hence Ege-M is the senior vessel in the 24-hrs 30k/25k." With no HP participant the HP berth goes to the 24-hrs 30k/25k quote vessels by reporting seniority — across every vessel that quoted it, HP-listed or not — so Ege-M (27 Oct) is ahead of Shen Hai Shou Xin (28 Oct) and Mettle Star (1 Nov). The board had used the HP list rank, which Ege-M is not on.
learn.fix: Adopted: (1) the HP slot falls back to the senior 24-hrs 30k/25k quote vessel before going down the order; (2) the 30k/25k pool takes every vessel whose list remark quotes 30K/25K, by reporting time; (3) Star Fighter and Mariblue join Mettle Star as "not participating in HP" (30k/25k quote vessels only) until a list says otherwise.

learn.v: CJ-6 after Levante Spirit — port: no taker
learn.exp: Board: Levante Spirit out 7 Nov 09:00 → Bristol (GOV 2, TSP + DAP) at CJ-6; failing her, the Govt slot's 30k/25k fallback → Shen Hai Shou Xin (pellets, HP 4) at 18:00.
learn.act: Mihir (6 Nov 19:34): "CJ-6 pe koi taker nahi hai. HP mein CJ-1 to 9 mein berth available nahi hai. MV Bristol will discharge the entire cargo at anchorage."
learn.why: Mihir (6 Nov 20:14): "CJ-6 is a damaged berth, so no cargo can be dumped on the berth — load / unload direct by truck at the vessel, or unload by hopper onto trucks. That is why normally only fertiliser vessels berth at CJ-6; another cargo is discharged there only with a special hopper arrangement." Pellets (stockpile → HMC) and General cargo that needs the quay apron therefore cannot use it; Bristol, the one fertiliser vessel, discharges at anchorage — so no taker.
learn.fix: Adopted in code: CJ-6 is open only to fertiliser vessels (urea / MOP / NPK / DAP / TSP / phosphate / potash / sulphate); any other cargo there would be a special arrangement the board does not assume. Bristol carried as not a berth taker.

learn.v: CJ-7 to the Govt vessel ahead of HP · two gearless fertiliser vessels together
learn.exp: Board for the 7 Nov window: Andreas Petrakis out ~00:00 → Zheng Rong (HP 1) at CJ-7; Michelangelo (GOV 1, 229 m gearless, 13.45 m) held back by the board's one-gearless-fertiliser-vessel-at-a-time rule while HN Doris works at CJ-8.
learn.act: Night signal 6 Nov (disp 1648): Andreas OUT 00:19 → Michelangelo IN o/c on the flood → 49–57¼ (NPK 36,500, HM permission for 13.45 m). Mihir (6 Nov): "2 gearless at a time is always the stevedore's choice — here the stevedore is ready to work 2 gearless vessels."
learn.why: Govt priority outranks HP for the one deep crane berth that frees: Michelangelo takes CJ-7, HN Doris keeps CJ-8, so the HP slot has no berth in CJ-1–9 and Zheng Rong waits. The second gearless vessel on the shore crane is not a port limit — it is the stevedore's call, and he agreed.
learn.fix: Adopted: the one-gearless-at-a-time block is removed (now a flip note: "stevedore must agree"); Michelangelo is on the board from the signal — norm / ETC with the 06.11 list.

learn.v: HM signals 5 Nov vs the board's morning estimates — the whole chain ran on the morning tide
learn.exp: Board (0700 list + programme readiness): Quail warp ~07:00; Emmanouil already sailed ~04:30 (missing from the list); Unity Melody in ~09:00; Lanna Naree in ~08:00 (gang sheet); Rome Trader out 14:00 (readiness); Levante Spirit CJ-1 → CJ-6 ~15:00; Nord Newport CJ-16 → CJ-1 ~17:00; Orion in ~19:30; Vishva Preeti out ~11:00; HN Doris in ~13:00; KSL Ruiyang out 17:50; Bateleur in ~20:00.
learn.act: Day sheet (disp 0825 → 1253): Quail SHIFT 08:45 → 149¾–159¾ (Deepak); Emmanouil OUT 09:15; Godavari OUT 09:15; Tan Binh OUT 10:00 → Andreas Petrakis IN on the flood (Mittal), Lanna Naree IN o/c (Madaan); Aya SHIFT 10:00 → 21¼–29; Rome ("Rona") Trader OUT 10:30 (Goel); Levante Spirit SHIFT 10:45 → 39–47¾; Nord Newport SHIFT 11:45 → 8–N; Orion IN 12:30 (Mittal); Vishva Preeti RT OUT 14:30 (Pankaj — the 09:00 sailing struck "delay in cargo operation") → HN Doris IN; Farsana OUT 16:00 → Saehan Kostar IN (OJ-2). Night sheet (disp 1505 → 2110): Atlantic Guard IN 17:30 OJ-6 (flood); Fareeda 5 RT SHIFT 20:00 OJ-4 → OTB → Malbec Heritage IN; SY Forward IN 20:30 OJ-5 (flood) → KSL Ruiyang OUT o/c → African Bateleur IN o/c (Rawat); Gautham B Star II OUT 23:50 (Omesh); SC Larimar RT OUT 02:30 OJ-3 → Bow Neptune IN.
learn.why: Rome Trader had completed at 06:30 (DPR), so the HM did not wait for the programme's 14:00 readiness: sailing 10:30, and the two port-convenience shifts and Orion's berthing followed on the same morning flood (10:45 / 11:45 / 12:30) — 4 to 7 h before the board's figures. The other way round for the two completions the board took from the list: Emmanouil was still alongside at 0700 although the 0700 list no longer printed her (DPR: completed, let go pending), and Vishva Preeti's last 781 MT ran past 09:00, so Unity Melody and HN Doris came later than the board said.
learn.fix: Two reading rules adopted: (1) DPR "COMPLETED, let go pending" at 0700 → expect the sailing on the next pilot / tide slot (~3–4 h after 0700), not at the programme readiness; (2) a vessel missing from the 0700 berth table but "let go pending" on the DPR is still alongside — her sailing time comes from the day sheet. Nothing new to ask Mihir.

learn.v: "RT" on the signal = the pilot's round trip
learn.exp: Board read RT as a flag on the sailing only and estimated each o/c berthing separately.
learn.act: Every RT OUT / RT SHIFT is followed on the same sheet by an "o/c IN" under the same pilot: Fareeda 5 → Malbec Heritage, Vishva Preeti → HN Doris, SC Larimar → Bow Neptune, Outrivaling 3 → Gautham B Star II, Shanaya → Caribbean 1, Manitoba → SC Larimar. The inward vessel is already waiting at OTB.
learn.why: The pilot takes the outgoing vessel to OTB and brings the waiting one in on the same trip, so made fast ≈ let-go + the OTB–berth transit: Ocean Pioneer let go 01:00 → Fareeda 5 made fast 04:00; Dank Silver 11:30 → Lujain 14:42; Alasia 10:32 → Nord Newport 13:30.
learn.fix: Board estimates an o/c IN after an RT OUT at let-go + 3 h (made fast) — used tonight for Lanna Naree, HN Doris, African Bateleur, Malbec Heritage, Bow Neptune.

learn.v: Programme for 06.11: no cargo-jetty movement at all · CJ-3 vacant since 1 Nov
learn.exp: Board (next window): Haj Abdullah T (GEN 1, 2 shore cranes) into vacant CJ-3 at 5 Nov 18:00; otherwise berths free as vessels finish.
learn.act: Programme for 06.11 has NO DPA cargo-jetty line (only TSS Amber at KICT-11, oil jetties, Tuna): all 13 berths keep their vessels till 6 Nov 18:00. CJ-3 stays vacant (DPR: vacant since Horizon Chaser sailed 1 Nov). Haj Abdullah T remains "DOC UNDER PROCESS"; Libra declared readiness 5 Nov 11:00 with 3,000 MT docs pending. Team (5 Nov 21:53): "Haj Abdullah is ready today but at Berth No 3 space is not available."
learn.why: Two reasons, one after the other. Till today her documents were under process — not a taker. Today she is ready, but CJ-3 no longer has the room: Aya was warped at 10:00 from 23½–30¾ to 21¼–29 to make 30–38 for Lanna Naree (SAAGAR), and Karpathos Dawn lies to 17¾ at CJ-2 — the free run inside CJ-3 is 17¾–21¼, about 80 m, too short for a 98 m vessel (the board's reading of "space not available"; the team did not name Aya). The run opens when Aya finishes (DPR pace: ~7 Nov 02:00; list ETC is a typo) or Karpathos Dawn sails (list ETC 8 Nov 11:18, DPR pace ~10 Nov).
learn.fix: Adopted: (1) "DOC UNDER PROCESS" / "docs NR" = not a taker until the list drops the remark; (2) a vacant berth is usable only if its free panel run — neighbours' positions counted — is long enough: the projection now checks the run at every berth, not only on CJ-13–16, and the free-runs card shows CJ-1 to CJ-8 as well. Haj Abdullah T now projects to CJ-3 ~7 Nov 08:00, once Aya completes (DPR pace: ~7 Nov 02:00) and the run re-opens — not 6 Nov 18:00.

learn.v: African Bateleur (not Global Express) at CJ-9 · Gautham B Star II into "14A" · Unity Melody by day
learn.exp: Programme for 05.11: Global Express into CJ-9 after KSL Ruiyang; Unity Melody after Emmanouil's 17:30 readiness; Gautham B Star II (coastal) not placed.
learn.act: List 05.11: African Bateleur B'TODAY at CJ-9 69¼–78 (GFPL berth), Global Express back on the waiting sheet (GEN 23, "CJ-09"); Gautham B Star II B'TODAY at 14A 141¼–148 (the run Outrivaling 3 left); Emmanouil completed 01:30 and sailed before 0700, Unity Melody booked on the 1st-shift gang sheet at 15A.
learn.why: CJ-9 is GFPL's: they berth by their own seniority — Bateleur reported 16:24, Global Express 22:24 (both on 4 Nov). A 93 m coastal vessel fits the 141¼–148 run exactly as the panel-run rule says. A readiness figure on the programme is the latest, not the actual, completion.
learn.fix: none — panel-run card already shows such runs; GFPL berth is data only.

learn.v: Orion → CJ-16 by shifting Nord Newport to CJ-1 on Cross Trade's account · Levante Spirit shifted again
learn.exp: Board: Orion (HP withdrawn, 30k/25k) far down — after Mettle Star / Unity Melody; Nord Newport at CJ-16 till 12 Nov; Levante Spirit at CJ-1 till 6 Nov.
learn.act: Programme for 05.11: Rome Trader out 14:00 → Levante Spirit CJ-1 → CJ-6 39–47¾ (port c.) → Nord Newport CJ-16 → CJ-1 8–N (port c., starboard, "A/C CROSSTRADE") → Orion in at CJ-16 173½–188 as 24HRS(30K). Done 5 Nov by day (sheet 0825): Rome Trader OUT 10:30, Levante Spirit SHIFT 10:45, Nord Newport SHIFT 11:45, Orion IN 12:30.
learn.why: Team (5 Nov 21:53): "Port will shift only 1 vessel to allot any vessel; when 2 shiftings are required to berth a vessel, the 2nd shifting is on the agent's account — so 1 shifting on Cross Trade's account." Not the agent's choice: the port decides the shifts and bears one port-convenience shift per berthing (Levante Spirit CJ-1 → CJ-6); the second shift needed for the same berthing (Nord Newport CJ-16 → CJ-1) is charged to the incoming vessel's agent.
learn.fix: Rule adopted: to berth one vessel the port will move up to two berthed vessels — the first on port account, the second on the incoming agent's account. So a berth can be "made" even when it takes two shifts; the board's shift option is no longer thought of as a single move.

learn.v: Andreas Petrakis (coal, 14.15 m) → CJ-7 under HP(50K) · draught limit
learn.exp: Board: at 14.15 m arrival draught she has no CJ berth (CJ-7/8 12.0 m + 1.5 m tide = 13.5 m) — treated as waiting with no berth; SGR 3 / HP 7.
learn.act: Programme for 05.11: Tan Binh 267 out 10:00 (sailing draught 13.0) → Andreas Petrakis in at CJ-7 49–57¼, HP(50K), arrival draught 14.15 m. Day sheet 5 Nov: Tan Binh OUT 10:00 (Madaan), Andreas Petrakis IN on the FLOOD (Mittal) — taken in on the tide; no lightening on any sheet.
learn.why: Team (5 Nov 21:53): "The agent obtained permission from the HM." Above the 14.0 m tidal allowance the HM can still permit a berthing on the flood / HW at CJ-6–10 on the agent's application; the channel draught at HW that day (14.85 m on 5 Nov) is the ceiling. No lightening.
learn.fix: Adopted in code: at CJ-6–10 a draught above 14.0 m no longer bars a vessel — the limit is the day's channel draught at HW, and such a pick is flagged "needs the HM's permission (agent applies)"; elsewhere the chart draught stays the limit.

learn.v: African Quail · warp to 149¾–159¾ · Lanna Naree CJ-5 · Tan Binh top-up at CJ-7
learn.exp: Board: Quail stays at 153–161¾; Lanna Naree next SAAGAR berth after Tan Binh's ETC; Tan Binh sails from CJ-5.

learn.fix: Rules already noted; the top-up rule now has two cases (YHWY, Tan Binh).

learn.v: Fortunelit at "18-21" (CJ-3) with 2 shore cranes — not on the list, not on any signal
learn.exp: Board / list 04.11: Fortunelit waiting, readiness N/A (docs not ready), working at midstream; CJ-3 vacant.
learn.act: 2nd-shift gang sheet 04.11 (14:00–22:00): "18-21 · FORTUNELIT · EXP · RICE BAGS · 1 PR · 02-SC · TSAS" — i.e. alongside CJ-3 panels 18–21 working rice bags with two shore cranes, while her sugar-bags line continues at midstream with 1 gang.
learn.why: Either she was berthed at CJ-3 after the 11:00 meeting (a General berthing from N/A — docs cleared at the meeting) and the signal is not with the board yet, or "18-21" means something else on this sheet.
learn.fix: Mihir (4 Nov 19:35): Fortunelit is NOT ready (list N/A) and works at midstream only; Crystal O likewise. So the gang sheet's "18-21" line is a midstream / other gang booking, not CJ-3 — the board's CJ-3 entry was wrong and is removed. Rule: the gang sheet's berth column is not proof of a berthing; only the list / signal is. (The same sheet's "barge of MV Crystal O" at CJ-10 is her midstream barge.)

learn.v: Gang sheet ≠ position: KSL Ruiyang (DPR: made fast 20:00), Fortunelit · Outrivaling 3 and Vishva Preeti sailings slip
learn.exp: Board read the 2nd-shift gang sheet as a position: KSL Ruiyang "at CJ-9 before 14:00", Fortunelit "at CJ-3"; Outrivaling 3 sails 22:00, Vishva Preeti 03:00 (programme).
learn.act: Day signal (final 1533): Cervia OUT 14:00, KSL Ruiyang IN o/c after her (~16:00) — the gang sheet had merely booked her for the 14:00–22:00 shift; Fortunelit is at midstream (Mihir). Night signal amended 2024: Outrivaling 3's 22:00 sailing POSTPONED ("0600" pencilled), Vishva Preeti's 03:00 sailing and HN Doris's berthing POSTPONED.
learn.why: The gang sheet is a labour / crane plan for the coming shift, written before the shift — it lists where gangs are to report, including berths a vessel is only expected at. Sailings on the programme are readiness figures; the HM postpones when cargo is not complete.
learn.fix: Rule: a gang sheet never moves a vessel on the board; only the list / signal does. Board carries Outrivaling ~06:00, Vishva Preeti ~10:00, HN Doris ~12:00 (all est).

learn.v: African Quail · SAAGAR · berthed 4 Nov at 153–161¾ — a day earlier than the board's last reading
learn.exp: Board last night: 5 Nov ~13:00 at CJ-5 (after Tan Binh 267); before that 4 Nov 20:30 at CJ-15 only if the port shifted Outrivaling 3. Team ETB: 4 Nov.
learn.act: Day signal 4 Nov (disp 0825): African Quail IN o/c → 153–161¾ (Capt Madaan) after Gas Ammon's 10:00 sailing; list 04.11: B'TODAY at "15A" under SAAGAR. Not in the programme for 04.11.
learn.why: The space was made last night and this morning: the 2200 amendment put Emmanouil at 163–173 (not 161¼–172) and the barge left 153–156¼ at 08:30 — between Outrivaling 3 (…150¾) and Emmanouil (163–) that is 12¼ panels, enough for a 180 m vessel. With Centurion Buyo gone the SAAGAR break-bulk slot was free, and Quail (SGR 1) took it. The board never looked at 150¾–163 as a berth because its slot map has CJ-15 ending at 159½ and Outrivaling 3 occupying "CJ-15" till today 14:16.
learn.fix: Model gap (noted): on CJ-13–16 a vessel can be berthed into any free run of panels ≥ its LOA, not only into a whole slot; the port moves neighbours by a panel or two to make such a run. Mihir (4 Nov 10:52): yes — go by panels. Quail's berth was FINAL at the 3 Nov meeting; it was not in the programme only because the space did not exist yet — when the space was made she berthed. And barges have NO priority: a barge gets a space only when one happens to exist and a window is there; otherwise the port takes the berthed barge out and berths the vessel. Board now: (1) a "Free quay runs · CJ-13–16" card that reads the quay panel-wise (barges ignored) and names the ready vessels that fit, in slot order; (2) rule noted that a meeting allotment can exist without a programme line ("allotted, awaiting space"). The projection itself still berths by slot — moving it to panel runs is the next code change.

learn.v: Yuan Hang Wei Ye · 24-hr · "night starboard shift" done as out-to-OTB by day + back by night (made fast CJ-7 4 Nov 06:20, list ETC 20:51)

learn.v: Emmanouil → CJ-15A · the programme chain re-planned
learn.exp: Morning board (list 03.11 0700): no shifts — Nord Newport CJ-16, Emmanouil stays CJ-1, Levante Spirit stays CJ-7; the board had Unity Melody (HP) at CJ-15A ~18:00 and African Quail at CJ-1 ~4 Nov 06:46 after Emmanouil.
learn.act: Programme for 04.11: the chain is back, around Centurion Buyo's berth instead of Alasia's — Emmanouil shifts CJ-1 → CJ-15A 161¼–172 (night, a/c Genesis), Levante Spirit CJ-7 → "CJ-02" 8½–N, Yuan Hang Wei Ye CJ-5 → CJ-7 (night starboard), Karpathos Dawn warps to 9½–18¼; Tan Binh 267 follows at CJ-5. Nord Newport CJ-16 and Lakmos CJ-13 as the list said. No HP berthing (Unity Melody not programmed). Mihir (5 Nov 22:39): "Yuan Hang Wei Ye, after achieving draft at CJ-5, was shifted to anchorage waiting for deep draft, so CJ-5 became vacant and Tan Binh 267 berthed there. As per the port's regular practice the vessel first shifted to anchorage for deep draft gets the first (deep) berth — so YHWY was allotted CJ-7 after shifting Levante Spirit to CJ-1 on port account and Emmanouil to CJ-15A on agent account. Therefore no new vessel got a berthing movement in Coastal or HP."
learn.why: The chain was not a fresh allotment — it re-berthed a vessel already in the system. A loader that has taken the 10.5 m draught at CJ-1–5 and waits at anchorage for a deep berth has first claim on the next CJ-6–8 berth that can be made free, ahead of every waiting vessel; the port makes that berth with up to two shifts — the first on port account (Levante Spirit CJ-7 → CJ-1), the second on the incoming agent's account (Emmanouil CJ-1 → CJ-15A). So the freed clean berth (15A) went to the shift, not to an HP / SAAGAR vessel, and no Coastal / HP slot was used.
learn.fix: Rule adopted: (1) a "top-up at anchorage" vessel (shifted out for deep draft) is first in line for the next deep berth (CJ-6–8), outside the group order and without using a slot; (2) the shifts that make that berth follow the 1 port-a/c + 1 agent-a/c rule; (3) when a list shows such a vessel at OTB without her return berth printed, the board books her on the first CJ-6–8 berth that frees as a fixed entry, before projecting the queue.
