learn.v: CJ-7 · Levante Spirit (Govt) after Meghna Venus
learn.exp: Board: Meghna Venus out ~16:00 → Levante Spirit, Govt, CJ-7 (draught 12.9 m with tidal benefit).
learn.act: Programme for 02.11: Meghna Venus out 13:00 (draft 12.72) → Rome Trader warps to 41–49¼ → Levante Spirit in at 50¼–57¼, GOV.
learn.why: As expected: the second Govt slot claimed by the waiting Govt vessel; tidal benefit allowed (channel 14.85 m at HW 2 Nov).
learn.fix: None — first test of the slot-claim rule and the 14 m tide rule passed. Meghna Venus finished 3 h earlier than the quote-based estimate.

learn.v: Mettle Star (HP) · Orion (24-hr Sr No 7) · Centurion Buyo shift
learn.exp: Board had CJ-4 → Mak 1 (General), CJ-14 → Orion under HP, nothing for Mettle Star (readiness N/A, HP "Y" only).
learn.act: Mihir (1 Nov 00:12): Mettle Star should berth under HP at CJ-15A after Centurion Buyo is shifted to CJ-4; Orion berths under 30k/25k against 24-hr at CJ-14.
learn.why: Mihir (1 Nov 00:26): in today's meeting Meghna Venus and Alasia hold both HP slots; Meghna Venus sails next day, so one HP slot is vacant in the window. Orion is senior but goes into the comfortable group (30k/25k against 24-hr) and Mettle Star, junior, berths under HP at 50k — "normally the senior vessel berths under the comfortable group and the junior vessel in Higher Productivity". Mettle Star (ETA 1 Nov 06:00, before the meeting) is declared at the meeting; a logs vessel is shifted to CJ-4 to make the second clean berth.
learn.fix: Coded: ETA vessels with a Y arriving before the first HW after the meeting are assumed declared; a Y without rank queues after the ranked vessels; shift is "required" when clean-berth demand (priority vessels) exceeds the clean berths freeing in the window; HP slot ordered junior-first whenever a 30k/25k fallback slot is open in the window (senior → comfortable slot), else by seniority.

learn.v: Project vessels · ball clay / feldspar berths
learn.exp: Board projected CJ-15 / CJ-14 freeing at its own estimate of when Katong WW / Feng Hai Da (project cargo) finish, and offered CJ-13 to Tan Binh 267 (ball clay / feldspar).
learn.act: Mihir: a project vessel has no discharge norm — it sails whenever it is done, so its berth cannot be programmed ahead; ball clay / feldspar can berth only at CJ-5 to CJ-8.
learn.why: Project cargo has no port norm; clay / feldspar handling is restricted to the CJ-5–8 stretch.
learn.fix: Coded: a berth held by a project vessel is kept in the meeting preview at the board's estimate but highlighted (red-orange, "PROJECT VESSEL · check sailing") — to be checked at the meeting and only then considered. Who is a project vessel: project / windmill cargo by name, or any vessel in the Steel/Project group with NO norm printed in the list (Rahma, CJ-13) — steel with a printed norm sails as per norms. Exception: a vessel berthed under 24 HRS (Feng Hai Da, CJ-14) must sail within 24 h whatever the cargo, so its berth is programmed at the next meeting — next 24-hr vessel, else a 30k/25k vessel. Clay / feldspar → CJ-5–8 only (a list remark cannot widen a commodity rule).

learn.v: Sr No 7 seniority · slot held at meeting · unprogrammed berths
learn.exp: Board gave CJ-4 to Tan Binh 267 (HP rank 2) against the Govt slot because rank-1 Yuan Hang Wei Ye (iron ore) cannot use CJ-4; gave Orion the Coastal slot after Katong WW's board-estimated sailing; berthed vessels on berths that free up tonight although the 1 Nov programme has nothing for them.
learn.act: Mihir: the 30k/25k slot goes to the most senior of the group (Yuan Hang Wei Ye) — a junior does not take it because the senior cannot use that berth. Katong WW was allotted in today's meeting against Coastal, so Coastal is engaged for the whole programme; Orion cannot take it. Nothing unprogrammed berths before the next meeting.
learn.why: Slots are decided at the meeting for the whole programme window, by seniority within the group; an estimated sailing is not a free slot.
learn.fix: Coded: (1) Sr No 7 fallback by seniority — the senior-most ready HP vessel first; if it cannot use this berth, the next 30k/25k vessel that can gets the movement (Mihir: "any vessel under 30k/25k"), the senior keeps its turn; (2) a ready vessel of a group waiting for a berth (Levante Spirit, Govt) claims the group's free slot for the window, so no 30k/25k fallback against Govt while a Govt vessel waits — if nobody is waiting in 24-hr, the 30k/25k vessel goes against 24-hr; (3) a vessel already in a programme holds its slot from now; a vessel alongside at the next meeting with only a board-estimated sailing keeps its slot till that window ends; (4) a berth freeing without a programmed inward vessel is allotted only at the next 11:00 meeting (+2 h); (5) General vessels only after every priority group that can use the berth.

learn.v: Berth × cargo restrictions · meeting review
learn.exp: Board offered CJ-4 to Yuan Hang Wei Ye (iron ore pellet feed), CJ-6 to African Quail (logs), and treated the Coastal slot as free while Katong WW (SAAGAR project against Coastal) was alongside.
learn.act: Mihir: iron ore not at CJ-1–5; timber cannot work at CJ-2, 3, 6; fertiliser not at CJ-13–16; coal only CJ-5–8; bags only CJ-1–4 and CJ-13–16; "2 shorecrane required" → CJ-2/3 only; vessel-specific requirement in the remark (e.g. Alasia aggregate → CJ-13–16) is binding; millscale is allowed at CJ-13–16; a vessel declared at the meeting counts for the programme only if it arrives before the first HW after the meeting.
learn.why: Commodity-wise berth restrictions and crane/shore limits are standing practice, not in the written policy.
learn.fix: All of the above coded as okBerth() + meetOK(); a SAAGAR project vessel berthed against Coastal occupies the Coastal slot.

learn.v: Sailing times · signal vs programme
learn.exp: Programme for 31.10: Moonlit out 17:00, Sea Gautam out 17:00; programme for 01.11: Ocean Camellia out 23:00.
learn.act: Day signal: Moonlit out 14:00 (amended from 16:15), Sea Gautam 15:15; night signal: Ocean Camellia 21:30.
learn.why: HM fixes the actual slot on the tide and pilot availability; the programme time is a planning figure, the signal is the real one and can be 1–3 h either way.
learn.fix: Board uses the signal time once a signal exists; programme time until then. Nothing to change in the rules.

learn.v: CJ-14 · African Quail vs Feng Hai Da
learn.exp: Board's meeting preview: CJ-14 (after AC Kathryn ~12:30) → African Quail, SAAGAR break bulk; "palat sakta hai agar SAAGAR bulk vessel ready ho".
learn.act: Programme for 01.11: AC Kathryn sails 1 Nov 17:05; CJ-14 → Feng Hai Da (24 HRS group). African Quail not programmed.
learn.why: Exactly the flip the preview named: Rome Trader (petcoke, ETA 31 Oct) reported, declared ready 09:00 and carries SAAGAR status (SGR = Y only in the revised afternoon list; blank in the 0700 list) — it took the SAAGAR bulk slot at CJ-6. With Centurion Buyo on the break-bulk slot, SAAGAR was full, so CJ-14 went down the order to 24 HRS. Also AC Kathryn finishes a day later than the board's estimate.
learn.fix: Mihir (31 Oct): no Indian-flag rule. A vessel is SAAGAR only if it declares SAAGAR priority (the SGR "Y" / rank in the list, or declared at the meeting) — the board takes the declaration as given and cannot know it earlier. So the Quail flip was not predictable from the 0700 list; the preview's "palat sakta hai" line is the right place for it. Board: SAAGAR status = list/meeting declaration only.

learn.v: Logs discharge rate · back to DPA norm
learn.exp: Board had used 4,800 CBM/day for logs vessels (working assumption) → AC Kathryn sailing 31 Oct 12:30.
learn.act: Programme: AC Kathryn readiness 1 Nov 17:05 (≈ 4,000 CBM/day). Mihir: drop the 4,800 figure, go by what the system prints.
learn.why: Per-vessel rates vary; a private assumption only creates confusion against the official sheet.
learn.fix: Logs ETCs taken from the list as printed; waiting logs vessels planned at the DPA norm (3,450 CBM/day, or the list norm where given).

learn.v: Rome Trader · petcoke at CJ-6
learn.exp: Board keeps coal at CJ-7/8 only and treated petcoke like coal.
learn.act: Programme: Rome Trader (petcoke, 50,010 MT, SGR) berths CJ-6 41½–49¾ after Outrivaling 3 shifts to OTB.
learn.why: Petcoke is not restricted to the coal berths; CJ-6 (hopper → truck, no stacking) is acceptable for it.
learn.fix: Petcoke allowed at any non-clean berth; only coal stays CJ-7/8.

learn.v: CJ-7 · HN Doris vs Meghna Venus
learn.exp: Board: CJ-7 after Fu Hai 16 → HN Doris (Govt #2).
learn.act: Programme: CJ-7 → Meghna Venus, HP 50,000 MTPD quote; HN Doris not programmed. Vishva Preeti (Govt #1) → CJ-8 as the board expected.
learn.why: Likely the two Govt berths were counted as Eva Bright (still at CJ-4, not in the programme for 01.11) + Vishva Preeti, so HN Doris waits; and a 50,000 MTPD quote took the HP slot. To confirm at the meeting.
learn.fix: Mihir (31 Oct): HN Doris is 229 m — LOA > 200 is mostly gearless, works only on the port shore crane at CJ-7/8, and only one gearless fertiliser vessel is taken at a time. So HN Doris waits while Vishva Preeti (229 m, urea) works CJ-8. Board now: gearless rule + one-gearless-fertiliser rule.

learn.v: CJ-16 · Alasia over Orion
learn.exp: Board: CJ-16 after Maritime Harmony → Orion (HP #4, salt).
learn.act: Programme: → Alasia (aggregates, ETA 1 Nov 00:30) with a 40,000 MTPD quote, berthing 1 Nov evening.
learn.why: HP is decided by the quote at the meeting, not by the printed rank; an ETA vessel that reports in time competes.
learn.fix: Board already flags "quotes decide" on HP/Sr No 7 slots; nothing more to model without the quotes.

learn.v: Tidal benefit observed · CJ-7
learn.exp: Berth draught 12.0 m, board allows +1.5 m at CJ-6–10.
learn.act: Programme: Fu Hai 16 outward draught 12.65 m; Meghna Venus sailing draught 12.72 m — both at CJ-7.
learn.why: First data points: ≥ 0.7 m over the chart figure is accepted at CJ-7.
learn.fix: Keep 1.5 m for now; two more observations will set the margin.

learn.v: CJ-15 · Katong WW (Coastal slot, SAAGAR project)
learn.exp: Board: CJ-15 after African Predator → Katong WW as SAAGAR project against the Coastal slot.
learn.act: Programme: CJ-15 → Katong WW, category CSTL(SGR). African Predator shifts to OTB 09:00 at agent's request.
learn.why: Rule confirmed on day one.

learn.v: Port-convenience shift · for whom?
learn.exp: Board would have shifted African Quail (logs, CJ-14) to CJ-4 within 10 h of berthing to make room for Feng Hai Da (48 windmill blades, 1,085 MT, ~22 h job).
learn.act: Not observed; board assumption.
learn.why: A 4-hour shift of a logs vessel for a one-day project parcel seems unlikely; shifts are made for sizeable clean-cargo vessels (salt HP, big project).
learn.fix: Mihir (31 Oct): no fixed format. Shiftable = cargo that can work at both CJ and OTB — mainly timber/logs, also bags; never project, fertiliser, salt or coal. No hour rule at all — "the port will shift if required, whether the vessel completes in 1 hour or later". When: a CJ-1–10 berth is free, a priority slot (e.g. HP) is free now or frees inside the programme window, the group's vessel in line needs a clean berth and nobody of that group can use the free berth → logs vessel shifts from CJ-13–16 to the free berth, the clean berth goes to the priority vessel. Coded exactly so; the shift row is shown in the preview with a SHIFT tag.

learn.v: Govt slot filled by a Sr No 7 vessel
learn.exp: Board had treated a 30k/25k (Sr No 7) vessel berthed against a Govt slot as occupying that slot, so the next Govt vessel (HN Doris) waited for it.
learn.act: Practice (Mihir): when a Govt vessel turns up, the Sr No 7 vessel already alongside is re-tagged to Sr No 7 day priority and the Govt vessel takes the next free berth it fits.
learn.why: The Govt earmark is 2 Govt vessels at berth, not 2 fixed berths; a fallback occupant does not count against it.
learn.fix: Govt slot count ignores fallback-filled vessels. Other groups unchanged.

learn.v: Tidal benefit · CJ-6 to CJ-10 only
learn.exp: Board first allowed 1.0 m over the berth draught at every berth.
learn.act: Practice (Mihir): tidal benefit is given only at CJ-6–10 — permissible draught + next low-water height (e.g. 12.0 + ~1.5 m), never at CJ-1–5 or CJ-13–16.
learn.why: Depth and LW height at the middle berths allow it; the shallow north berths and the clean south berths are held to the chart figure.
learn.fix: Mihir (31 Oct): keep it simple — at CJ-6–10 permissible draught is 12 m but up to 14 m is allowed when the channel draught at HW that day is more than 14 m. Board now uses exactly that (TIDE_MAX 14.0, from the DC circular HW table).

learn.v: SAAGAR has three types · project goes against Coastal
learn.exp: Board gave the SAAGAR break-bulk slot (CJ-14 after AC Kathryn) to Katong WW (project cargo, SGR #1) ahead of African Quail (logs, SGR #2).
learn.act: Practice (Mihir): SAAGAR = bulk, break bulk, project. The 1 bulk + 1 break-bulk slots are for bulk / break bulk; a SAAGAR project vessel is berthed against the Coastal slot (when no coastal vessel is ready), and never SAAGAR bulk / break bulk there.
learn.why: Project cargo is slow and small; the coastal slot absorbs it without eating a SAAGAR cargo slot.
learn.fix: Coastal fallback = SAAGAR project vessels by SGR rank; SAAGAR slots skip project vessels while a bulk / break-bulk SAAGAR vessel is ready.

learn.v: Berth draught limits · all groups
learn.exp: Board placed deep-draught vessels (e.g. Tai Knight 14.2 m coal, Bristol 13.5 m DAP, Levante Spirit 12.9 m MOP) on any berth by group.
learn.act: DC chart: CJ-1–5 permit 10.5 m, CJ-6–10 12.0 m, CJ-13 13.5 m, CJ-14–16 14.5 m (tidal benefit possible).
learn.why: Arrival draught decides which berths a vessel can take at all; a 14.2 m coal vessel cannot use CJ-7/8, which is why Tai Knight asks for OTB.
learn.fix: Vessels are now offered only berths whose permissible draught covers their arrival draught (strict, no tidal benefit assumed).

learn.v: Katong WW · SAAGAR break bulk
learn.exp: African Quail (SGR #2 on 30 Oct) next SAAGAR break-bulk vessel after AC Kathryn.
learn.act: 31 Oct list gives Katong WW (project cargo, 1,321 MT) SGR rank 1; it was only STL #4 the day before.
learn.why: A project-cargo vessel can carry SAAGAR status and then ranks in the SGR column by its own reporting date, ahead of logs vessels that reported later.
learn.fix: Ranks are now taken from the SGR column as printed; SAAGAR break bulk includes project cargo.

learn.v: Levante Spirit · Govt priority
learn.exp: Board had a third Govt vessel at CJ-14 on 1 Nov.
learn.act: Policy allows 2 Govt berths at a time.
learn.why: Board bug: a berth already allotted (vessel on the way in) was not counted against the group until the vessel was alongside.
learn.fix: A berth counts against the group from the moment it is allotted.

learn.v: Moonlit · CJ-2 sailing
learn.exp: List ETC 31 Oct 10:05.
learn.act: Programme TF/SH/2102 sails her at 17:00 (readiness draft 10.10 m).
learn.why: Deep-draft departures wait for the tide; ETC is not the sailing time.
learn.fix: When a programme exists, its sailing time overrides the list ETC.

circulars.t: Corrigendum — vacant Bitumen place: the 6,500 MTPD priority, for break bulk cargo only
circulars.s: Corrigendum to the circular of 21.11.2026, which it cites as …/Berthingpolicy/2026/5737. In partial modification of clause (iii), Bitumen Priority (Sr. No. 5): in the absence of a suitable vessel under Bitumen priority, the berth earmarked under this category shall be operated under the 6,500 MTPD priority category (Sr. No. 3(E)) for break bulk cargo only. All else in the policy of 24.03.2025, the circular of 21.05.2026, the corrigendum of 09.07.2026 and the circular of 21.11.2026 stays in force. Approved by the Competent Authority; signed by the Traffic Manager. No date of effect is printed. The reference number (3152) is handwritten.
circulars.eff: ON THE BOARD from v279: from the meeting of 27 Nov (berths from 27 Nov 18:00) a vacant Bitumen place goes to the senior BREAK BULK vessel of the 6.5K line — bags, logs, steel, project cargo; a vessel with cargo in bulk (salt, clay, ore) cannot take it. What it drops from the clause of 21 Nov: the words "instead of the General group" and "subject to eligibility, readiness and seniority" — the policy's own conditions still apply. TODAY IT CHANGES NO ORDER: the 6.5K line is Crystal Land 1, Glimlit 2, Porto Fiscardo 3, Captainannis L 4 (bags), CD Glory 5, Dariya Priya 6, African Tiger 7, Paiwan Ace 8 (logs) — all break bulk; only Rex (ball clay, 8K 11) falls out. The Bitumen berth is CJ-2, with DSM London till about 28 Nov. THE NUMBER OF THE 21 NOV CIRCULAR: handwritten on that paper and read by the board as 5237; this corrigendum types it as 5737; by the run of the series (3089 on 15 Nov, 3152 on 26 Nov) it may well be 3137. The board keeps calling it "circular 5237" until the number is settled.

circulars.t: Trade notice — export of minerals / ores: shipper registered with Geology & Mining, NOC to be given when declaring the vessel ready
circulars.s: On the letter of the Geologist, East Kutch (Anjar), of 28.12.2023 (enclosed), under the Gujarat Mineral (Prevention of Illegal Mining, Transportation and Storage) Rules 2017: shippers who export minerals / ores must be registered with the Geology & Mining Department, and the vessel agent must submit the No Objection Certificate of that Department while declaring the readiness of a vessel planned to load minerals / ores. The Geologist's letter names black trap, china clay and silica sand found stocked in the port.

The papers name black trap, china clay and silica sand; the word salt does not appear in the notice, the letter or the text of the 2017 Rules sent with it. Mihir (21 Nov 2026): this NOC is NOT asked for salt — it does not touch our salt export vessels. (The 47-page Rules are kept in the file, not on the register; date on the notice corrected by hand.)

circulars.t: Deputy Conservator — SOP for disposal of non-hazardous waste from vessels (Swachh Sagar portal), from 09.09.2026
circulars.s: For every vessel at any DPA berth, anchorage, oil jetty or terminal: the Master / agent raises the Advance Notification Form on the Swachh Sagar portal at least 24 hours before arrival (weekly at anchorage) with the inventory of food, domestic, cooking-oil, ash and non-hazardous cargo-residue waste; the portal assigns a DPA-empanelled vendor — no offline vendor; Traffic verifies the ANF before the vessel is programmed for waste hand-over; no separate Harbour Master or fire permission for routine hand-over; the vendor gives a Waste Delivery Receipt endorsed by the Master, uploaded on the portal; zero-value invoices in iPortman are stopped. Failure is reported to DG Shipping. Hazardous, oily, sewage and biomedical waste are outside this SOP.
circulars.eff: For the agency desk on every vessel of ours: ANF on Swachh Sagar 24 hours before arrival, only an empanelled vendor, WDR uploaded. No effect on the berthing queue.

circulars.t: Trade notice (Marine) — Harit Sagar norms for vessels: effluent discharge, scrubbers, waste declaration, ballast water
circulars.s: Effluent discharge as per MARPOL Annex IV and DG Shipping rules; hybrid scrubbers in closed-loop mode within port limits and open-loop scrubber vessels on compliant fuel — no open-loop wash-water in port; every ship declares in advance the type and quantity of waste on board and disposes of it only through the port's facilities; ballast water management as per the IMO convention. Monitoring by the pilot, the Marine representative at the berthing meeting and the safety inspector, with escalation to the Harbour Master, the Deputy Conservator and MMD; penalties, withholding of clearance or reference to DG Shipping for repeated non-compliance.
circulars.eff: For the agency desk: tell the Masters before arrival (scrubber mode, waste declaration, ballast record). The waste declaration is checked at the berthing meeting. No change to the queue.

circulars.ref: HM/AC/General Correspondence/3169 (May 2026; day blank on the copy)
circulars.t: Trade notice (Marine) — Ebola health advisory: Maritime Declaration of Health, self-declaration and screening for crew with Africa travel history
circulars.s: After the WHO declaration of 17.05.2026: agents must obtain the Maritime Declaration of Health from every arriving vessel with the Africa travel history of the last 21 days, have such crew fill the Self Declaration Form, report any person with symptoms to the Port Health Officer / Harbour Master, and allow no shore leave to crew with Africa travel history before thermal screening and clearance. Masters must isolate and report a symptomatic person. Screening categories 1 to 3; non-compliance can mean denial of entry or detention of the vessel. In force until further orders.
circulars.eff: For the agency desk on vessels that called at an African port in the last 21 days. No withdrawal on record. (The register date 20.05.2026 is only a place-holder: the copy shows May 2026 with the day blank.)

circulars.eff: Liquid only. The parent draft circular of 12.06.2026 and the one for October – December 2026 are not on the register.

circulars.t: Circular — renewal of stevedoring and shore handling licences (expiring 31.03.2023), with the proposed scale of rates by commodity
circulars.s: Licences under the 2019 Regulations expire on 31.03.2023; existing stevedores renew for three years or the licence is treated as cancelled; ceiling rates as per the upfront tariff; royalty as per Board Resolution 138 of 16.12.2022. Enclosed: the proposed scale of rates (Rs per tonne, foreign / coastal) for stevedoring with and without winchman and for shore handling methods M1 to M5 — 17 break-bulk groups (bagged cargo, steel, timber logs soft and hard, granite and others) and 13 dry bulk groups (fertiliser, coal, ores, scrap, gypsum, salt and others).
circulars.eff: Our licence and our ceiling rates. As read from the copy, stevedoring with winchman, foreign / coastal: salt Rs 56 / 34, timber logs soft Rs 172 / 103, timber logs hard Rs 274 / 164 per tonne — check the PDF before quoting. The three years from this renewal ran to 31.03.2026; the 2026 renewal circular is on the register. (File number as printed; date corrected by hand to 21.02.2023.)

circulars.t: Circular — penal berth hire dues to be paid immediately on invoice
circulars.s: Some port users are not paying penal berth hire charges even after the Harbour Master's office issues invoices; the dues must be cleared immediately after the invoice.
circulars.eff: For the accounts desk: a penal berth hire invoice is to be paid at once; unpaid dues also block the yearly authorization renewal. No effect on the queue.

circulars.t: Circular — safety advisory after high-potential near-miss incidents inside the port
circulars.s: Four lessons: dumper trucks must be driven with the body lowered; coal heaps are to be sprayed only by a tanker with a water monitor, from at least 10 m; chain-mounted excavators are to be lifted by crane only as per the maker's rigging instructions; truck drivers need safety training — the entry pass is issued only after it, and a negligent driver can be barred.
circulars.eff: For our dumpers, excavators lifted into holds and truck drivers. Read with the punitive action notices on the register.

circulars.t: Circular — RFID (e-Drishti) dock entry permits compulsory for cargo vehicles from 06.12.2022
circulars.s: From 07:00 on 06.12.2022 only vehicles holding a valid dock entry permit from the e-Drishti portal / app are let in through the cargo gates.
circulars.eff: For our trucks and dumpers. (The day in the date is not clear on the copy; read as 25.11.2022.)

circulars.t: Circular — entry passes for one year with police verification; three months for temporary labour, supervisors and drivers
circulars.s: Entry passes for one year for those with valid police verification; temporary passes for labour, supervisors and drivers for three months, with police verification; till RFID is in place at the North Gate.
circulars.eff: Continued by the circular of 06.03.2023 and the later gate-pass circulars on the register.

circulars.t: Circular — port users must exchange vessel messages through PCS 1x
circulars.s: Messages to be sent through PCS 1x for every event: vessel profile, voyage registration, berth management, ETA / ETD, pilot memo, pre-arrival notification, crew list, agent delivery order, terminal performance report, vessel movement, re-berthing, dangerous goods notification, agency change.
circulars.eff: For the agency desk; the system has since moved to NLP-Marine and EBS (circulars of 2024 and 2026 on the register).

circulars.t: Trade notice — Cargo Jetty 2 withdrawn for maintenance dredging, 12 – 17 November 2022
circulars.s: CJ-2 withdrawn for maintenance dredging from 12.11.2022 to 17.11.2022.
circulars.eff: Period over. History only: how long a CJ-2 dredging closure lasts (6 days).

circulars.t: Trade notice — withdrawal of Cargo Jetty 1 and 2 and Oil Jetty 1 and 4 (November 2021)
circulars.s: CJ-2 withdrawn 01 – 06.11.2021 and CJ-1 08 – 17.11.2021 for maintenance and dredging; OJ-1 on 09.11.2021 and OJ-4 on 11.11.2021 for dismantling of old loading arms.
circulars.eff: Period over. History only: CJ-1 dredging took 10 days, CJ-2 six.

circulars.t: Trade circular (Finance) — revolving PDA (Port Deposit Account) from 01.07.2024
circulars.s: With the new port operating system from 01.07.2024 a revolving PDA is introduced: no minimum balance; the user tops up under one of three heads on the NLP / EBS portal — Cargo (wharfage, storage, demurrage), Stevedoring (stevedoring royalty, mobile harbour crane hire), Vessel (marine services) — and money under one head cannot be used for another. Charges are assessed before the berthing request, as before; a shortfall must be paid before asking for the No Due Certificate and again at the final invoice; after vessel closure any excess assessed goes back to the PDA for use on another vessel; no interest; a refund of idle balance is given on request.
circulars.eff: For the accounts desk: keep the right PDA head funded before the berthing request — a vessel head balance will not pay wharfage or stevedoring royalty. No change to the queue.

circulars.t: Circular — royalty for stevedoring and shore handling Rs 8.97 per MT for one year from 01.04.2024
circulars.s: Royalty at the existing rate of Rs 8.97 per MT, with nil annual escalation, on combined stevedoring and shore handling for one year from 01.04.2024.
circulars.eff: Our royalty for 2024-25. Then Rs 9.06 (16.04.2025) and Rs 9.10 (07.05.2026), both on the register.

circulars.t: Circular — royalty Rs 8.00 per MT on stevedoring and shore handling for one year from 20.10.2022
circulars.s: Board Resolution 138 of 16.12.2022: royalty Rs 8.00 per MT on both stevedoring and shore handling for one year from 20.10.2022, subject to escalation.

circulars.t: Circular — no 200 % berth hire at Cargo Jetty 02, 03 and 10 when the ship works only with her own gear
circulars.s: Board Resolution 213 of 11.03.2024: 200 % berth hire at CJ-2, CJ-3 and CJ-10 is not levied if the ship works exclusively with ship's gear; it is levied if DPA ELL shore cranes or any other shore cranes are used. Booking of the ELL cranes is not mandatory. Review after 11 months.
circulars.eff: The first paper of this rule; modified on 24.07.2024 and repeated on 05.08.2025 and 18.06.2026, all on the register. (Date printed 12.03.2024, corrected by hand to 15.)

circulars.t: Corrigendum — Board resolution numbers in three circulars of 13.03.2024
circulars.s: In the circulars of 13.03.2024 (SAGAR / cargo promotion …/127, relaxation …/126, OJ-5 …/125) the Board resolution numbers are corrected to 213, 212 and 214.
circulars.eff: A numbering correction only.

circulars.t: Circular — renewal of port users' authorization for 01.04.2024 to 31.03.2025
circulars.s: Authorizations expire on 31.03.2024; renewal for 2024-25 with the same conditions as later years: identical names in application, police NOC and ID; PF certificate for stevedoring licensees; dues and damage dues cleared; labour contractor only through the appointing company with a labour licence; at most 5 signatories for gate passes.
circulars.eff: Period over; the 2025-26 circular (…/293 dt 07.02.2025) is on the register.

circulars.t: Circular — renewal of trade licences for 01.04.2023 to 31.03.2024, with the application form
circulars.s: Trade licences (ship chandling, repairs, bunker supply and the other trades) expire on 31.03.2023; renewal for 2023-24 on the composite application form, enclosed with instructions and the fee / deposit schedule.
circulars.eff: Not the stevedoring licence. Period over; the 2026-27 circular is on the register. (Date printed 13.02.2023, corrected by hand to 20.)

circulars.t: Circular — longer validity of gate passes against residence, Aadhaar and police verification
circulars.s: Gate pass validity is extended on: permanent resident certificate, attested Aadhaar copy, police verification from the Gandhidham / Adipur / Kandla police station of residence, the individual's application, a certificate from the company that he is on its payroll, and an undertaking. Without police verification no pass beyond 15 days; for workers from other states hired temporarily, 3 months.
circulars.eff: For our staff and labour. The one-year gate pass circular of 05.08.2025 and the Aadhaar circular of 21.04.2026 on the register came later. (Date corrected by hand to 07.03.2023.)

circulars.t: Circular — police verification of drivers on the e-Drishti portal
circulars.s: CHAs and transporters must upload the police verification of their drivers on the e-Drishti portal within 15 days (reminder of circular …/775 dt 17.08.2022).
circulars.eff: For our transport side. (Date corrected by hand to 07.03.2023.)

circulars.t: Circular — support e-mail for NLP-Marine (PCS module live from 05.12.2022)
circulars.s: The PCS module of the NLP Marine portal went live on 05.12.2022; support requests go to the NLP support e-mail given in the circular.
circulars.eff: For the agency desk. The EBS helpdesk notice of 23.03.2026 on the register is the current support channel for EBS.

circulars.t: Circular — rebate on vessel-related charges for container vessels from 01.01.2024
circulars.s: Board Resolution 148: coastal container vessels 40 % on coastal charges; foreign container vessels 50 % up to 35,000 GRT, 75 % for 35,001 – 65,000 GRT, 80 % above; from 01.01.2024.
circulars.eff: Containers only. Modified on 19.03.2025 and 20.08.2025, both on the register.

circulars.t: Circular — container vessel VRC rebate continued till the Board decides
circulars.s: The rebate for container vessels of circular TF/SH/VRC/2022 dt 23.12.2022 remains valid till a decision of the Board.
circulars.eff: Containers only. Replaced by …/716 dt 15.12.2023 on the register.

circulars.t: Circular — container vessel VRC rebate for 01.01.2023 to 31.01.2023
circulars.s: In supersession of circular MW/WK/1148/4000 dt 08.12.2021: coastal container vessels as per SOR; foreign container vessels 50 % up to 40,000 GRT, 75 % for 40,001 – 65,000 GRT, 80 % above; for January 2023.
circulars.eff: Containers only. Period over.

circulars.t: Circular — fertiliser storage in covered godowns: 60 days on rent (01.11.2023 to 30.04.2024)
circulars.s: From 01.11.2023 to 30.04.2024 imported fertiliser may be stored in covered godowns on rental terms for the first 60 days, then demurrage as per SOR.
circulars.eff: Fertiliser only. Period over.

circulars.t: Circular — fertiliser storage policy amended: 60 days in peak season, 90 days in lean season, from 01.05.2023
circulars.s: Board Resolution 161 of 03.02.2023: covered godowns for imported fertiliser on rental terms up to 60 days in the peak season and up to 90 days in the lean season from 01.05.2023, instead of 30 days; the Chairperson fixes the seasons each year.
circulars.eff: Fertiliser only. The base of the later fertiliser storage circulars on the register.

circulars.t: Circular — fertiliser storage in covered godowns: 90 days on rent (01.01.2023 to 30.04.2023)
circulars.s: From 01.01.2023 to 30.04.2023 imported fertiliser may be stored in covered godowns on rental terms for the first 90 days, then demurrage as per SOR.
circulars.eff: Fertiliser only. Period over.

circulars.t: Trade notice — rebate on vessel-related charges for salt vessels: 20 % / 30 % / 35 % by parcel size (the base notice)
circulars.s: Vessels discharging or loading coastal / foreign salt at DPA berths get a discount on pilotage, port dues and berth hire: parcel 40,000 – 49,999 MT 20 %; 50,000 – 59,999 MT 30 %; 60,000 MT and above 35 %. From 30.08.2024 for six months, subject to review.
circulars.eff: SALT — our line. This is the notice all the later salt VRC extensions on the register point to, so these are the slabs: nothing below 40,000 MT. Its own six months are over; the extensions keep it alive.

circulars.t: Circular — trade promotion rebates 01.10.2024 to 31.03.2025: 15 % wharfage discount on salt in bulk at the jetties and on timber logs mid-stream, HMC hire, open-plot storage
circulars.s: In continuation of circular TF/SH/Relaxation/2024/126 dt 13.03.2024: (1) hire of 60 MT and 120 MT harbour mobile cranes on the quantity handled, for all dry bulk cargo; (2) open-storage benefit of coal and coke (circular …/209 dt 03.03.2023) extended to all dry bulk cargo; (3) the overstayal-cargo circular of 16.08.2020 in abeyance for coal and coke in open plots; (4) 15 % off wharfage for 75,000 MT or more of coal and coke in one voyage mid-stream, with two barge points; (5) 15 % off wharfage on timber logs handled mid-stream; (6) 15 % off wharfage on salt in bulk at the dry cargo jetties.
circulars.eff: SALT and TIMBER — the base notice of the trade promotion benefits. Continued by …/390 dt 01.04.2025 and …/1864 dt 16.04.2026, both on the register. Worth checking that our salt wharfage bills carry the 15 % discount.

circulars.t: Circular — berthing policy amended: priority groups 3(A) to 3(G) for dry cargo
circulars.s: Appendix-01A modified: 3(A) SAAGAR — one berth, seniority by parcel size; 3(AA) bitumen tankers at dry cargo berths — one, 15 % above norm; 3(B) higher productivity — two, 15 % above norm or 10,000 MTPD, highest commitment first; 3(C) parcel of 8,000 MT and more finishing within 24 hours — one; 3(D) 15,000 MTPD priority — one; 3(E) 8,000 / 6,500 MTPD priority — one (bulk 8,000, break bulk 6,500, or 15 % above norm); 3(F) parcel of 14,000 MT and more finishing within 48 hours — one, when no 3(B) vessel is eligible; 3(G) any vessel committing higher productivity — one. 3(A) to 3(G) are the Priority group, at most 7 berths.
circulars.eff: History of the priority groups the board uses. SAAGAR was changed by circular …/61 dt 14.02.2025 and the whole table was re-issued in the policy …/2025/385 dt 24.03.2025, both on the register; the board follows 385 and its amendments. No change to the board. (The circular prints the effective meeting as 28.09.2023 — a slip for 2024.)

circulars.t: Trade circular (Harbour Master) — new port operating system live from 01.07.2024; only the agent who registered the vessel can pay
circulars.s: The ERP-based port operating system, linked to NLP (Marine), went live on 01.07.2024 for documentation, traffic and marine services and their payments. Only the vessel agent who registered the vessel is allowed to make the payment.
circulars.eff: For the agency and accounts desks; goes with the third-party payment circular of 23.05.2025 on the register. No effect on berthing.

circulars.t: Trade notice — rebate on vessel-related charges for coal and coke vessels: 20 % / 30 % / 35 % by parcel size (the base notice)
circulars.s: Vessels with coastal / foreign coal or coke at the dry cargo jetties: discount on pilotage, port dues and berth hire of 20 % for 40,000 – 49,999 MT, 30 % for 50,000 – 59,999 MT, 35 % for 60,000 MT and above; from 19.07.2024 for six months.
circulars.eff: Coal and coke. The base notice of the later extensions on the register. (It came with a KPSAA letter of 23.09.2024 asking for refund of the rebate — that letter is kept in the file, not on the register.)

circulars.t: Trade notice — rebates on vessel-related charges for coal and coke vessels continued to 17.07.2025
circulars.s: The rebates of trade notice …/549 dt 18.07.2024 continue for six months, up to 17.07.2025.
circulars.eff: Period over; continued by the later notices on the register.

circulars.t: Circular — 200 % berth hire at Cargo Jetty 02, 03 and 10 only if DPA ELL shore cranes are used
circulars.s: In partial modification of circulars …/PF1/136 dt 15.03.2024 and …/291 dt 29.04.2024: 200 % berth hire at CJ-2, CJ-3 and CJ-10 is levied only when DPA ELL shore cranes are used there.
circulars.eff: Repeated by …/553 dt 05.08.2025 and …/2230 dt 18.06.2026, both on the register.

circulars.t: Circular — port HMC charges for thermal coal apply to pet coke as well
circulars.s: The charges for use of port-owned harbour mobile cranes for thermal coal apply also to pet coke.
circulars.eff: Taken into the commodity-wise HMC rates of …/531 dt 29.07.2025 on the register.

circulars.t: Trade notice — 20 % wharfage discount on bagged cargo loaded entirely mid-stream (first notice)
circulars.s: 20 % off wharfage on bagged cargo when the vessel loads its whole cargo mid-stream by barges using the Zero Panel area beside CJ-1; for vessels starting loading from 04.11.2024, for six months.
circulars.eff: Period over; extended to IKLL / Bunder Basin by …/88 dt 07.11.2024 and continued by the later notices on the register.

circulars.t: Trade notice — bagged cargo wharfage discount extended to barges loaded from the IKLL barge jetty and Bunder Basin
circulars.s: The 20 % discount of circular …/896 dt 04.11.2024 applies also to barges loaded from the IKLL barge jetty and the Bunder Basin.
circulars.eff: Period over; continued by the later notices on the register.

circulars.t: Trade notice — wharfage on bitumen under the head "POL Products"
circulars.s: Wharfage on bitumen is collected under "POL Products" of the Liquid (in bulk) category of the Scale of Rates.
circulars.eff: Bitumen only.

circulars.t: Trade notice — wharfage on sludge oil under "All other unspecified goods"
circulars.s: Wharfage on sludge oil is collected under "All other unspecified goods" of the dry cargo category of the Scale of Rates.
circulars.eff: Sludge oil only.

circulars.t: Corrigendum — schedule of pilotage fees in the Scale of Rates (Vadinar slab above 60,000 GRT), with the gazette notification
circulars.s: Gazette notification CH/DPA/04/2024 dt 13.08.2024 corrects Schedule 2.1 of the SOR: in the Vadinar slab above 60,000 GRT the words "over 30000 GRT" are to be read "over 60000 GRT". Pilotage per GRT at Kandla, unchanged: up to 30,000 GRT Rs 27.5577 coastal / US$ 1.1147 foreign; 30,001 – 60,000 GRT Rs 8,26,732.12 + Rs 22.0462 per GRT over 30,000 / US$ 33,440.66 + US$ 0.8918; above 60,000 GRT Rs 14,88,117.81 + Rs 19.2904 per GRT over 60,000 / US$ 60,193.19 + US$ 0.7803.
circulars.eff: A wording correction for Vadinar only; of use as a ready copy of the Kandla pilotage slabs. (Date on the copy corrected by hand to 27.08.2024.)

circulars.t: Circular — RFID access control (e-Drishti) at the North Gate: only valid RFID cards from 15.09.2024
circulars.s: The earlier circular is kept in abeyance till 14.09.2024; all port users must register their personnel in e-Drishti. From 15.09.2024 entry at the North Gate is only with a valid RFID card.
circulars.eff: For our staff and labour entering by the North Gate. No effect on berthing.

circulars.t: Circular — RFID access control (e-Drishti) at the North Gate: date moved to 01.09.2024
circulars.s: Circular …/511 dt 08.07.2024 kept in abeyance till 31.08.2024; RFID-only entry at the North Gate from 01.09.2024.
circulars.eff: Date moved again to 15.09.2024 by the circular of 28.08.2024 on the register.

circulars.t: Circular — storage policy for imported fertiliser: 90 days on rent in covered godowns (01.09.2024 to 31.03.2025)
circulars.s: From 01.09.2024 to 31.03.2025 imported fertiliser may be stored in covered godowns on rental terms for the first 90 days, then demurrage as per SOR.
circulars.eff: Fertiliser only. Period over; continued by …/312 dt 05.05.2025 and the later circulars on the register.

circulars.t: Circular (Vadinar) — SOP for ship-to-ship transfer of petroleum, chemicals and liquefied gases at the Offshore Oil Terminal
circulars.s: STS operations at OOT Vadinar follow the CDI / ICS / OCIMF / SIGTTO Ship to Ship Transfer Guide; the STS superintendent must hold a Master (FG) certificate and the advanced tanker training certificate; Yokohama fenders; cryogenic hoses; a tug with external fire fighting; only at the designated Vadinar anchorage; suspended at wind of 20 knots and above with 2.0 m swell; charges as per SOR.
circulars.eff: Vadinar liquid only; nothing for Kandla dry cargo.

circulars.t: Circular — third-party payments discontinued
circulars.s: Before EBS the port accepted payment from one party on behalf of another with the consent of both. This is discontinued: payment is accepted only from the entity to whom the service or facility is allotted.
circulars.eff: For the accounts desk: each DPA bill must be paid from the account of the firm it is raised on — one group firm cannot pay for another, and a receiver cannot pay the agent's bill. No effect on berthing.

circulars.t: Circular — royalty for stevedoring and shore handling Rs 9.06 per MT from 01.04.2025
circulars.s: TAMP indexation for 01.04.2025 – 31.03.2026: 1.04 % (60 % of WPI) for the SOR and royalty, 1.74 % (100 % of WPI) for the performance-linked tariff. Royalty for S&SH activity Rs 9.06 per metric ton for one year from 01.04.2025.
circulars.eff: Our stevedoring royalty for 2025-26. Replaced by Rs 9.10 per MT from the circular of 07.05.2026 on the register.

circulars.t: Circular — renewal of port users' authorization for 01.04.2025 to 31.03.2026, with the undertaking formats
circulars.s: Authorizations expire on 31.03.2025; renewal for 2025-26 at the Shipping Section. Conditions: names identical in the application, police NOC (not older than one month) and ID proof; stevedoring and shore handling licensees give the PF deduction certificate, others a PF undertaking; one person cannot be authorized by two firms unless the owners are the same; changes in the firm's constitution to be reported; port and government dues (TDS, damages) to be cleared, with a no-dues undertaking; damage dues within 15 days or the entry permission is suspended; a labour contractor must hold a labour licence naming the principal employer and is authorized only through the appointing company, with an indemnity letter; at most 5 authorized signatories for gate passes.
circulars.eff: The yearly authorization of our firms and staff. Period over; the later authorization papers are on the register. A second copy came with the date left blank — the same circular.

circulars.t: Circular — berthing policy amended: SAAGAR group 3(A) seniority and berths; group 5 (granite / break bulk within 96 hours) suspended
circulars.s: Appendix-01A, dry cargo, from the meeting of 17.02.2025: 3(A) vessels declared under the SAAGAR scheme — two berths; inter-se seniority by the time of documentary readiness (including payment of charges) or the time of reporting, whichever is later; when reporting times coincide the larger parcel is senior; one berth for dry bulk and one for break bulk, both open to the other kind when no vessel of one kind is there. Group 5 (granite block / other break bulk except steel / project cargo, finishing within 96 hours) stands suspended.
circulars.eff: History of the SAAGAR rule the board uses. Taken into the comprehensive berthing policy …/2025/385 dt 24.03.2025, which is on the register and is what the board follows. No change to the board.

circulars.t: Trade notice — fixed base rate as per SOR of each commodity as HMC crane hire
circulars.s: The fixed base rate of each commodity as per the Scale of Rates is approved as the crane hire charge for cargo handled by HMC cranes.
circulars.eff: Replaced by the commodity-wise rates of …/531 dt 29.07.2025 on the register (salt Rs 43.76 / 72.93 per MT).

circulars.t: Trade notice — trade promotion rebates continued to 31.03.2026 (mid-stream and jetty cargo, open-plot storage, HMC hire, wharfage)
circulars.s: The relaxations / rebates of trade notice …/800 dt 27.09.2024 — cargo handled mid-stream and at the dry cargo jetties, storage charges at open plots for all dry bulk cargo, hire of port HMCs for dry bulk, wharfage discount — continue for one year, up to 31.03.2026, reviewed every 3 months.
circulars.eff: Period over; carried forward by …/1864 dt 16.04.2026 on the register.

circulars.t: Trade notice — 20 % wharfage discount on bagged cargo loaded entirely mid-stream, continued to 31.03.2026
circulars.s: 20 % off wharfage on bagged cargo when the vessel loads the whole cargo mid-stream by barges using the Zero Panel area beside CJ-1, the IKLL barge jetty and the Bunder Basin (notices …/896 dt 04.11.2024 and …/88 dt 07.11.2024), valid to 31.03.2026.
circulars.eff: Period over; carried forward by …/1779 dt 01.04.2026 on the register.

circulars.t: Trade notice — 50 % concession in railway terminal charges (first notice, 24.02 to 23.08.2025)
circulars.s: 50 % concession in railway terminal charges for rakes of all commodities, containers included, at KPRK and DDPS, for six months from 24.02.2025 to 23.08.2025.
circulars.eff: Period over; continued by …/861 dt 01.10.2025 and the later notices on the register.

circulars.t: Circular — rebate on vessel-related charges for container vessels (slabs at 1,400 TEUs)
circulars.s: Coastal container vessels 40 %; foreign container vessels 50 / 75 / 80 % by GRT slab up to 1,400 TEUs handled and 80 / 85 / 90 % above 1,400 TEUs; from 19.03.2025.
circulars.eff: Containers only. Modified by …/616 dt 20.08.2025 (slab cut to 1,000 TEUs), on the register.

circulars.t: Circular — storage policy for imported fertiliser: 90 days on rent in covered godowns (01.04 to 31.12.2025)
circulars.s: From 01.04.2025 to 31.12.2025 imported fertiliser may be stored in covered godowns on rental terms for the first 90 days; after that, demurrage as per SOR on the balance. Other terms of the storage policy of 30.09.2021 unchanged.
circulars.eff: Fertiliser only. Period over; the fertiliser storage circular of 06.08.2026 on the register is the current one.

circulars.t: Circular — fertiliser storage policy applied to imported fertiliser raw material till 15.09.2025
circulars.s: The storage policy of circular …/312 dt 05.05.2025 applies also to imported fertiliser raw material, till 15.09.2025.
circulars.eff: Fertiliser raw material only. Period over.

circulars.t: Trade notice — no berth for a vessel carrying goods originating in or exported from Pakistan
circulars.s: On DGFT Notification 06/2025-26 dt 02.05.2025 and the CBIC circular of 03.05.2025: DPA will not berth any vessel with goods originating in or exported from Pakistan on board; other vessels move as usual, till further orders.
circulars.eff: A vessel with any such cargo on board is refused a berth. No withdrawal on record. Does not touch our salt or timber calls.

circulars.t: Trade notice — onboard permissions granted by the Marine Department alone
circulars.s: Permissions for onboard works asked by vessel agents are granted only by the Marine Department; approval of Traffic officials is no longer needed.
circulars.eff: For the agency desk: onboard work permission goes to Marine, not Traffic. No effect on berthing.

circulars.t: Trade notice — wharfage on fly ash under the head "Construction material and Sand"
circulars.s: Wharfage on fly ash is collected under "Construction material and Sand" of the dry cargo category of the Scale of Rates.
circulars.eff: Fly ash only.

circulars.ref: Traffic/Shipping/3006/wharfage/2024/… (number not clear on the copy)
circulars.t: Trade notice — wharfage on LPG revised: propane Rs 176.18 / 293.63, butane Rs 171.93 / 286.55 per MT
circulars.s: In partial modification of the SOR and of notice …/103 dt 03.03.2025: wharfage per MT, coastal / foreign — propane 176.18 / 293.63, butane 171.93 / 286.55, from 16.04.2025.
circulars.eff: Liquid (LPG) only.

circulars.t: Circular — One Nation One Port Process documentation at all major ports
circulars.s: On the Ministry's letter of 20.12.2024, the One Nation One Port Process documentation applies at all major ports from 01.01.2025. The standardised list of documents for PHO, Immigration and the Port Authority was circulated for feedback by 17.02.2025; a peer audit was held on 20 – 21 February 2025. Documents must be submitted as per the standardised list.

circulars.t: Trade notice — temporary land outside the Customs Landing Area for aggregation of export salt (revised terms)
circulars.s: To raise salt exports in the last quarter of FY 2025-26 (port target 175 MMT): land outside the Customs Landing Area, near the dock, allotted for 3 months, extendable on performance, for stocking export salt before shipment. The exporter commits a Minimum Guaranteed Cargo (MGC); for an existing exporter the MGC is over and above his AVERAGE volume through DPA in the last 3 financial years. Land shared in proportion to the MGC committed; licence fee Rs 26,789.10 per acre per annum (Rs 2,232.42 per acre per month); refundable security deposit of 3 months' licence fee, forfeited if the MGC is not achieved. Open storage only, no structures; DPA may end it at any time.
circulars.eff: SALT — our line. Softer than the first notice of 16.01.2026 (…/186): average instead of peak volume, a security deposit of 3 months' fee instead of a bank guarantee for the wharfage, and extension allowed. Whether the facility is continued in FY 2026-27 is not on record — to ask the port if we want land for export salt.

circulars.t: Trade notice — temporary land outside the Customs Landing Area for aggregation of export salt (first notice)
circulars.s: Land outside the Customs Landing Area, near the dock, for up to 3 months for stocking export salt. MGC over and above the exporter's PEAK volume of the last three years; licence fee Rs 26,789.10 per acre per annum; bank guarantee equal to the wharfage (with GST) on the MGC quantity; wharfage payable on any shortfall, and the guarantee can be invoked; the allotment lapses after 3 months with no right of extension.
circulars.eff: SALT. Replaced by the revised notice …/1535 dt 09.02.2026 (on the register), which eased the terms.

circulars.t: Trade notice — pre-commencement procedures to be completed at OTB in fair weather (dry bulk export vessels)
circulars.s: Agents of dry bulk export vessels must complete the pre-commencement procedures while the vessel is at the Outer Tuna Buoy, before berthing, in the fair-weather season (September to May). For break-bulk export vessels the same at anchorage is strongly advised wherever feasible. The aim is less idle time at berth.
circulars.eff: SALT export vessels: pre-commencement (surveys and the like) to be done at OTB before the vessel comes alongside, September to May. Saves berth time; no change to the queue.

circulars.t: Circular — safe handling of timber logs at berths (safety net, divers, standby boat, loss-over-board report)
circulars.s: Timber handling agents must: (1) rig a robust safety net between vessel and berth during timber work; (2) arrange professional divers to recover logs that fall in the water — if the port has to recover them, the agent pays the cost and penalties; (3) keep a small boat on standby alongside for the whole stay; (4) record every Loss Over Board log in the daily working report and report it to the Wharf Supervisor / Shift In-charge / ATM. Damage to harbour craft, vessels or port property by floating logs is recovered in full from the stevedore and the S&SH agent.
circulars.eff: TIMBER — our line. This is the parent circular 528 that the timber-log corrigendum of 22.07.2026 on the register refers to; it was missing till now. Net, divers, standby boat and LOB entry in the daily report are on the stevedore for log vessels; the corrigendum of 22.07.2026 made it not mandatory for hard wood logs.

circulars.t: Trade notice — punitive actions in case of incidents in the port premises (framework and table)
circulars.s: Punitive Action Framework, imposed by the departmental heads: (1) low-potential dangerous occurrence — warning notice, dock entry permit suspended 1 week, Rs 10,000; (2) high-potential dangerous occurrence (vehicle into the sea, crane tipping, cargo / grab falling, no injury) — show cause, permit suspended 1 month, Rs 50,000; (3) minor injury, minor fire or spill — show cause, 15 days, Rs 20,000; (4) major injury, major fire or spill — show cause, 3 months, Rs 50,000; (5) fatal / major incident — show cause, 6 months or cancellation of the permit, Rs 1,00,000.
circulars.eff: Applies to our stevedoring work (grab or log falling, vehicle or crane incident). The stevedore undertaking and punitive action matrix of 16.04.2026 on the register came after this — read the two together.

circulars.t: Circular (Finance) — TDS at 2 % on vessel-related and cargo-related charges paid to DPA; 10 % on lease rent
circulars.s: Port users must deduct TDS at 2 % under section 194C of the Income Tax Act on payments to DPA for vessel-related charges (port dues, pilotage, berth hire, anchorage, tug hire, penal / priority berth hire) and cargo-related charges (wharfage, stevedoring royalty, ground rent, demurrage, MHC hire and royalty, terminal charges), and at 10 % under section 194-I on lease rent of land / estates, at credit or payment, whichever is earlier. If not done, the PDA account can be debited. The TDS must be deposited and reported in the return, and Form 16A given to DPA every quarter by the statutory date, failing which the outstanding TDS is debited from the PDA account.
circulars.eff: For the accounts desk: applies to every DPA bill of ours (berth hire, wharfage, stevedoring royalty, ground rent, lease rent) — deduct, deposit, and give Form 16A each quarter, or the PDA is debited. No effect on berthing.

circulars.ref: IT/RA/Safety Officer/… (number not legible on the copy)
circulars.t: Trade notice — mandatory undertaking by the stevedore at berth allotment; SOP for cargo handling; punitive action matrix
circulars.s: Three documents are enforced. (1) UNDERTAKING by the stevedore at the time of berth allotment — stevedore, vessel agent, vessel and berth, cargo; equipment (HMC, excavators, pay loaders, forklifts, hoppers, trucks, loose gear); manpower for 12-hour shifts with safety training and medical certificates (responsible person / port captain, foremen and berth supervisors with names and mobile numbers, operators, signalmen, drivers, labour); PPE by cargo (helmets, jackets, shoes, masks, goggles); signed by the owner / director / partner. It goes to ATM(O), copy to TM, Sr. DTM, DTM and the Safety Officer, at least 24 hours before work starts. (2) The approved SOP for cargo handling is followed at site — the foreman keeps a signed copy; the ship-shore safety checklist is completed before starting; a tool box talk every shift, with record and photographs. (3) PUNITIVE ACTION MATRIX — unsafe act / PPE or traffic violation: warning, Rs 1,000; low-potential occurrence: dock entry permit suspended 1 week, Rs 10,000; minor injury / fire / spill: 15 days, Rs 20,000; high-potential occurrence (vehicle into the sea, crane tipping, cargo or grab falling, no casualty): 1 month, Rs 50,000; major injury / fire / spill: 3 months, Rs 5,00,000; fatality or major incident: 6 months or blacklisting, Rs 25,00,000 per fatality for the first incident in a year and Rs 30,00,000 for the second; CARGO FALLING INTO THE SEA (logs, timber, coils, loose items): Rs 50,000 per incident with no damage, Rs 2,00,000 plus full repair cost if a tug, pilot boat or port craft is damaged, and stevedore operations suspended 1 month. A list of 100 unsafe acts names who is responsible for each. In force at once. (The SOP for cargo handling, 47 pages in Hindi, came with it and is not attached here; the undertaking form and the matrix are — circ/2026-04-16_stevedore-undertaking-form.pdf, circ/2026-04-16_punitive-action-matrix.pdf.)
circulars.eff: No effect on the berthing order, but it sits on every berth allotment: the stevedore files the undertaking 24 hours before work. For timber: a log falling into the water is Rs 50,000 an incident, and Rs 2,00,000 plus repairs with a month's suspension if a port craft is hit.

circulars.ref: TF/SO/DGOSH/2026/… (number not legible on the copy)
circulars.t: Trade notice — mandatory use of designated rest areas by dock workers; no resting in operational areas, including on board vessels
circulars.s: After an incident in which workers resting in an operational area were hurt by a vehicle: no worker may sit, rest, sleep or take breaks on berths and jetties, backup areas and cargo plots, stacking areas, truck lanes and roadways, or on board in cargo work areas, on hatch covers, decks or access ways. Workers must use the rest shelters, canteens and welfare facilities. A CHA or stevedore who wants more rest shelters may apply to the port, which will permit portable container-based shelters. CHAs, stevedores, contractors and labour suppliers must brief the workers, supervise, and correct at once. A worker found resting in an operational area is a serious safety violation for which the employer is held responsible — suspension of operations, violation notices, recovery of costs and penalties are possible. In force at once.
circulars.eff: No effect on berthing. A duty on the stevedore as employer of the gangs; a stevedore may ask the port for a container rest shelter near the work.

circulars.t: Non-operational Automatic Identification System (AIS) on ships in Indian waters
circulars.s: Deputy Conservator's circular: agents must tell their masters to follow DG Shipping Order 15 of 2022 (dt 27.05.2022, enclosed). AIS must stay on under way and at anchor; if it is switched off or fails, the master must at once inform the nearest Indian MRCC and DGCOMM Centre and log it. A vessel with a non-operational AIS, or AIS switched off without informing, may be detained, with a fee of Rs 8,00,000 to the Central Government and action against master and owners — on the decision of the Principal Officer, MMD. The Signal Station reports any such vessel to the Harbour Master and the DC.
circulars.eff: No effect on the berthing order. A duty on the vessel agent for every vessel. (The HM signal of 21 Nov night carries the remark "AIS not working" against the barge with tug Sagar 5.)

circulars.t: Collection and safe disposal of empty fumigant / chemical containers, fumigant residues and quarantine waste
circulars.s: M/s Sensation Pest Control Services is allowed to install two collection chambers inside the port. Vessel agents must see that fumigant residues, empty cans and quarantine waste on vessels with imported timber logs / agricultural cargo are removed and disposed of safely, using the chambers. Fumigation agencies need a valid DPA authorization; after an incident on an import vessel, all fumigation technicians must hold training certificates from Government-approved centres.
circulars.eff: Superseded by the circular of 09.10.2026 (…/1372/1656), which repeats and tightens it. Kept for the record.

circulars.t: Standardization of mandatory safety PPE — helmet / bump cap, reflective jacket and safety shoes: colour coding, specifications and mandatory use in port operational areas
circulars.s: Colour code: (1) port management, managers of agents / CHAs / stevedores / terminals, officers, surveyors, supervisors and foremen — white helmet, green jacket, black shoes; (2) all workers, signalmen, equipment operators, truck drivers, tally clerks, casual labour — yellow helmet, orange jacket, black shoes; (3) visitors, trainees, contractors under induction — blue helmet, green jacket; (4) safety / HSE people and first aiders — green helmet, green jacket; (5) fire and emergency team — red helmet, green jacket, brown shoes. Helmets to IS 2925 or EN 397; workers carrying bags on the shoulder must wear bump caps to EN 812; jackets to IS 15809 or EN ISO 20471; shoes to IS 15298 (Part 2) or EN ISO 20345. Employers — stevedores and agents included — must provide, inspect and replace the PPE. Transition till 31.07.2026; in force from 01.08.2026: no entry into the port without the prescribed PPE.
circulars.eff: No effect on berthing. Applies to every person a stevedore or agent sends into the port: supervisors in white helmet + green jacket, workers and tally clerks in yellow helmet + orange jacket; bag gangs need bump caps.

circulars.t: Trade notice — Standard Operating Procedure for prevention, detection and control of alcohol influence within port limits
circulars.s: No person under the influence of alcohol may enter, remain or work within port limits. CISF, security and authorised officers may do random and surprise breath-analyser tests at the gates and in operational areas. A person found under the influence faces action under the SOP, including suspension or cancellation of the RFID / port entry pass and removal from operations. Transporters, stevedores, shipping agents, contractors, labour contractors and terminal operators must ensure that no driver, worker, supervisor, operator or employee of theirs enters or works under the influence, must circulate the notice and SOP to their people and display awareness posters. In force at once. (The SOP itself is named as an enclosure; it is not in this copy.)
circulars.eff: No effect on berthing. A duty on the stevedore and agent as employer; entry passes can be cancelled.

circulars.t: Berthing policy modification — vacant Govt / Coastal places, timber log norms, vacant Bitumen place
circulars.s: In partial modification of the berthing policy and its corrigendum: (i) with no suitable vessel under Government priority or Coastal priority, berth allotment proceeds sequentially by the prescribed order of priority, up to and including Sr. No. 3(B) — 3(A) is Higher Productivity, 3(B) is SAAGAR. (ii) Productivity norms: timber logs — pine logs (Sr. 12, break bulk, Appendix-02A) a uniform base norm of 4,000 MTPD whatever the parcel size and bulk density; timber logs — hardwood (Sr. 13) a base norm of 5,500 MTPD. (iii) Bitumen priority (Sr. No. 5): with no suitable bitumen vessel, the berth is operated under the 6,500 MTPD priority, Sr. No. 3(E), instead of the General group — subject to eligibility, readiness and seniority. All else in the policy of 24.03.2025, the circular of 21.05.2026 and the corrigendum of 09.07.2026 stays. In force from the berthing meeting of 23.11.2026 at 11:00, until further orders. The reference number is handwritten; read as 5237.
circulars.eff: ON THE BOARD from v217: (ii) logs counted at 4,600 a day for pine (base 4,000 + 15 %, as the list prints for a berthed vessel) and at the circular's 5,500 for hardwood; (iii) from 23 Nov 18:00 a vacant Bitumen place goes to the senior 6.5K vessel, not to General. Hardwood is counted at 5,500 (v219). (i) AS THE PORT APPLIES IT (programme 27.11, the meeting of 26 Nov): a vacant Govt place went to Hai Nam 81 — first of the HP column, on a 30K quote, printed "GOV(30K)" — ahead of the SAAGAR line. On the board from v278: a Coastal vessel, then the 30K / 25K quote vessels of the HP column, then SAAGAR. (From v272 to v277 the board had read the HP step as an HP bid only, and so put SAAGAR before the quote.) (iii) CORRECTED by the corrigendum of 26.11.2026 (…/3152): the 6,500 line takes the Bitumen berth for break bulk cargo only. That corrigendum cites this circular as 5737.

circulars.t: Trade circular — constitution, jurisdiction, powers and functions of the Adjudicatory Board for Major Ports (Major Port Authorities Act, 2021)
circulars.s: The Central Government has constituted the Adjudicatory Board for Major Ports under Chapter VI of the Act (sections 54 to 60; Major Ports Adjudicatory Board Rules, 2023 — G.S.R. 30(E) dt 17.01.2023; gazette notification S.O. 3740(E) dt 13.08.2025 names the Presiding Officer and two members). It takes the work of the former tariff authority other than tariff setting, disputes between port authorities and PPP concessionaires or captive users, stressed PPP projects, and complaints by port users against the services and terms of service of a port authority or a private operator. It has certain powers of a civil court. The annexure (gazette notification, 11 pages) and the Rules of 2023 (43 pages) came with it and are not attached here.

circulars.ref: DGMA Order No. 31 of 2026 · F. No. 16-17011/5/2022-SD-DGS
circulars.t: Age norms for registration under the Indian flag, compliance for vessels under the Indian flag, and age and compliance for foreign-flag vessels needing a licence under the Coastal Shipping Act 2025
circulars.s: Directorate General of Maritime Administration, Mumbai. In force from 18 Nov 2026; replaces DGS Order 06 of 2023 and DGS Order 1 of 2026. Annexure I sets, by type of ship, the age up to which a vessel may enter the Indian flag freely, the age band where a rating is needed, and the age above which only the Director General can relax (para 12, on a technical committee's advice). Bulk carriers / general cargo: free below 15 years; 15 to 20 years needs grade C or better under Annexure II, or a RightShip safety score of 3 or more; above 20 years by relaxation only. Oil tankers: free below 15; 15 to 20 needs CAP 1 hull / CAP 2 machinery. Container and cement carriers, gas / chemical carriers: free below 20; 20 to 25 with rating. Harbour tugs, long-tow tugs and ocean-going cargo barges: free up to 20. Existing Indian-flag vessels continue whatever their age, with the same ratings by the next survey. A foreign-flag vessel needing a coastal licence — or exempted from it — must meet the same entry-age conditions on the day she starts the voyage or cargo. Not covered: passenger vessels, dredgers, heavy-lift and similar special vessels. Annexure II is the inspection form and scoring (A 95 % +, B 85 %, C 60 %, D below).
circulars.eff: No change to berthing or to this board. It matters when cargo moves coastwise (Indian port to Indian port) on a foreign-flag vessel, or when a vessel, tug or barge is bought for the Indian flag: check her age against Annexure I before fixing her.

circulars.t: Trade notice — handling of coal / coke / iron ore fines / iron ore pellets at Berth CJ-16

Initially the three newly developed plots — Plot Nos. 3, 4 and 11 in the back-up area of CJ-16 — are designated for stacking these cargoes. In force from the proceedings of the berthing meeting of 15.11.2026 (11:00) until further orders; all other terms, conditions and productivity norms of the policy are unchanged.
circulars.eff: Makes official what the port had been doing since 13 Nov — the board has treated CJ-16 as open to coal and dirty bulk since then, so the projection does not change. CJ-16 is no longer a clean-only berth: coal and iron-ore vessels can be allotted it, and salt, project and windmill vessels now share it with them; CJ-13, 14, 15 and 15A are not mentioned and stay clean. Mihir, 16 Nov 18:10: the circular is final — pellets too now go only to CJ-16 (the relaxation of 11 Nov, pellets at all of CJ-13–16, is over), and salt is still loaded at CJ-16 after coal has been worked there.

circulars.t: Operation of Cargo Berths 09 & 10 through M/s Gautam Freight Pvt Ltd — procedure for vessel and cargo handling
circulars.s: GFPL operates CJ-9 & 10 (panel 69 to the end of CJ-10) for five years with its own HMCs. Vessels need GFPL's written consent before DPA considers berthing; berthing, shifting and sailing stay under DPA control; priority berth-hire is not charged merely because GFPL nominated the vessel. Cl. 9: where the berth lies idle for more than 24 hours, DPA may use it for other vessels; on GFPL's advance intimation of its own arrival the berth is vacated in the next tide. Effective 11.09.2026 for CJ-9, CJ-10 on handover.
circulars.eff: Explains KSL Ruiyang at CJ-9 after Cervia (programme for 04.11): an idle operator berth can take a DPA-queue vessel for a short stay. The board keeps CJ-9/10 outside the projection pool and shows such berthings as programme data.

circulars.t: Corrigendum — 24-Hour Priority Category
circulars.s: Any vessel needing berth occupancy for cargo operations of at most 24 hours is eligible, irrespective of parcel size. It must vacate in the same tide on the day after berthing; total stay not to exceed 24 hours or the last available sailing pilot in that tide. Allotment within the category by seniority.
circulars.eff: Modelled: 24-hr slot stay ~22 h + sailing on the next tide; seniority within the group. A vessel that cannot finish in a tide loses the category.

circulars.t: SAAGAR revised terms & conditions — clause 06 (berthing priority) cancelled
circulars.s: Clause 6 of the 19.08.2025 terms (inter-se seniority of importer / exporter vessels over CHA / stevedore vessels within dry bulk and break bulk) stands cancelled; SAAGAR vessels are scheduled to berth as per the berthing policy of 24.03.2025 and the amendment of 11.08.2025.
circulars.eff: SAAGAR order on the board is by reporting seniority only — no importer-over-CHA tie-break.

circulars.t: Revised terms & conditions for cargo commitment holders under the SAAGAR scheme
circulars.s: Minimum commitment the highest of 0.75 MMT / last three years' average / previous tenure; bank guarantee at coal & coke wharfage; yard space up to 40% of the commitment; tenure April–February with March as grace; wharfage discount 5–20% on volume above commitment (telescopic); shortfall penalty at coal & coke wharfage (80% for 10–20%, full above 20%); vessels declared under the scheme must meet the policy productivity norms. Clause 6 (berthing priority, importer-over-CHA inter-se seniority) was cancelled on 17.12.2025.
circulars.eff: Defines who is a SAAGAR vessel (Sr No 7 remark); the priority itself comes from the berthing policy.

circulars.t: Berthing policy amendment (1st amendment)
circulars.s: First amendment to the comprehensive berthing policy of 24.03.2025 (170 MMT target circular).
circulars.eff: Modelled in the berthing rules.

circulars.t: Levy of 200% berth hire at Cargo Jetty 02, 03 and 10 only if DPA ELL shore cranes are used
circulars.s: Circular 569 dt 24.07.2024 continued till 31.03.2026 or SOR revision, whichever earlier.
circulars.eff: Extended to 31.03.2027 by circular 2230 dt 18.06.2026.

circulars.t: Booking priority of port-owned HMC cranes — 60 T Italgru (old) HMCs optional
circulars.s: Booking of the 60 T Italgru (old) HMCs is optional for cargo handling; clause (ii) of circular TF/SH/MHC/2011-12/2424 dt 31.05.2018 (priority booking of 120 T and 60 T HMCs) in abeyance until further notice.
circulars.eff: Crane booking — no change to berthing order. Agents are not forced to book the old 60 T cranes.

circulars.t: Comprehensive berthing policy 2025 — order of allotment for dry cargo and liquid cargo
circulars.s: The policy in force: order of allotment (Govt, Coastal, Higher Productivity, SAAGAR, 24-hr, 8k / 6.5k, Steel / Project, Bitumen, General), group sizes, readiness and reporting rules, productivity norms, penal berth hire, port-convenience shifting, liquid cargo appendix. Amended 11.08.2025, 21.05.2026, 09.07.2026 (two corrigenda), 21.07.2026 and 06.08.2026.
circulars.eff: The rulebook the board's projection is built on.

circulars.t: SAAGAR scheme — clarification: cargo counts towards the commitment even when the vessel berths as General
circulars.s: In continuation of TF/SH/SAGAR/Cargo Promotion/2024/127 dt 13.03.2024 and /408 dt 10.06.2024: the cargo volume of a vessel declared under SAAGAR remains eligible for credit to the commitment even if the vessel is berthed under the General category.
circulars.eff: A SAAGAR vessel taking a General or cross-fill berth (as the board projects for African Quail) loses nothing on its commitment.

circulars.t: Comprehensive berthing policy 2024 (Hindi circular) — effective from the 15.07.2024 meeting
circulars.s: The previous policy: vessels reported before the tide after 18:00 and ready by 11:00 are considered at that day's meeting; allotment per Appendix 01-A (dry) and 01-B (liquid); a higher category vessel is considered before a lower one for a free berth. Superseded by the 24.03.2025 policy.
circulars.eff: Historical — the meeting-gating and order-of-allotment principles carried into the 2025 policy.

circulars.t: Amendment to the berthing policy — non-commencement shifting, oil-jetty allotment (App. 01B) and liquid norms (App. 02B)
circulars.s: A vessel not commencing within 4 hours of all-fast is shifted to OTB in the next tide at the agent's cost (or stays on 3× penal berth hire). Oil-jetty allotment: OJ-1 LPG (by inter-se seniority of LPG ships, priority berth hire); OJ-1 to OJ-4 all compatible cargo by seniority (max two edible-oil tankers at OJ-1–4); OJ-5 IFFCO; OJ-6 IOCL / BPCL; OJ-7 edible / vegetable oil (senior-most edible tanker). Norms (MTPH): edible oil 275–650 and chemicals 225–550 by parcel size, palm fatty acid / stearin 225, export cargo 250, molasses 275, LPG butane 380 / propane 500 / both 775.
circulars.eff: Still the visible pattern on the Liquid tab (LPG at OJ-1, IFFCO at OJ-5, POL at OJ-6, CDSBO at OJ-7); the edible / chemical slabs were widened 5% on 09.07.2026. The 2025 policy carries the current liquid appendix.

circulars.t: DPA Kandla — fertiliser handling hub (infrastructure capacity presentation)
circulars.s: Fertiliser and raw-material volumes FY 2025-26 by commodity (DAP 13.2 lakh MT, MOP 13.0 lakh MT, NPK 4.0 lakh MT …), 9 HMCs (Liebherr, Italgru), covered storage ~3.7 lakh MT inside the port plus 4 lakh MT outside, rail evacuation up to 4 rakes a day, Tuna terminal 0.5–0.75 lakh MT extra capacity.
circulars.eff: Background for the Govt-priority fertiliser traffic at CJ-7 / CJ-8.

circulars.t: Layout plan of Kandla Port — cargo berths, oil jetties, Bunder area, plots
circulars.s: Port layout drawing with berth details, draught table, covered storage, railway tracks and plot allotments.
circulars.eff: Base for the quay geometry together with the Civil Engg "Cargo Berth Details" sheet (berth lengths, live load, HM panel marks).
